Results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6).

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (three studies, total n=59 controls) performing social-related tasks (person knowledge, famous names, socially relevant concept words) contrasted against non-social semantic conditions and active baselines. Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses (one-way ANOVAs and contrasts such as social > non-social) are reported, with peak coordinates and whole-brain results described and shown. Results for the healthy/control group are presented separately and clearly. Reporting of voxelwise task-evoked maps and coordinate tables/figures satisfies whole-brain evidence requirements. Therefore all inclusion criteria for empirical task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain group results are met.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-related approach-avoidance (AA) task comparing social versus nonsocial stimuli (meets social-processing requirement). Participants were healthy adults (male, mean age 21.35) with results reported separately for treatment groups of healthy subjects. The manuscript reports group-level task analyses and explicitly states exploratory whole-brain results were performed and reported (in main text/supplement), and contrasts are clearly identified at the group level. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI social task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, mean age 23.8), using an impression-formation task involving social perception of faces varying in race and socioeconomic status — a social-related construct (perception and understanding of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task analyses (GLM contrast images used for PLS; voxelwise whole-brain results with cluster reporting and coordinates identified via xjview) and presents whole-brain PLS results and clusters. Results for the healthy adult sample are reported directly and are not restricted to a narrow subgroup. Thus the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for task fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain task-evoked maps. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6.

The study reports task-based fMRI of joint dyadic interaction (leading/following), which probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others, social coordination). The sample is healthy adults (n=18, ages ~40) meeting the age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts, conjunctions) with Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholds described, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Results are presented for the healthy participant group (whole-group and subgroup analyses). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is an empirical fMRI study).

The study uses fMRI during a social perception task (trustworthiness/fear appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group (ages 18–45). However, the paper does not clearly report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map that is explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain results appear to be across all participants or between-group contrasts, and control-group results are reported mainly via ROI analyses and statistics rather than an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (real-time mutual eye contact) in healthy adults (mean age ~21.8). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (LIVE > REPLAY) with corrected inference and provides tables/figures of activated clusters and interbrain synchronization. Results for the healthy participant group are reported separately and satisfy whole-brain reporting requirements.

This study reports task-based fMRI using a social-emotional Face Processing Task (fearful vs neutral faces), recruiting healthy adult participants (N=49, ages 18–33). The paper presents group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain analyses (TFCE, FWE-corrected, 5,000 permutations) for contrasts (Fearful > Neutral and Neutral > Fearful) and reports coordinates and figures for these results. Questionnaire-regressed and seed-based FC results are supplemented by whole-brain exploratory analyses and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion requirements for an fMRI social task in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps (also described in text and figures).

This is an fMRI study using a social task (modified cyberball) probing social exclusion — a social-related process. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (female, mean age ~21.7, final N=71 across groups) within the 18–65 range. The authors report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (initial whole-brain threshold p<0.001 uncorrected with clusters surviving FWE small-volume correction), provide peak MNI coordinates and statistical maps/figures, and describe contrasts and within-group effects. Results are clearly from healthy participants and reported as whole-brain task-evoked activations (coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply.

This study used task-based fMRI to measure neural responses to dynamic social interactions (dyads) in healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–35). Group-level whole-brain analyses are described: whole-brain beta maps were generated, whole-brain contrasts were used for localizer ROI definition (interaction > scrambled interaction, bodies > objects, faces > objects, mentalizing > pain), and a whole-brain searchlight analysis was performed and reported. Results include group-level statistical outcomes and descriptions of whole-brain searchlight peaks. Thus the paper meets the requirements for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (reported in main text and supplementary materials).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=31 analyzed) investigating social perception of others (neural and behavioural responses to facial disfigurement; relevant to perception/understanding of others and stigma). The fMRI analysis includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (SnPM nonparametric group analysis with familywise error correction and cluster-level reporting) comparing pre- vs post-surgery faces, with results presented as whole-brain activation/deactivation clusters. Participant ages (18–35) fall within the 18–65 range. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults are met.

This study used task-based fMRI during a social-economic paradigm (prisoners' dilemma) addressing social behaviour (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (15 controls, ages 18–50) with results reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses and explicitly describes significant activations for the control group (one-sample t-tests per group and visualizations/tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group maps (I5). Whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, reports within-group healthy results (not only between-group contrasts), includes adults within 18–65, and is empirical fMRI data. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Although this fMRI study involves a social task (dynamic facial expression processing) and includes a healthy adult control group, the full text does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly attributable to the healthy/TD group alone. The paper reports ROI-based results and whole-brain analyses focused on group differences, and emphasizes between-group contrasts and DCM (effective connectivity) findings. There is no clear presentation of a whole-brain within-healthy-group task effect (e.g., TD: expressions > mosaics) in the reported results or figures/tables described in the text. Therefore the study effectively reports only between-group contrasts and connectivity/ROI analyses without the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map, meeting exclusion criterion E4.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of action observation and weight-discrimination (perception of others’ hand actions), which falls squarely under social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). Healthy adult participants were tested across Experiments 1–4 (total N≈79 healthy subjects) and group-level activation contrasts (e.g., ActionOBS–CtrlOBS; Sleeve/NoSleeve contrasts) are presented. Analyses include voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (reported and visualized across the whole brain and specifically the cerebellum; some contrasts are presented at whole-brain level, e.g., NoSleeve–Sleeve FG4 result). Results for the healthy/control groups are reported separately from patient data. Therefore the study meets the fMRI social-task requirement, includes healthy adults, and provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (reported in figures/text/tables), satisfying I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates social cognition using an ecological language-based social task (listening to movie excerpts and inferring characters' mental states), meeting the review objective. It reports a healthy control group (n=28; ages 18–65) analyzed separately from the patient group. The paper provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy controls (one-sample t-test, INT>HIN; maps thresholded at p<0.05 FWE) with coordinates and figures. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the paper does not provide an unmasked, within-group whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports group contrasts/whole-sample effects but no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task map). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during social-related tasks: SID, EFP, FER) and I4 (includes a healthy control group of adults aged 50–60, reported separately). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported specifically for the healthy/control group). The paper reports ROI analyses, whole-group (combined sample) maps, and between-group contrasts, and supplies whole-brain tables for group comparisons, but does not present an unmasked, within-control-group whole-brain activation map required by the review. Full text appears complete.

This article is a non-empirical review (Review article) and does not report original fMRI data in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not present an fMRI study during a social-related task), I4 (no reported healthy adult participant group with data), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (no whole-brain results described). Additionally, only abstract/metadata are available here (no full methods/results), so fulltext_incomplete=true per screening guidance.

This study reports an fMRI task probing social processing (observation of dynamic facial expressions—Social Communication/Perception of Others), with a healthy adult sample (n=51; mean age 22.5 within 18–65), and provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (one-sample t tests and ANOVAs) with FWE-corrected thresholds and reported activation tables/figures. Whole-brain results are clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This paper appears to be a review/synthesis of multiple fMRI studies rather than an original empirical report presenting new, unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation maps for a healthy adult group. Exclusion met: E6 (non-empirical/review without original fMRI data in healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (discusses fMRI during social-related tasks) and I4 (describes healthy adult participants/groups in cited studies). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the article itself does not present an original, clearly identified group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy/control group as primary data) — although it reproduces/adapts figures from prior empirical papers, those are not new original whole-brain results within this article. Therefore the article should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (imitation/urge to imitate) in healthy adult participants. The sample comprises 37 healthy right-handed adults aged 18–25, satisfying the adult age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses with cluster-level correction (P<0.001, corrected to P<0.05) and presents coordinates/tables/figures of activations (e.g., SMA, MCC) and PPI results. Whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age range appropriate, and empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (eye gaze, self-propelling motion, implicit mental inference) in healthy adult participants (aged 19–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and second-level analyses (e.g., [E–O]+[S–X], PCA-based regression, cluster-corrected thresholds) with coordinates and figures/tables. All core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text, and healthy-group results are reported separately. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (imagining Self, Loved-one, Stranger in pain), addressing affiliation/attachment and perception/understanding of others. Sample: 36 healthy adult participants (mean age 23), right-handed, within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, voxel-level P<0.05 FDR corrected, extent thresholds) with tables/figures of coordinates and statistical maps described in the text and supplementary tables. Results are reported for the healthy participant group (not limited to a subgroup). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not purely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary tables referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (25 right-handed British women, mean age 23.5) that uses task-based functional MRI during social-related judgments (beauty/attractiveness comparisons), meeting the review’s focus on perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and conjunctions (thresholds and coordinates provided) and also presents tables/figures of whole-brain results; these satisfy whole-brain evidence requirements. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion provided.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 19–31) that measured task-evoked BOLD responses during multiple social-related tasks (theory of mind, face perception, biological motion, voice perception) and an auditory language task. The paper reports voxelwise GLM analyses and group-level mixed-effects activation maps (used to define search spaces and peak coordinates), and provides whole-study methods, results, and figures with group activation coordinates and overlap analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related tasks in healthy adults and reports group-level voxelwise task activations. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is incomplete: the provided 'Full Text Content' is a website privacy/cookie notice and does not contain the article's introduction, methods, results, or discussion. Although the metadata (title/authors/journal) suggests an fMRI study of self-knowledge (a social-related construct), there is no information to confirm any inclusion criteria. Cannot verify I3 (task-based fMRI on social-related processing), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), or I6 (whole-brain results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the supplied content. Recommend obtaining the complete article PDF/text to determine eligibility.

This is an fMRI study using the Animated Triangles Task, a social/mentalizing paradigm (meets I3). The paper includes a healthy adult control group (N=17) with results reported separately (meets I4). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task activation for the control group (e.g., intentional>random activated temporal gyrus, occipital cortex, inferior frontal cortex, pSTS) and presents cluster-corrected whole-brain maps/analyses (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are provided. Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and figures. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related decision-making in healthy adults. The neuroimaging cohort comprises healthy participants aged 18–53 and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level GLM analyses (random-effects), voxelwise results thresholded and corrected (p<.001, extent), and provides statistical maps via NeuroVault and supplementary tables. The task manipulates social information and examines social influence on decisions, meeting the social-processing construct. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-task-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed person dyads and performed sex-categorization while BOLD data were acquired. Sample: 12 healthy adult participants (ages 21–31) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses (random-effects), voxelwise and cluster thresholds, and tables/figures listing peak coordinates and clusters (whole-brain results provided). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-emotional processing (schadenfreude and fremdscham) in healthy adult participants (N=34, ages 19–31). Methods include whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SIT vs NEUT contrasts) with FWE-corrected results reported at the group level; parametric and connectivity analyses are supplementary but whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study uses task-based BOLD fMRI with a social-cognitive paradigm (affective Theory of Mind, emotion recognition, face processing), satisfying I3. It includes a separate healthy adult control group (18 male controls) reported separately from the psychopathy group, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level task-evoked activations for the healthy controls (text describes task-associated activation in healthy controls; whole-brain analysis threshold P<0.001 uncorrected and whole-brain results referenced in Supplementary Tables; coordinates and contrasts for healthy controls are reported), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs only, are not connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain activations are provided. Full text appears to contain introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-related task (participant-generated autobiographical social situations and negative self-beliefs) involving perception/understanding of self and social processes. The sample includes 35 healthy adults within the 21–55 age range, and all analyses and results are reported for this healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (tables, figures, and corrected cluster/TFCE analyses) rather than ROI-only or resting-state/ connectivity-only results. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception (a social-relevant task: perception/understanding of others) in a healthy adult sample and reports group-level whole-brain task activation. The methods describe an fMRI faces-versus-houses block design, preprocessing and second-level (group) SPM8 analyses. Results present significant group activations (Table 2, FWE-corrected maps shown in figures) and report suprathreshold voxel counts in bilateral fusiform gyrus (voxelwise whole-brain analysis). The fMRI sample is a healthy adult subset (N=22, mean age ~18.9) within the 18–65 range. Therefore inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult participants), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social-communicative processing (speech act comprehension) in healthy adults. It uses task-based fMRI during a social communication paradigm (Naming vs. Requesting) and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts (e.g., Request > Naming) with FDR-corrected results and coordinate tables/ROI SVC results. Sample consists of healthy adults (n=18 analyzed; age range 18–41). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social-cognitive content (agency vs. communion) using a valence-classification task. Methods report SPM8 whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts), cluster correction (AlphaSim), and report group-level activation/deactivation maps and tables. Sample: 42 healthy adult (18–25 years) participants, right-handed undergraduates, with exclusions and group-level results clearly described. The task and contrasts constitute task-evoked whole-brain maps from the healthy group (agency vs. fixation, communion vs. fixation, conjunction, and direct comparisons), satisfying the review’s requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communicative speech in healthy adults (n=29, ages 18–24). The task is explicitly social (communication vs description), and the paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2) with contrasts, statistical thresholds, activation maps/figures, and tables of activated coordinates. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so full text is complete.

The study uses fMRI during a clearly social-related task (Socio-emotional Preferential Task; “Do you like this face?”) assessing social appraisal, satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) reported separately alongside patients, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected peaks, cluster coordinates, and contrasts including HC>SZ and task effects; figures and Supplementary Table S1 report whole-brain maps/peaks), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is sufficiently complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, age out-of-range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the article meets all inclusion requirements for this review.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of online imitative social interaction in healthy adult participants (N=23, females, ages 18–30). It addresses social cognition (imitation, role switching, intention attribution) matching the review objective. The paper provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation results (GLM contrasts imitating, being imitated, observation vs rest) with correction for multiple comparisons (FWE p<0.05) and tables/figures of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Although the study also reports PPI connectivity analyses, whole-brain activation maps for the healthy adult group are clearly presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social task—the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–22). However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy/control group. Analyses are restricted to ROI-based univariate statistics and task-based gPPI connectivity with small-volume corrections; the paper emphasizes ROI and seed-to-target connectivity results and between-group (OT vs PL) contrasts but no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task maps are provided. Therefore it violates E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results), E3 (reports seed-based/gPPI connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map), and E4 (focuses on between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Excluding on grounds of missing required whole-brain task-evoked maps per I5.

This is an fMRI study that uses a social-related task (faces as targets) embedded in an oddball target-detection paradigm, reported in healthy adult participants (N=19; ages 19.3–47.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (shape targets vs novels; face targets vs novels; direct comparisons) using mixed-effects FSL analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and provides MNI coordinates (Table 2) and figures of activation maps. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes retaliatory behavior—clearly social-related processing. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 22.3), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise statistical maps, Talairach coordinates, cluster-corrected thresholds, and illustrative figures and tables of coordinates (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from the healthy group). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interaction task (Cyberball/virtual ball-toss) with healthy adult participants (analyzed N=31, ages ≈21). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (e.g., ball-toss [high-frequency – normal-frequency] > button-press [high-frequency – normal-frequency]) with voxelwise results, cluster-level FWE correction, coordinates, tables, and figures. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the submitted full text. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social hierarchy tasks) in healthy adult participants. The sample comprises 72 healthy adults (ages reported within 19–43 and 19–38 ranges for experiments), meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and thresholding (e.g., p<0.005 FDR-corrected; coordinates and Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–5), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social task (virtual characters, gaze and social vs arbitrary facial expressions) that directly probes social-related processing. Sample: 18 healthy right-handed adults (age ~26) reported separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted using SPM2 with random-effects inference and reported contrasts (e.g., SOC>ARB, ME>OTHER) with stereotactic coordinates and tables/figures. Results include whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and figures/tables, so core article content is present and sufficient for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a social-related task (viewing traffic-campaign videos designed to elicit socio-cognitive processes such as mentalizing and empathy). The sample consists of healthy adults (male drivers, ages 19–30), satisfying the age/sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (campaign videos vs neutral videos) presented for each group (see Fig. 1 and associated text) and ROI analyses; whole-brain results for the healthy groups are clearly described. Reporting includes figures/tables of voxelwise effects (and text description), meeting acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-group whole-brain maps, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This study uses task-based fMRI of self–other processing (a social-cognition/‘perception and understanding of self/others’ task) meeting I3. It reports a healthy typically-developing (TD) control group with results presented separately from the ASD group, and the control group mean age (post-exclusion) is within the adult range, meeting I4. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level task activation results for the healthy/control group (within-group contrasts and tables/figures), meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 — the study reports only resting-state fMRI connectivity/graph-theory analyses and does not provide any task-evoked, whole-brain healthy-group activation maps. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — the paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=12) reported separately. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — the study did not use fMRI during any social-related task (it used a resting-state protocol); I5 — no whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map for a healthy/control group is reported. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because the review objective requires task-based whole-brain activations in healthy adults, and this paper provides only resting-state analyses and behavioral task scores (outside the scanner), it must be excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (social working memory/perspective-taking), fulfilling the social-related task requirement. The sample includes 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 21.6), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and parametric modulation analyses (conjunction and SWM vs CWM contrasts) with cluster thresholds and tables of regions/coordinates, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are clearly described for the healthy group. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only metadata/abstract-like content provided). Cannot verify whether the study reports task-based whole-brain fMRI results for a healthy adult group. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met (cannot be confirmed from provided content): I3 (uncertain whether a social-related fMRI task with whole-brain healthy-group results is reported), I4 (uncertain whether a healthy adult control group 18–65 is included and reported separately), I5 (no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from a healthy group), I6 (cannot confirm whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot apply inclusion criteria; study cannot be included at this time. Recommend obtaining full article (methods/results) for re-screening.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making (modified iterated prisoner's dilemma) in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 23–38). The task probes perception/understanding of others and social learning, satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., COMP>COOP, conjunction vs. control) with second-level random-effects analyses and cluster-level correction; results are presented in text, figures, and tables, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: Why/How social inference task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, healthy-group task activation map (e.g., within-group main effect or within-group whole-brain contrast for the control group). The whole-brain results focus on Group × Stimulus interactions and post hoc between-group simple effects rather than an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task map. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (N=20, ages 21–47) using a social-related task (explicit mental simulation of other persons’ actions and feelings), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses: ISPS maps, seed-voxel correlation maps, and task-evoked BOLD GLM SPM-t maps thresholded and FDR-corrected, fulfilling I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and is included.

This full-text report describes an empirical fMRI study that includes multiple social-related tasks (false belief, intentional triangles, trustworthiness, eyes intention, vocalization) meeting the review’s definition of social processing (I3). The sample comprises 78 healthy adults (age range 18–40), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and thresholded statistical maps (voxelwise p<0.05 FWE), provides peak coordinates and supplementary maps, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the target age range. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Supplementary info).

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study that used a social perception task contrasting affiliation, isolation, and nonsocial images (I3). The sample includes a healthy younger adult group (mean age ~20.8), meeting the 18–65 requirement and reported separately from the older group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses and thresholding, with tables/coordinates and voxelwise contrasts for within-group and between-group effects (e.g., social vs nonsocial; Affiliation vs Isolation), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (I5, I6). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results (including tables/figures), and discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age out of range only, non-empirical) are met.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the social-task requirement (I3). The fMRI paradigm is a motion-perception task (moving vs. stationary concentric rings) aimed at visual/motion processing and not a social-related task (e.g., affiliation, social communication, self/other perception). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult control groups are reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) — NOT met. I5 (reporting a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map): the paper reports whole-brain ANOVA-derived ROIs and group beta values but does not clearly present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map specifically identified as coming from the healthy/control group for a social task; regardless, failure to meet I3 is sufficient for exclusion. Exclusion criteria met: none of E2–E6 appear to apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion) with healthy adult participants (Chinese university students). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (exclusion vs inclusion) across participants with FWE-corrected results and tables of activations/coordinates, and also presents ROI/PPI analyses. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables provided). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study uses task-based fMRI with a social-related face encoding paradigm (meets I3) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and coordinates for the control (typically-developing) group (meets I5 and I6). However, the control group is not clearly an adult-only sample (mean age ≈18.7 with participants under 18; study procedures explicitly include minors and adolescent consent), and the paper does not report results for a healthy adult (18–65) subgroup separately. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 reported separately). No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI (task-based) hyperscanning study of social interaction (cooperation/competition) meeting the review topic. Sample: 44 healthy adults (mean age 22.37, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results (FLAME) with non-parametric permutation correction and threshold-free cluster enhancement, and lists clusters in Tables 1–3 and shows whole-brain t-maps (figures). Whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy participant group. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3: uses fMRI during a social-related task (trustworthiness judgments of faces). I4: includes a healthy adult control group (n=18, mean age 32.2, within 18–65) reported separately. I5: reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group task-evoked analyses for the control group (whole-brain contrasts; Tables 1 and 2; detailed thresholding described). I6: whole-brain results are described in the text and tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of voice-identity processing, a form of social communication/perception relevant to social cognition. It includes healthy adult control groups (two matched control groups, mean age ~31, n=16 each) and reports within-group/group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts (e.g., vocal>non-vocal; speaker>speech) for control participants, with tables of coordinates and SPM results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study that explicitly probes social-related processing (social vs. non-social/solitary contexts and self- vs. other-generation) during encoding and recognition of episodic memories. The sample is healthy adults (n=24; age range 18–28). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 random-effects, contrasts, cluster-level correction) and present tables/figures of activations and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Taken together, the manuscript satisfies the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain task activation maps.

The paper reports an fMRI deception task that probes social behavior (deception/manipulation/theory-of-mind–relevant processes), using a healthy adult sample (24 males, ages 19–60). The analysis is a random-effects, voxelwise SPM group analysis reporting whole-brain task contrasts (lie > truth and truth > lie) with thresholding and tables/figures of activations; correlations with psychopathy trait scores are reported at the voxel level. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (Theory of Mind) using an established social visual paradigm (moving triangles) and task-based BOLD acquisition. The sample includes healthy adults with mean age 45.6 and range 24–64 (within 18–65), satisfying participant criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (ToM > R, ToM > Baseline, R > Baseline) with thresholding, coordinates, figures, and tables; Bayesian and correlation analyses are also reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This fMRI study examines vocal emotional processing (social communication/perception) in healthy adults (N=36, age 20–35), so I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) are satisfied. However, the paper does not report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures of voxelwise activations for the healthy group. Analyses are ROI/parcellation-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical metrics (Power-264 ROIs) and report ROI-level/nodal/global network measures and interregional FC, not unmasked whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore it fails I5 (whole-brain voxelwise task map). This meets exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI/connectivity analyses with no whole-brain results) and E3 (reports connectivity/network analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Consequently the study should be excluded.

Full text is complete. The study is excluded because it does not meet the sample inclusion criterion (I4): the healthy control group reported is mixed-age with an age range of 12–23 years and is not an adult-only (18–65) healthy group, nor are healthy adult-only results reported separately. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task using emotional faces), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task activation maps are reported for the control group), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none (no ROI-only analyses, no connectivity-only or resting-state-only analyses, control group results are reported, and participants are not exclusively outside 18–65). Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study is an fMRI experiment of affective (social) touch in healthy adults (N=22, ages 19–35). It uses a social-related task (affective/affiliation-related touch; satisfies I3), includes a healthy adult sample within 18–65 (I4), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (arm>baseline, palm>baseline, arm>palm) with thresholds and cluster correction (I5). Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no only connectivity-only, not outside age range, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self, friend, celebrity trait judgments) directly addressing perception/understanding of self and others. Participants were healthy adults (N=37 males; mean age 22.9), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) and whole-brain regression analyses with FDR correction, with peak coordinates and cluster sizes provided. Results include task-evoked activations and gPPI connectivity analyses, and reporting is sufficient in tables/figures/text. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (approachability judgments from faces) that includes a healthy adult control group and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the control group. The Methods and Results present random-effects whole-brain analyses for the approachability>gender contrast with peak coordinates, cluster-corrected p-values, and figures/tables for control participants. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps for controls), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses an fMRI social/attachment task (baby-cry) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3, I4). However, reported results are restricted to a priori ROI analyses (SVC within extended amygdala, NAc, dmPFC) and group-difference contrasts/gPPI connectivity. No unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map is reported or provided for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and meets exclusion criteria for ROI-only reporting and lack of an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effect (E2, E4).

This is an fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing using the Dynamic Social Gestures (DSG) task (social vs nonsocial gestures) and reports group-level task-evoked whole-brain analyses. The sample comprises 20 healthy young adults (mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7) described as a healthy adult group; analyses and results are reported for this healthy group. Group-level whole-brain results are reported (cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates; Table 1 and figures), satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening. Note: one participant’s age is reported as 16.9 (<18), but the cohort is otherwise an adult healthy sample and results are presented for the healthy group as a whole, so I4 is considered met with moderate-high confidence.

This is an fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts. The task manipulated perceived live versus recorded speech (a social-interactive manipulation) and analyzed BOLD responses during the story period; whole-brain Live>Social and Social>Standard contrasts are reported (cluster-corrected) and mentalizing-network ROI and whole-brain results are described. Sample comprises healthy adults (final N=29, ages 18–27). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The article reports an fMRI study of prosocial learning (social-related processing) using task-based fMRI with clear whole-brain group-level analyses. Sample: 31 healthy adult males (age 19–32), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain statistical results and contrasts (flexible factorial SPM analyses, main effects, conjunction and contrasts, Tables S1–S4, and FWE-corrected peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental tables/figures are referenced. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This study reports an fMRI experiment explicitly probing social interaction perception (gaze modulation of social vs individual actions), meeting the review objective. Participants: 17 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 26), meeting the sample criterion. Analysis: whole-brain, second-level random-effects analyses with reported main effects and interaction maps and coordinate tables (p<.001 uncorrected), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain task-evoked results. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

Full text is complete. The study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-cognitive task: affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group with ages within 18–65 and reports control-group data). However, the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (I5 not met). The reported whole-brain results are either main effects across participants and group-by-condition interactions or post hoc eigenvariate tests; no clearly described healthy-group whole-brain task map is presented in the main text (supplementary materials are referenced but do not clearly provide a healthy-group whole-brain map). Therefore the study is excluded under E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions or mixed/group-ambiguous maps without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect).

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly investigates social-related processing (implicit social stimuli) alongside self-referential processing. Inclusion criteria met: I3 — uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (pictures depicting humans; sociality factor); I4 — healthy adult sample (n=28; ages 30–50) reported separately; I5 — reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA across healthy subjects) with FDR-corrected maps, coordinates, tables and figures; I6 — whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants investigating social-related processing (recall of self- and other-related relationship episodes). The sample comprises 35 healthy adults (screened for psychiatric disorders). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (self-relevant > control; other > control) with one-sample t-tests, FDR correction, and tables/figures of significant clusters. Results for the healthy group are reported explicitly. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing complete assessment. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are healthy adults, and the paper is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

Full text appears incomplete (abstract only). The study clearly used fMRI to probe social-cognitive processes in healthy/normal subjects, meeting I3. However, the provided text does not report participant ages/sample characteristics required to confirm I4 (healthy adults 18–65). It is also not possible to verify that group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation maps are reported (I5) from the truncated content, despite region-based activations being described in the abstract. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are demonstrably met from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, I exclude the study pending full-text availability.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test), which targets perception/understanding of others; (I4) the sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 26.4, within 18–65); (I5) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy/control group (one-sample t-test within the placebo condition for ToM>gender and paired t-tests and exploratory whole-brain analyses reported in tables/ text); (I6) whole-brain results are presented in tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only analyses, no connectivity- or resting-state-only focus, not an only between-group report, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates empathy/social cognition (social-related processing) using a task with emotional vs. neutral and social relation contrasts, satisfying the review topic. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=17 recruited, N=16 analyzed; mean age 27.8), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (EMOT vs NEUT; TWO vs ONE), used FDR-corrected statistical maps and lists peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying whole-brain reporting (coordinates/figures/tables). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and imaging acquisition/analysis details, so full-text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (attribution of emotions to humans and non-human animals), involving healthy adult participants (N=18; ages 21–46). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected statistical maps and whole-brain contrasts described in text and figures), and also provides ROI and whole-brain results. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adults within 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported; I6: whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI task study of social cognition (ToM and empathy) in a healthy sample of college students, reporting group-level whole-brain task activation maps (SPM analyses with RFT correction and coordinates in supplement) and using these maps in analyses. The sample consists of healthy participants (ages 17–21, mean 19.3); although a few participants are 17, the group includes adults within 18–65 and is reported as a healthy group. The paper provides voxelwise whole-brain task effects for the healthy group. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI task explicitly probing empathy (a social-cognition/Perception and Understanding of Others construct) in healthy adult controls and clinical patients. It includes a healthy control group (age-matched adults), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps for the healthy control group (one-sample t-test activation map and between-group contrasts), with results presented in tables and figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-, mother-, and social attribution tasks) in healthy adult participants (n=17 analyzed; mean age 21.5, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (conjunctions and contrasts) with FDR correction and provides tables of peak coordinates and figures. It is empirical original fMRI data, notROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes unmasked healthy-group task effects. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social-cognitive tasks (affective ToM, emotion recognition, neutral face processing) meeting the review focus. A healthy adult control group (N=13) is reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain activations (group comparisons) and indicates single-group results for each group at whole-brain thresholds (Supplementary Tables S1–S4), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map; coordinate/table reporting in supplements is acceptable. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age, or non-empirical) apply.

The paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory-of-mind) in healthy adult participants. The Methods and Results describe group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level contrasts, thresholded to provide whole-brain corrected maps) and present tables/figures of significant activations (e.g., Table 1, Figures 4A–C). Participant ages and sample sizes for the fMRI experiment (N=17, mean age 22) and behavioural sample (N=39, range 18–60) fall within the 18–65 range. Whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (mentalising > factual; parametric modulation contrasts) are reported for the healthy group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (reappraisal of angry faces), includes a healthy adult sample (N=60, ages 18–57) with results reported for healthy participants, and provides group-level whole-brain task contrasts and coordinates (e.g., Observe-angry vs Decrease, Increase vs Observe-angry) in the main text/tables. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster thresholding are described; results are presented as group-level maps and tables of peaks. Resting-state analyses are also included but do not preclude inclusion. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social-political cognition (political-judgment task) and examines neural correlates of social-related processing. The fMRI sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages 22–45; N=26). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (F- and t-statistics), thresholding, and coordinates/figures of activations (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group). Full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines emotion evaluation from voice and music, an instance of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others’ emotions/mental states). It tested healthy adult participants (N=16; ages 18–26) and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., emotion task vs pitch task, music vs rest, voice vs rest) with cluster-level correction and figures/tables describing results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and whole-brain results are clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (hand-holding/social regulation of threat) in a healthy adult sample (N=22; mean age ~23.6). The task is social/affiliation-related (friend vs stranger vs alone during threat anticipation), satisfying I3. The sample includes healthy adults aged 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses used to define multisubject ROIs (FEAT, cluster-wise tests with Z>2.3 and cluster p<.05) based on threat vs safe contrasts, i.e., a group-level whole-brain task-evoked map clearly from the healthy group, satisfying I5. Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures (ROIs and coordinates), satisfying I6. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports between-group whole-brain contrasts (healthy>manic, manic>healthy) but does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain within-group healthy-control task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task map reported), I6 (not applicable because qualifying whole-brain healthy-group results are absent). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants observed cooperative and affective social interactions during fMRI, satisfying the review topic. Sample: 36 healthy adults (ages within 18–65) reported separately, meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects analyses, cluster-extent FDR correction) with tables/figures and reported coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task activations, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages only, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete for screening purposes.

This peer-reviewed fMRI study includes a healthy adult control group (n=13) and uses an explicit social-related task (self- and other-evaluation of personality traits) during whole-brain task fMRI. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise one-sample (within healthy controls) contrasts (SELF vs baseline, OTHER vs baseline, conjunctions, and coordinates/tables/figures) with whole-brain correction and parameter estimates. All required inclusion criteria are met: social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample reported separately (I4), whole-brain group-level task activation maps for controls (I5), and acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports an fMRI task (Social Detection Task) that explicitly probes social cognition (valence judgments of naturalistic social interactions), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (final N=38, ages 18–30), meeting I4. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (full-factorial ANOVA, whole-brain FWE cluster correction) with tables/figures of activations (Table 1, Figures 2–4), meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of task-evoked whole-brain fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/highlights provided). While the study is an fMRI investigation of interpersonal synchrony and clearly addresses social processing (meets I3), the provided content lacks necessary details to verify participant ages and whether at least one healthy adult group (ages 18–65) was analyzed separately (I4 cannot be confirmed). Crucially, the manuscript text available does not include methods/results/tables to confirm the presence of group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps from the healthy group (I5 not verifiable). Therefore I cannot confirm I4–I6. No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 are clearly met based on available content, but the incomplete full text prevents reliable eligibility determination. Recommend obtaining full article (methods and results) to reassess whole-brain results and sample ages.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N≈120) using two social-cognitive tasks (emotional perspective-taking and emotion attribution) that target social processing/mentalizing. Group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., emotion perspective-taking > shape matching; emotion attribution > gender matching) and whole-brain regression analyses are reported, with FWE- and voxelwise thresholds and peak coordinates/cluster sizes provided. The sample is healthy adults within the 18–65 range. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI of social processing, healthy adult sample, and clearly reported group-level whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text appears incomplete (provided content contains highlights, abstract, keywords, and references but lacks full methods/results/discussion). The abstract indicates an fMRI interactive mentalizing (prisoner’s dilemma) task in healthy adults (n=195; fMRI subgroup n=163), so inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) are met. However, the supplied content does not allow verification of I5: there is no accessible full-text methods/results or explicit whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Although regional activations are mentioned in the abstract, this is insufficient to confirm whole-brain voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are demonstrably met in the provided content. Because I5 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article (fulltext_incomplete=true). Recommend obtaining the full PDF to reassess inclusion.

This study used task-based fMRI with a social-emotional face-processing paradigm (dynamic fearful faces), includes a healthy adult control group (n=19; mean age 31.8 years), and reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) task activation maps and contrasts (e.g., face>place; one-sample and between-group analyses) clearly identified for the healthy control group. The full text includes methods, results, figures, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not restricted to between-group contrasts without an unmasked healthy-group map, and participants fall within the age range).

The article reports an empirical fMRI study using social-related tasks (face-viewing with person-judgment localizer assessing perception/understanding of others and social valuation), satisfying I3. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=26, mean age 28.7), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects parametric analyses (Fig. S1, Table S4) with FWE correction and whole-brain regressions tied to target popularity, satisfying I5; whole-brain results are described in text and supplemental figures/tables, satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only (E2), not limited to connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), age range is within 18–65 (E5), and this is an empirical fMRI study (not a review) (E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (social-comparative judgments of close vs. non-close others), meeting the review objective (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample consists of healthy adults (N=20, mean age 18.7) with exclusions for neurological/psychiatric conditions, meeting the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level contrasts (random-effects SPM analyses) and provides peak coordinates and statistical maps for task contrasts (Target × Breadth, Valence, Close vs. Non-Close), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked group results; results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. Although multiple-comparison correction was performed within a priori ROIs, group-level voxelwise contrasts and coordinate results are reported, and qualifying whole-brain results are presented. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (impression formation/updating), meeting key inclusion criteria: (I3) task involves social perception/understanding of others (faces paired with valenced behaviors); (I4) healthy adult sample (N=24, ages 18–45); (I5/I6) reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task analyses (interaction L2>F3, L2>F3 within inconsistent targets, thresholding procedures, tables/figures, supplementary tables). The manuscript includes complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion), and whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI using a social cognition paradigm (empathic and forgivability judgments) (I3). It includes a healthy adult comparison group (14 subjects, mean age 30.5 years) scanned and analyzed separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise activation results for the healthy/control group and describes their within-group activation maps (e.g., bilateral medial prefrontal cortex, temporal and posterior regions) using SPM99 random-effects analyses (I5). Results are presented in the main text (with supplements) as whole-brain contrasts and figures/tables are referenced (I6). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided in the supplied full text, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy maps, out-of-age-range samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be INCLUDED.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social processing (empathy and forgiveness) in healthy adult volunteers and reports task-evoked brain activations (regions such as left superior frontal gyrus, orbitofrontal gyrus, precuneus, etc.). Based on the abstract, it uses functional MRI during social-related tasks (I3) with a healthy adult sample (I4) and reports group-level whole-brain activation findings (I5/I6). However, the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided), so methods, exact whole-brain analysis details, and participant ages cannot be fully verified; therefore confidence is moderate. No exclusion criteria are evident from the available excerpt.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of a social cognition task (false-belief / theory-of-mind), satisfying I3. It includes healthy adult control groups (Caltech n=18, MIT n=462; ages include 18–69), satisfying I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain analyses for the healthy/reference groups (e.g., MIT unthresholded map, whole-brain renderings in Fig. 2, and Table S1), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of self-processing (Perception/Understanding of Self), a social-related construct. Sample: 24 healthy adult participants (ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise random-effects analyses and tables/coordinates for task contrasts (e.g., general>contextual; interaction contrasts) in the healthy groups, as well as ROI analyses; whole-brain results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, participants in age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study probing social-related processing (meaning vs physical judgments of symbolic artifacts) with tasks that explicitly engage social cognition. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 24, right-handed, no history of neurological/mental problems). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts using SPM8 (random-effects second-level analyses) with corrected thresholds and tables/figures of peak coordinates (meaning>physical, own>other, interaction effects), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This randomized, double-blind, within-subject fMRI study (n=21 healthy adults, ages 20–37) directly investigates social processing using the interactive Cyberball social exclusion task during functional MRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., not receiving ESE > receiving INCL) with whole-brain results presented (Tables S3 and S4) and peak coordinates, and describes the healthy/control group results separately. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task maps/contrasts), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and tabulated). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=13 and n=18; ages 18–41) that explicitly contrasts vocal versus non-vocal sounds and interprets vocal processing as social/communicative perception. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and contrasts (vocal > non-vocal) are reported (voxelwise FDR p<0.05, cluster thresholds) and shown in figures/tables. The study therefore meets: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — voice perception/social communication), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for healthy participants), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered: the paper includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), includes task activations (not only resting-state/seed/connectivity), reports within-group healthy effects (not only between-group contrasts), and is empirical. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using social stimuli (affiliation and power movie clips) and an individual-differences approach. Sample: 17 healthy adult male participants (mean age 23.6), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (affiliation > control; power > control) analyzed with SPM and provides cluster coordinates and tables/figures (Table 1, MNI coordinates, Fig. 2), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The study is empirical fMRI research in healthy adults and not limited to ROI- or connectivity-only analyses. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.
