This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task: participants judged whether a moving dot appeared animate (perception/understanding of others). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–36, N reported; fMRI groups of 19 each after exclusions), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (conjunctions, whole-brain FWE-corrected maps) and provides coordinates and tables of activations (Tables S1/S2, figures), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a resting-state fMRI study manipulating participants’ belief about being observed; participants are healthy adults (age 18–22). However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps from a social task. Analyses focus on resting-state / connectivity (node-node Pearson correlations and network-level connectivity based on Neurosynth-derived maps). Therefore it meets exclusion E3 (resting-state/connectivity analyses only) and does not meet inclusion I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked map). Inclusion I4 (healthy adult sample) is met. Inclusion I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is not met as this is not a task-based social paradigm but a resting-state manipulation of implied social presence. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults examining processing of mutual vs. averted social gaze (a social-cognitive task). The sample includes healthy young adults (fMRI N=8), within the 18–65 range. The authors report group-level voxelwise whole-brain activation maps (t-statistic activation maps averaged across subjects and displayed on a standard brain; Figure 4) in addition to ROI analyses, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not between-group-only; participants are in age range; empirical data are presented).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social joint action (leading, following, mutual) involving haptic interaction—clearly a social-related task. Sample: healthy adult dancers (n=18 analyzed, mean age 40.4), meeting the adult age requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and provides Talairach coordinates and whole-brain maps/tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of moral reasoning—a social-cognition task—meeting the review objective. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=28) with results reported separately. It reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps/analyses for the healthy group (one-sample analyses, FWE-corrected results; tables and figures provided), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain task effects. Participants are adults within the 18–55 range. Reporting of results appears in the main text (tables/figures) and meets the acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social interactions (live face-to-face and joint attention tasks) in healthy adult samples (Experiment 1: n=16, ages 18–29; Experiment 2: n=13, ages 18–29). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Live > Recorded; Joint Attention > Solo Attention) with corrected statistical maps and tables of coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an fMRI study using a social/theory-of-mind task (Frith–Happé animations) and includes a clearly reported healthy control group of adults aged 19–56. The paper describes group-level one-sample t-tests and whole-brain analyses for each group (results referenced in main text and Supplementary Data), and presents whole-brain activation maps and cluster results identified for contrasts in the neurotypical group and subgroup analyses. Thus it provides whole-brain, task-evoked group maps for the healthy/control group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only without unmasked healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interactive task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) and a well-matched non-social control (Gamble). Participants are healthy adults (Exp 1: n=20 females, mean age ~20.8; Exp 2: n=30, mean age ~21.2), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (PD vs. Gamble; in-group vs. out-group contrasts and whole-brain exploratory analyses) with tables of activations, thresholding, and figures—satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Although ROI and connectivity analyses are also presented, these are supplementary to and do not replace the reported whole-brain random-effects maps. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related visual perspective-taking task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (age 18–50) with results reported (I4). However, task-evoked activation analyses were restricted to predefined prefrontal ROIs (region-of-interest analyses) and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Instead it reports ROI task results and seed-based connectivity analyses. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E4 (no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete. Excluded for lack of required whole-brain healthy-group task activation map.

Full text appears incomplete here (only abstract/highlights provided). I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: Prisoner’s Dilemma mentalizing) is clearly satisfied. However, I cannot verify I4 (participants are adults age 18–65) because the methods/participant details are not present, and I cannot confirm I5 (reporting of at least one unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy/control group) despite the abstract listing activated regions. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on the available content. Because essential information needed to confirm I4 and I5 is missing from the provided full text, the study is excluded for incomplete reporting/full text. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3. Inclusion IDs not met / not verifiable: I4, I5.

This is a resting-state seed-based functional connectivity study in a pediatric sample (male children/adolescents, age 6.5–18.7) contrasting ASD and typically developing children. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only resting-state / seed-based connectivity without any task-evoked fMRI/social task) and E5 (participants are outside the healthy adult age range 18–65). No inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (no task-based social fMRI), I4 (no healthy adult group aged 18–65), I5 (no whole-brain, task-evoked healthy-group map), I6 (not applicable because no task results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

Exclusion (E2) met: the study reports only ROI analyses focused on the amygdala and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Inclusion met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — threat-related social facial expressions) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group). Inclusion not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task activation map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given the absence of any whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps (only ROI results), this study does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task evidence and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=63; ages 20.4–36.6) that explicitly employs a social incentive delay task with social reward (smiling faces) and reports task-evoked neural activation. The paper presents both ROI and whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level results (e.g., whole-brain FWE-corrected activations reported for insula, visual areas, fusiform gyrus, hippocampus, amygdala; whole-brain tables and figures are provided), and contrasts for social versus monetary reward are reported for the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults examining social processing (Cyberball exclusion and Dictator Game), meeting inclusion criteria: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processes), I4 (healthy adult sample, mean age 20.7, N=26 after exclusions), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts with voxelwise results and peak coordinates; whole-brain contrasts such as Exclusion no ball > Inclusion ball and Excluders > Includers are reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates, figures, and tables). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental materials are not required. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only lacking healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using a public good game (social tie formation and prosocial decision-making). The sample includes healthy adults (25 scanned participants, ages 22–23) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (parametric modulations and contrasts with MNI coordinates and clusterwise FWE correction). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (empathy, ToM, self–other differentiation) in healthy adults (n=15 males, age 18–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and voxelwise contrasts (main effects, interactions) with coordinate tables and figures, clearly from the healthy sample. Thus it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text describes an fMRI study of social cognition (attribute framing/self and reflected perspectives), with a healthy adult sample (N=21, ages 19–41; analyses exclude two participants), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frame, frame-consistent vs inconsistent) with voxelwise thresholds, cluster-size correction, coordinates, and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical fMRI study (HCP data, N=493 healthy adult subjects) includes analyses of working memory, motor, and social cognition tasks. The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation results (GLM-derived mean activation maps and sensitivity analyses; e.g., Fig. 9b, Fig. S3/S4) linked to task conditions and interprets whole-brain task activations for healthy subjects. Participants are healthy adults from HCP, and whole-brain, group-level task effects are presented (figures and quantitative analyses). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

The study reports task-based fMRI of emotional face discrimination, a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). Sample includes 38 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 27.5) within 18–65. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrast maps (FACES>OBJECTS) with SPM results, figures (axial/coronal SPM t-maps), and cluster-level inference (p<0.001 voxelwise, p<0.05 FWE cluster-corrected), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this review.

Provided content appears to be metadata and abstract only (full text incomplete). From the abstract, the study used fMRI during incidental fearful face processing (social-related task) and included a healthy adult control group (13 controls). However, the provided material does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (no whole-brain activation map or coordinates are available in the supplied content). Therefore inclusion criterion I3 and I4 are satisfied, but I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map) is not met in the available content. Because the full article (methods, results, and figures/tables) is not present, I cannot determine whether exclusion criteria such as E2, E3, or E4 apply. I therefore exclude this record at this stage due to incomplete full text and lack of evidence for I5; full text should be retrieved to complete screening.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related task (passive viewing of facial emotions), satisfying I3. It includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=27) with ages within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain task activation results for the control group (described in Results and shown in figures/tables; full list in Supplementary), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy maps, participants are adults, and it is an empirical fMRI study).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a social cognition task (affective and cognitive Theory of Mind) meeting the review objective. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected cluster results, peak coordinates and tables/figures for task effects and RFQ regression), and results for the healthy group are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of eligibility.

This empirical study used task-based fMRI during a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma), tested healthy adult participants aged 18–22, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM, cluster-corrected Z-thresholding) with results presented in the text/figures/tables. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-connectivity only, includes a healthy adult group within 18–65, and is an empirical fMRI study. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examined processing of facial color—a social communication cue—during an in-scanner task (viewing faces and scrambled images with target detection). Sample: 25 healthy adults (mean age 25.24), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (natural-colored face vs natural-colored scrambled image) and used those maps to localize face-selective regions (thresholds and coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. The content includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Only the abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true), so I cannot verify whether the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (required I5). The study clearly investigates a social cognition task (theory of mind) using fMRI and includes younger and older healthy adults (I3 and I4 met). However, without the full text/methods/results I cannot confirm whole-brain task activation reporting (I5 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria appear to be triggered based on the abstract, but the missing full text prevents definitive inclusion. Therefore I exclude pending access to the complete article.

This is a task-based fMRI study of live verbal social interaction (social communication). Participants: 22 healthy adult women (mean age 27.2), meeting the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (second-level voxel-wise t-tests, cluster correction; figures/tables including supplementary Table S2 and Fig. S1), providing unmasked whole-brain task effects for talking/listening/imagining and inter-individual coupling. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state-only, patient-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining implicit attitudes and executive control in regulating interest in extra-pair relationships (a social/affiliative/attachment domain). Sample: 27 healthy adult males (ages within 18–65) with no neurological/psychiatric history — meets I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts for the IAT (incongruent vs. congruent) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates — satisfying I5 and I6. The experimental tasks and contrasts clearly probe social/attachment processing (I3). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (social reflection: self and other judgments) during task-based fMRI (meets I3). It reports a healthy adult sample (n=22, mean age 37.4, screened to exclude psychiatric disorders), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain (cortical surface–based and cluster-corrected) task activation results for the SR > AL contrast (figures and Tables 1–3, cluster-wise corrected maps and coordinates), clearly from the healthy group, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state analyses, not between-group-only contrasts, and participants are adults within 18–65. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text is incomplete: the provided content is a website cookie/privacy preference page rather than the article text (missing introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I cannot verify whether the study used fMRI during a social-related task (I3), included a healthy adult group (I4), or reported whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps (I5/I6). Because core article content is not available, I must exclude the record pending access to the full article. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (affective Theory of Mind using cartoons and emotional facial expressions), meeting the review topic. Sample: 22 recruited, 21 healthy adult datasets (mean age 23.7) — meets healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., EFE > no EFE) with tables/coordinates and cluster-corrected results, and describes ROI analyses secondarily. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI using socially relevant stimuli (social interaction, human faces, erotica) and directly examines neural responses to social stimuli (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, mean age 28.2) reported separately from the depressed group (meets I4). The authors performed voxelwise, whole-brain repeated-measures ANOVAs and report group-level whole-brain cluster results and coordinates (Tables 3–5) and figures, and they describe within-group (control) contrasts (e.g., greater activation to social interaction at time 1), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps/contrasts (meets I5 and I6). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only reporting, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This fMRI study examines perception and anticipation of an opponent's actions (perception/understanding of others), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult badminton players. Methods report group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., shots–mctrl contrasts, thresholded at p<0.05 FWE) with coordinates/figures of activations. The sample comprises healthy adult participants across expertise levels. Whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not patient-only, and is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of empathy (perception/understanding of others), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=23, ages 19–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task contrasts (e.g., Pain > No Pain; No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar) with stereotactic coordinates and thresholding, and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported for healthy group), and I6 (results reported as coordinate tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes primary whole-brain healthy-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about friends vs kin) using a task-based paradigm during BOLD fMRI, satisfying the review’s domain. The sample is healthy adults (n=25 females, mean age 23.2), meeting the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (friend > kin, kin > friend no significant clusters) and linear parametric whole-brain analyses across network layers with cluster-thresholded results and coordinate tables/figures (i.e., whole-brain statistical maps reported as corrected clusters and local maxima). Reporting includes tables of cluster coordinates and thresholding details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not a non-empirical paper, and healthy adult group results are reported). Full text materials (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) are present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (legal decision-making involving inferences about others’ mental states and moral judgments), meeting I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=20 after exclusions; ages 18–45), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation results (whole-brain contrasts, tables of peak coordinates, and descriptions of voxelwise effects), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results (behavioral, ROI, and whole-brain analyses), and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete: provided content contains only title/metadata/navigation and lacks core article sections (methods, participants, results, figures/tables). Therefore I cannot verify the required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria not confirmed: I3 (cannot confirm that a task-based fMRI social-related whole-brain task effect for healthy adults is reported), I4 (sample characteristics and separate healthy-group results not verifiable), I5 (no evidence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map for the healthy group), I6 (supplementary/tables/figures with whole-brain results not available). No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are identified from the available metadata alone. Because core content is missing, the study cannot be judged as meeting all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded pending a complete full text.

This study reports fMRI task data addressing social cognition (imagined triadic interactions, self- and other-referential processing), tested in a healthy adult sample (N=19, mean age 26.5). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., triad>iron, conjunctions, and contrasts triad>(self&other)) are reported with family-wise error correction and peak coordinates/tables. Behavioral methods, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, GLM and second-level group analyses are fully described. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults with whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports task-based functional MRI during observation of virtual social interactions (I3). It reports data from a group-level analysis (activation maps based on data from 15 participants) showing whole-brain task-evoked activations in social cognition regions (STS, mPFC, amygdala), satisfying whole-brain reporting (I5, I6). Participants are described as recruited based on age/health and providing written informed consent; group data are presented separately (healthy adults implied), satisfying the sample criterion (I4). The full text includes methods, scanning parameters, preprocessing, and representative group results, so core article content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical) are met. Minor uncertainty remains because exact ages are not explicitly listed in the excerpt; confidence is therefore 0.80.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (modified Cyberball with social exclusion and performance evaluation) collected in healthy adult participants (N=40; mean age 27.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8 random-effects; voxel-level FWE-corrected results; tables of MNI coordinates and contrasts such as EX > IN, conjunctions, and PG EX > FG EX). Reporting of whole-brain results is provided in tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of political (social) attitude processing using the IAT during task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 21–40). The methods report a within-subject task, sample of healthy adults, preprocessing and voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (including FDR correction), and reported activations/coordinates and correlational whole-brain results. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures and described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain effects, age in range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) using the EmpaToM paradigm in a healthy adult sample (N=178; mean age 40.9, within 18–65). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task contrasts are reported and entered into one-sample t-tests/random-effects analyses (empathy: emotional vs neutral videos; ToM: ToM vs non-ToM questions/videos) with coordinates, figures and tables provided. Behavioral and neural results for the healthy group are clearly presented. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activations despite also reporting connectivity/DCM/resting-state). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social sharing/affiliation) in healthy adults (n=58–60, ages 20–33). The task is social-related (shared vs unshared viewing of emotional pictures) and uses fMRI during task performance. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses and whole-brain-corrected activations (e.g., DLPFC, precuneus) in addition to ROI results; contrasts are clearly from the healthy participant group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=13, mean age 27.2) that used whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses to test responses while subjects watched video clips of social interactions. The task is explicitly social (observation of social relational interactions). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (relational vs. alone; relational vs. rest) with multiple-comparison correction and presents figures and tables of activated clusters (e.g., DMPFC, precuneus) and time courses. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the provided full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social-evaluation task (being watched by a peer) and includes a sample of healthy participants that contains adults aged 18–22.9. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical results (e.g., MPFC activation related to age effects) and whole-brain PPI connectivity analyses, clearly coming from the healthy sample. Although analyses model age continuously across a mixed-age sample rather than presenting an adult-only contrast, the inclusion criteria require healthy adult participants and whole-brain healthy-group results, both of which are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–22) that uses a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) probing social interaction and unreciprocated cooperation. The paper reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses (e.g., main effect CD>CC and whole-brain OT/AVP effects described and shown in figures and supplementary resources) in the healthy sample, and presents coordinates/tables and corrected cluster results. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study (dynamic multimodal empathy task) directly investigates social-related processing (empathy, perception/understanding of others) using task-based whole-brain fMRI. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=24, mean age 35.25) and reports group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript describes whole-brain GLM analyses, cluster-level correction, and presents within-group T-contrasts for each participant group (reported in main text and online supplementary Tables/Figures), satisfying the requirement for an unmasked healthy-group task effect. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplemental materials referenced but not required). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level healthy-task results), and I6 (whole-brain results allowed in supplement).

This is an fMRI study of social gaze (social-related task) in healthy adult participants (23 right-handed volunteers, ages 21–37). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (main effects and interactions) analyzed with SPM5 and thresholded/cluster-corrected; results are presented in text, figures and tables. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This fMRI study examined neural processing during perception of co-speech gestures in a continuous narrative—directly addressing social communication (social-related processing). Participants: 20 healthy adults (ages 22–35). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported (SPM12 analyses, cluster-corrected results and tables/figures of activation peaks). Thus it meets I3 (social communication task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study directly examines social-related processing (social attribution vs visuospatial task) using task-based fMRI (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=17, ages 18–45) reported separately from the recovered-anorexia group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (People – Bumper) for all participants and separately for the control group (figures and tables of coordinates; Tables 2–4, Fig.3), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the review: (I3) Task is social-related (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation — perception/understanding of self), (I4) Sample comprises healthy adults (final N=31, ages 19–24), (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (GLM whole-brain analyses with reported contrasts and Tables 2/3), and (I6) Whole-brain results are provided in text/tables/figures with statistical thresholds (voxel-wise p<0.001 and cluster-level FWE p<0.05). The full article contains introduction, methods, results (behavioral and fMRI), connectivity analyses, discussion, and references, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (facial emotion recognition/implicit emotion processing), using healthy adult participants (N=29, ages 20–35). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected maps and tables of activated regions, direct contrasts explicit vs implicit) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study (combined EEG-fMRI) that examines social processing (minimal group affiliation and perception of others) using a group categorization task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=20 analyzed, mean age 23.4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses (with voxelwise threshold and cluster-level FWE correction) identifying clusters (e.g., mPFC, STS/TPJ) and refers to coordinates/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This empirical fMRI study (n=110 healthy adults, age 19–31) used a social-cognitive task comparing self-reference (SR) and other-reference (OR) versus a non-semantic control, meeting the review’s focus. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results (second-level random-effects analyses with FWE correction) and displays voxelwise activation maps and contrasts (e.g., SR>OR, OR>SR). Although the paper also reports effective connectivity (DCM), it includes unambiguous whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy sample. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (appropriate reporting). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social interaction (gaze-based joint attention) in healthy adult participants (n=24; ages 20–34), meeting I3 and I4. Group-level, voxelwise contrasts (e.g., self>other, JA>NJA, selfjoint>selfnonjoint) were computed with second-level random-effects analyses and reported with peak MNI coordinates and statistical inference (albeit using small-volume correction within a priori ROIs). These constitute group-level task-evoked voxelwise results for the healthy sample and are reported in the text/tables/figures, satisfying I5 and the allowance in I6. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social-related processing (empathy for pain modulated by experimentally induced ingroup/outgroup membership), using a task-based paradigm. Sample: 30 healthy adult participants (ages 18–35) reported separately; meets healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 ANOVA), with tables and descriptions of main effects and interactions, including FWE-corrected results and uncorrected maps; whole-brain coordinate tables are provided. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Provided content contains highlights, abstract, and references but lacks core full-text sections (methods, participant demographics, full results). Inclusion I3 (fMRI social task) is satisfied based on abstract. Cannot confirm I4 (healthy adult sample, age 18–65) or I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) from the available material. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met. fulltext_incomplete=true pending access to complete methods and results to verify participant sample and whole-brain reporting.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses fMRI during a social-related task (joint attention/gaze perception and attribution of what another person sees—a Perception and Understanding of Others paradigm). (I4) The sample comprises healthy adults aged 20–31 (group-level results reported for the healthy participants). (I5) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task contrasts (body>place and place>body) with whole-brain statistical maps and cluster tables. (I6) Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables and described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy whole-brain task effects, participants in age range, empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports fMRI data collected during an interactive social gaze (joint attention) task (study II), a social-related paradigm (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=16) with results analyzed and reported separately (meets I4). The authors conducted second-level one-sample t tests in the control group for task contrasts (self-initiated JA > NJA) and report activation in reward-related regions for controls (results referenced in the main text and Supplementary Table S4 and Fig. S4), satisfying the requirement for a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked map from the healthy group (meets I5). The paper also provides coordinates and SVC-corrected results and describes within-group effects in text and supplemental materials (meets I6). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only).

This fMRI study directly probes social-related processing by contrasting why vs how conceptualizations of actions, engaging mentalizing/theory-of-mind networks (perception and understanding of others). Sample consists of healthy adult participants within 18–65 (N=17 analyzed; mean age 29.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (voxelwise contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) with results described in main text, figures, and supplementary tables of coordinates. Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (whole-brain results provided in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Full text reports an fMRI study of causal attribution (social/mentalizing task) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–41) with no psychiatric diagnoses. The paper presents group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (voxelwise thresholds and whole-brain FWE-corrected results are reported) alongside ROI analyses; behavioral and imaging results are reported for the healthy sample. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain results.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (impression formation/person evaluation) meeting the review objective (I3). The sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants aged 19–31, satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement (I4). The manuscript includes an exploratory whole-brain, voxelwise analysis (group-level ANOVA) with reported activations in Table 1 and Figure 3 (coordinates and cluster information), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results (I5) and reporting of those results in tables/figures/text (I6). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full-text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants underwent fMRI while viewing faces whose social roles were learned in a cyber-ball social interaction paradigm (social affiliation/ostracism). Sample: 15 healthy adults (mean age 24.1) — meets healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from an exploratory searchlight analysis (random-effects SPM group analysis, FWE-corrected clusters in superior temporal sulcus reported with MNI coordinates), and these whole-brain results are described in the text with coordinates — satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study probes social-related processing (integration of voice-based speaker characteristics with sentence content — pragmatic social inference), includes a healthy adult control group (n=24, ages 18–39) with results reported separately, and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses and within-group contrasts for the control group (reported in text/tables/figures). Full article contains intro, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (ultimatum game) in healthy adult participants (male, ages 23–28), satisfying the population criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level multivariate (SVM) analyses across subjects with voxelwise discriminating volumes provided as MNI coordinates and figures/tables (thresholded at p<0.05, cluster size reported), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. The study uses an explicit social task (UG), reports methods, results, and discussion in full text, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study uses task-based fMRI of social stimuli (erotic and fearful social scenes) in healthy adult participants (N=55 males, mean age ~24.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., erotic > neutral; fearful > neutral; erotic > fearful) with voxelwise FWE-corrected results and ROI analyses; coordinates and cluster results are described in the text/tables/supplement. This clearly meets the review’s focus on social-related processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain, healthy-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical study, or out-of-range participants) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic happy and fearful facial expressions) with both a healthy adult control group (age ~early 20s) and a familial-risk group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and within-group BOLD responses for both groups (figures and cluster-thresholded maps described; group analyses used FLAME and cluster correction). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented (figures/tables and text). The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, is empirical). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social communication (referential collaborative vs. individual learning) in healthy adults. The sample consists of healthy participants aged 18–33. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Collaborative > Individual, Individual > Arbitrary, Arbitrary > Individual) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures describing whole-brain results; ROI analyses are supplementary. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults: participants (N=20, ages 18–27) performed a task of thinking about others’ mental states (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain multivariate (searchlight) and univariate analyses combined via one-sample random-effects t tests, corrected maps, tables of regions (Tables S2/S3), and network-level whole-brain results—satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting for the healthy group. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social cooperation (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma), meeting the review objective. It reports task-evoked BOLD responses during a social task (I3). The sample includes healthy adult participants (final imaging N=18, mean age ~21) within 18–65 (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (CC vs. other outcomes), with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates in tables/figures (I5, I6). The full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical).

This fMRI study uses a social task (processing direct vs. averted gaze), which falls under social perception/understanding of others. It includes a typically developing (healthy) control group with adults (reported ages 16.1–42.4) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts for the healthy/control group (Direct > Averted; Table 2, reported statistical maps and coordinates). Whole-brain results for the control group are clearly reported in tables and text. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Note: the healthy group includes some adolescents (<18) but also adults and the healthy group results are reported separately; this was considered acceptable for I4.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports only between-group (high-risk vs low-risk) whole-brain contrasts (control minus high-risk) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task—Reading the Mind in the Eyes) and I4 (there is a healthy control adult group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using the RMET, a social cognitive task (meets I3). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (16 women, mean age 20.8) meeting the 18–65 range (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (emotion vs control), with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction and tables of peak coordinates (meets I5 and I6). The full text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided (fulltext_incomplete = false). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only, results include whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study used task-based fMRI of biological motion perception (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others), enrolled healthy adult participants (mean age 28.2, n=13), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (canonical vs scrambled biological motion, p<0.05 corrected) with tables/figures. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports only between-group (patient vs control) whole-brain contrasts and group-difference results; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-control group task activation map (no within-group/control group whole-brain task effect is reported in the Results or Tables). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — dynamic face/emotion processing) and I4 (healthy adult control group reported, age-matched 21 controls between 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map identified as coming from the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this fMRI study uses a social-related task (being liked by peers) and reports whole-brain task results, the sample is a mixed group of late adolescents (18–21) that includes both healthy and clinical (current MDD) participants and the paper does not report a separate whole-brain, group-level task activation map for a healthy adult/control subgroup. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5 (no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social fMRI task) and I6 (acceptable reporting formats). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (no accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

Provided content appears to be an abstract-level summary only (full text incomplete). While the study uses fMRI during social-related tasks (viewing/imitating facial expressions and social hand gestures), the excerpt does not report participant details (age range or explicit statement that participants were healthy adults aged 18–65) nor does it explicitly state that group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables/figures for the healthy group are reported. Therefore I3 is met, but I4 and I5 (and I6) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be positively identified from the truncated text, but full-text is incomplete and additional information is required to confirm inclusion. Recommend obtaining the complete article (methods and results) to re-assess.

This fMRI study investigates social cognition during naturalistic movie viewing (reverse correlation identifying scenes of social interaction), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample: 34 healthy adults (mean age 22.2) meets the adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise reverse correlation analyses and group-level maps (e.g., Figure 3; χ2 tests with whole-brain correction and reported clusters), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is a resting-state fcMRI investigation in adolescents with ASD and matched typically developing adolescents (ages 11–18). It does not use task-based fMRI of social processing (violates I3), does not include a healthy adult sample aged 18–65 (violates I4/E5), and does not report any group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for a healthy adult group (violates I5). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (resting-state analyses only, no task activation maps) and E5 (participants outside 18–65 with no separate healthy adult subgroup). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (task-based social fMRI), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain task-evoked maps for healthy group) [I6 not applicable because no task results are reported]. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded from this review.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports only between-group contrasts (VCFS vs controls) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related facial emotion processing task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=9, mean age 37). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level task-evoked map reported for the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails I5 and meets exclusion E4.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognitive (Theory of Mind) task (animated interacting shapes) (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=20; ages 22–56) reported separately from the clinical bipolar group (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps and coordinates for the healthy subjects (within-group ToM > random-motion contrasts) with tables and figures and corrected voxelwise thresholds (meets I5 and I6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of analyses and results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, within-range ages, and is empirical).

Although the study used fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps, it does not investigate a clearly social-related task/construct. The paradigm centers on negative emotion processing using IAPS images (emotion/reactivity), with a simple perceptual button-press (person present) and subjective emotion ratings. While the discussion links dmPFC to social cognition, the experimental task does not target social processes (e.g., theory of mind, social communication, affiliation, explicit perception/understanding of others) as defined by the review objective. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task) is not met, while I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports event-related fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–30) performing social evaluations (trustworthiness judgments of faces). It provides group-level, random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPMs) and reports voxelwise results and coordinate tables; small-volume corrections are used for ROIs but whole-brain task-evoked effects and coordinates are clearly presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, stimuli, imaging and analysis), Results and Discussion, and thus appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study should be excluded because it does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps. Specifically: (a) Exclusion criteria met: E2 (analyses were performed using small-volume/ROI correction and the second-level analyses were restricted to pre-specified ROIs rather than reporting unmasked whole-brain results) and E4 (the paper focuses on between-group contrasts [ALS > HC; HC > ALS] and does not report an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect or main-effect activation map for the control group). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used fMRI during a social-related task — Theory of Mind) and I4 (a healthy adult control group is reported; controls’ age distribution includes adults within 18–65). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group). The full text appears complete. Given these points, the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis objective requiring healthy-group whole-brain task activations.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study of social gaze processing (a social-related task), includes a neurologically normal healthy adult comparison group (n=9; ages within 18–65) with results reported separately, and presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables for the healthy/control group (figures, Table 1, and random-effects analyses). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes healthy adult whole-brain task activation maps). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social-emotional processing (face emotion discrimination), with a community sample of healthy adults (screened with SCID, IRB consent), and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (EE vs baseline; EE vs EI) with tables/coordinates. The task probes social cognition (emotion perception/understanding of others). The full text includes intro, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing: it uses an event-related Social motor response learning task involving social inclusion/exclusion animations and records BOLD responses (I3). Sample is 18 healthy adults age 42±12 (within 18–65) with no psychiatric history (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with whole-brain FDR correction and presents significant activations (figures/tables) identified for the healthy group (I5,I6). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/summary and metadata provided). From available content I can confirm: I3 (study uses fMRI on social-related task—face perception and expression). I cannot confirm I4 (no participant demographics or ages provided to verify healthy adults 18–65) nor I5 (the manuscript summary reports region responses but does not explicitly state whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task maps or provide coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied from the truncated content. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the provided full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article (methods/results) to confirm sample and whole-brain results.

This fMRI study investigates voice processing (social perception/communication) and reports group-level whole-brain task activation for healthy adult controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — voice perception), I4 (healthy adult control group, results reported separately), I5 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps for controls reported), and I6 (results described in text and figures). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, and does report unmasked healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary material is noted but not required. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (third-party punishment) meeting the review objective. It collected task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages ~26, within 18–65) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM; whole-brain FDR threshold q<0.05) with peak coordinates and figures for main effects and interactions. The text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are presented in the main paper (coordinates, statistical maps/figures). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of charitable donation decisions (socially relevant: altruism, affiliation/attachment). Sample: 19 healthy adult participants (mean age 28.2), within 18–65. Methods report whole-brain GLM with random-effects group analyses and contrasts, results reported with coordinate tables/figures and cluster thresholds (P<0.005) and supporting tables—satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables/figures are referenced. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This empirical fMRI study used a social-related task (passive viewing of point-light displays of biological motion), includes a healthy adult sample reported separately (n=48, ages 20–35), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (biological > scrambled) with cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables. Thus it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-related task: perception/understanding of self). Participants were healthy adults (n=12; mean age 19.36) meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM group contrasts) and presents thresholded maps and tables of activations for contrasts (e.g., self vs familiar, familiar vs unknown), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related gaze-following task (politicians’ gaze) that probes social perception/affiliation processes, satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=28 analyzed, ages 18–29), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, Table 3 and figures), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and appears complete, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and should be included.

This study used task-based fMRI to probe empathy for others’ pain (a social-related construct: perception/understanding of others), included a separate healthy adult control group (N=13; ages within 18–65), and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and coordinate tables/figures for the control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (imaging acquisition and whole-brain random-effects analyses), Results (within-group activations, tables of coordinates, figures), and Discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but core article content is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an original task-based fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) in healthy adults. Methods report 19 healthy participants aged 20–53, satisfying the adult sample criterion. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., SocAdj > PhyConf) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction, and tables of peak coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided in the submission. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The full text reports an event-related fMRI study using a social cognitive task (false belief/theory-of-mind), meeting the review objective. Sample: 34 healthy adults aged 20–28 (meets age and healthy participant requirement). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrast (ROMS vs CTRL) is reported with statistical activation maps and a coordinate table, analyzed with SPM2 and appropriate group-level thresholds. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20 males, ages 21–37) that used a social task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) during task-based fMRI and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and second-level analyses (FWE cluster-corrected maps, tables and extracted contrasts). All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (functional MRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (interpersonal resource conflict) using a social vs computer task, meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adults (final N=17, mean age 23.5), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Conflict > No Conflict; interaction and conjunction analyses) from random-effects second-level analyses, with tables/figures of activations and coordinates, meeting I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study manipulating social information (trustworthiness) and working memory load in healthy adults (mean age 22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2x2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and provides tables of peak coordinates and figures showing main effects and interactions. Thus it meets: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked voxelwise maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not out-of-range ages, and not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The paper reports original task-based fMRI data in healthy adult participants (age ranges and means within 18–65), employing social-cognition (Theory of Mind) tasks (Why/How and False-Belief Localizer), thus addressing social-related processing. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts are reported (e.g., Why>How; Belief>Photo) with cluster- and voxel-level FWE correction and tables of peak coordinates across samples (Studies 1–3). Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are present, indicating the provided full text is complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures with clear description). No exclusion criteria are met.

Provided full text is incomplete (only cookie/website boilerplate and metadata). Cannot verify whether the study used task-based fMRI in a social-related task (I3), whether a healthy adult group (age 18–65) is reported separately (I4), or whether whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation maps are reported (I5/I6). Therefore I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from the list can be confidently identified from the available material. Exclusion decision is due to incomplete full text preventing assessment of I3–I6.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It used task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (race perception and trustworthiness evaluations), addressing social-related processing. The sample comprises 30 healthy adult participants (White, ages 18–29), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., Black>White contrasts), peak coordinates, cluster thresholds, and corrected significance levels; results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text. Although PPI connectivity analyses are reported, they are supplementary to and do not replace the whole-brain activation maps. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria were met.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract/metadata, lacking methods, participant details, and results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task — dyadic eye-contact interaction). Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be verified: I4 (no information on sample age or whether healthy adults are reported separately), I5 (no clear report of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps). No exclusion criteria clearly met from the available text. Because core information is missing, the study cannot be confirmed eligible.

This paper reports fMRI task-based investigations of social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) in healthy adult samples (Experiments 1a/b and 2; participant ages and Ns reported, within 18–65). The EmpaToM is a social-related task and neural results include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., emotionally negative > neutral videos; ToM > nonToM questions) with reported activation tables, thresholding details, and resting-state whole-brain connectivity analyses. Behavioral and neural validation vs. established tasks are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, analysis), Results (behavioral, physiological, fMRI), Discussion, and supplementary references, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants played a competitive matching-pennies game after brief social interactions with five opponent types, addressing perception/understanding of others and mentalizing. Sample: healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–25). fMRI methods report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (GLM, random-effects one-sample t-tests, voxel-wise threshold p<.001 and cluster-level FWE correction; Tables 2–3 list peak coordinates), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses fMRI during an adaptive emotion-recognition task (social cognition) and includes a healthy adult control group (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the paper reports mainly between-group contrasts, group-by-emotion interactions, and ROI analyses; it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., no standalone whole-brain healthy-group activation map is reported). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotional sentence attribution that explicitly targets social-cognitive processes (emotion, theory of mind, social communication). The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=25) with results reported separately and describes whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (task effects and group/interaction contrasts, with FWE-corrected whole-brain thresholds and figures/tables). Whole-brain healthy-group activations (including a control-specific mPFC EMO effect) are reported and described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (empathic concern) using empathy-evoking film clips and contextual/musical manipulations. Participants are healthy adults (n=26, mean age 30.3), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results (GLM contrasts, cluster-level FWE-corrected maps/tables and figures) clearly identified for the healthy sample, and coordinates/figures are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition (a second-order Theory of Mind task) meeting the review objective. Evidence: (1) fMRI task explicitly targets social-related processing (ToM/self vs other, threat/boost scenarios) fulfilling I3. (2) Healthy control group (n=25, ages 18–60) is reported separately from the bipolar group, satisfying I4. (3) The manuscript describes whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports whole-brain results (Table 2 listing activated brain regions during ToM contrasts and whole-brain figures at uncorrected thresholds), and notes that whole-brain analyses and within-group contrasts were completed; ROI analyses were also run within groups — this constitutes group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy/control group (I5). (4) Whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and described in text, consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria appear to be met (e.g., results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and healthy adult subgroup is present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task fMRI study of social processing (joint attention) using hyperscanning fMRI with healthy adult participants (mean ages ~23–24), meeting the sample criterion.
