The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses via group ICA (spatial component maps across the brain) and links component time courses to task phases (INT vs NoINT) with statistical testing; spatial component maps (e.g., rTPJ) are presented and tested at the group level. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level task-related evidence for the healthy sample. The task is explicitly social (sender/receiver joint attention) and results for the healthy groups are reported and replicated. Full text of methods, results, and discussion is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical, out-of-range age) apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (face-based trustworthiness judgments) relevant to perception/understanding of others. It includes a healthy younger adult group (ages 20–33) meeting the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical results (ANOVA and whole-brain analyses, with tables/figures and coordinates), and these results are clearly described for the healthy participants. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (viewing dynamic facial emotional expressions), includes a healthy adult sample (n=40, mean age ~30.5) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (dynamic > static) with thresholded maps and tables of coordinates (one-sample t-test at the second level). The full text contains methods, results, and figures/tables describing whole-brain fMRI activation and coordinates. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The provided content appears to be incomplete (abstract and metadata only). I3 is satisfied: the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (perception of racial ingroup vs outgroup faces). However I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map) cannot be verified from the supplied text, and participant ages (I4: adults 18–65) are not explicitly reported. Because not all inclusion criteria can be confirmed, the study is excluded. No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the provided excerpt. Recommend obtaining the full text to reassess whole-brain reporting and participant ages.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~21) investigating neural responses to others’ pain—a social cognitive task (empathy/perception of others). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts (painful vs non-painful) with FDR-corrected results and whole-brain analyses described for pre- and post-priming sessions, and provides coordinate tables and figures. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task: empathy/perception of others), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps reported), I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participant ages within range, and empirical with original fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (natural social vs nonsocial gestures) using a task during fMRI. Participants are a healthy young adult sample (N=20; mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7) so the study includes healthy adults within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results using TFCE and permutation testing (FSL Randomise) with figures/tables of activations (main effects and interactions), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range-only sample) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This fMRI study recorded BOLD responses in healthy adult participants (N=6) during passive viewing of natural movies that explicitly included social communication categories. The authors used voxelwise encoding models that included a ‘social communication’ category and report group-level, voxelwise analyses (PC projections and cortical flatmaps) aggregated across subjects, providing whole-brain voxelwise maps of category representations for the healthy group. Thus the study (1) involves social-related processing (social communication present in stimuli and modeled) (I3), (2) includes healthy adult participants (I4), (3) reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps/visualizations derived from the healthy cohort (I5), and (4) presents results in figures and text suitable as whole-brain evidence (I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study meets I3 (fMRI of social-related processing: passive viewing of faces — perception/understanding of others) and I4 (includes a healthy adult sample, ages 18–37). However, it does not provide a clearly identified group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map explicitly reported for the healthy adult group alone. The reported whole-brain results are primarily age-regression analyses across the entire sample and participant-level/ROI FFA summaries; no unmasked adult-group whole-brain faces>objects map is presented in the full text. Therefore I5 is not met, so the paper cannot be included. Full text appears complete.

The full text shows this is an fMRI study of social processing with a healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain (searchlight) results reported are for the combined sample (all participants) rather than a healthy-group map; reported healthy-group results are restricted to ROI-based analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task map). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) strictly apply, but failure to meet I5 requires exclusion. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. I3: It uses task-based fMRI to examine social-related processing (mirror neuron system responses and modulation by emotion, relevant to perception/understanding of others). I4: Sample comprises healthy adult participants (final N=19; mean age 27.7, within 18–65). I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (untrained>trained contrasts) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates (e.g., right SMA and IFG), clearly identified as healthy-group effects. I6: Whole-brain results are reported in text, figures, and tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of emotion perception (social communication / perception of others) using task-based whole-brain BOLD acquisition and voxelwise GLM analyses. The participants are healthy adults (university students aged 19–24; Study 2 N=33, mean age 19.67), and group-level whole-brain results are reported (repeated-measures ANOVAs, voxelwise contrasts with PFWE<0.05, tables/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply.

This study is an empirical fMRI experiment that examines social gaze processing (observed eye contact and gaze following), which falls squarely under social-related processing (Social Communication / Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=21; mean age 24.6), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts, cluster tables, and figures with coordinate reporting and thresholding procedures), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core content appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social communication/perception (audiovisual emotional voice and face integration) in a healthy adult sample (N=24, mean age 26.6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported (conjunction AV>A AND AV>V) with coordinates, voxelwise maps, and SVC corrections; additional voxelwise correlation analyses are reported. The full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social decision-making task (modified prisoner’s dilemma) that probes perception/understanding of others’ intentions. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=20, ages 23–45) with results reported separately. The paper presents group-level whole-brain task activation and connectivity analyses for the healthy group (within-group HC (Task > CONT) contrasts, conjunctions, and tables/figures of whole-brain results) with cluster-level correction. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures. The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social/emotional facial affect matching task (social-related processing), includes a healthy adult control group (n=12, ages within 18–65), and reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps/contrasts for the healthy group (Emotion Match > Shape Match within-group results presented in Table 1 and figures). Whole-brain results are reported for the healthy group (not limited to an ROI), and results are described in the text and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met: I3 - the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (face processing). Inclusion criteria not confirmed / not met based on available text: I4 - cannot verify that at least one healthy adult group (18–65) is reported separately (controls are mentioned but group-level healthy results are not clearly detailed); I5 - cannot confirm that a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group is reported. No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the abstract alone (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). This fMRI study investigates social processing (eye contact and mimicry) in healthy adults using task-based fMRI. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Direct > Averted, Incongruent > Congruent, interaction contrasts) with thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction and provides tables of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Sample: 20 healthy adult participants (mean age 23 ± 4.8), satisfying the adult age criterion. The task probes social-related constructs (social communication/affiliation via gaze and mimicry). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs, not only connectivity/resting-state, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and figures/tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

The study used task-based fMRI in a social/empathy paradigm (threat to self, friend, stranger) meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=22, mean age 23.6) satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (threat minus safe), conjunctions, whole-brain corrected analyses, and tables/figures with coordinates (Tables, Figures, Supplementary Materials), meeting the whole-brain evidence reporting requirement. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes healthy adults, is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (emotion processing and theory-of-mind tasks) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, ages 28–31) reported separately. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts (EMOTION–GENDER) for healthy controls (figures and supplementary tables of active clusters and subtraction analyses are described), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Tasks and analyses are clearly described (block design, SPM2 preprocessing, random-effects group analyses at voxelwise p<0.001 with cluster threshold). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are within 18–65). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20, age 21–32) that explicitly investigates social-cognitive processing during personal prayer (a social-related task involving theory-of-mind/social cognition). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts and provides thresholded results and coordinate tables (FDR-corrected whole-brain analyses and tables of coordinates for contrasts such as Personal Praying > Wishes to Santa Claus and Personal Praying > Lord's Prayer). All inclusion criteria are met (social-related task, healthy adult sample, whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported, acceptable reporting of coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates neural processing of perceived cooperation (social interaction) using task-based fMRI (meets I3). It includes a healthy control group of adults (19 controls) reported separately from the patient group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts for the healthy control group (e.g., C+ > C– in controls; FDR-corrected whole-brain results and tables/figures are described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not limited to ROIs, not only connectivity/resting-state, and healthy-group task effects are explicitly reported. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore, include for the meta-analysis of task-based social processing in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study investigating evaluative processes of social/moral emotions (guilt and embarrassment), which fall under social-related processing (Perception/Understanding of Self/Others). Sample: 19 healthy adult participants (mean ages within 18–65) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (G−N, E−N, G−E, E−G) with statistical thresholds, coordinate tables, and figures, and regression analyses—satisfying whole-brain evidence. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI investigation of social-related processing (perspective taking/empathy) in healthy adults (N=18, ages 21–31). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported and described (e.g., Self vs Other, View-Pain vs View-No-Pain) with SPM8 analysis, cluster-level FWE correction, and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying requirements for whole-brain evidence. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related face-processing task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately (behavioral and ROI statistics) (I4). The paper reports whole-brain results for the combined sample and reports coordinate tables for contrasts (I6). However, it does not provide an unmasked, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming specifically from the healthy/control group (i.e., a within-group whole-brain faces>houses map for NT alone). The absence of a healthy-group whole-brain activation map means it fails inclusion criterion I5 and thus meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions or ROI results for the healthy group without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task—viewing socially awkward scenes) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, it does not report a whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The paper presents whole-brain results collapsed across groups and reports group-difference contrasts (NT > ASD), but no unmasked NT-only whole-brain activation map is provided in the full text. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). fulltext appears complete for core content.

The full text reports an fMRI study using a social interaction task (an adapted Taylor Aggression Paradigm presenting opponents' facial expressions), includes a healthy adult sample (32 males, mean age 23.3), and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results (angry>neutral contrasts) with cluster-wise FWE correction, tables, and figures. The paper meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This study is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) investigation of grey matter volume correlates of moral sentiment proneness in healthy adults. Although participants are healthy adults (I4 met), the paper does not report task-evoked, whole-brain functional MRI activation maps from the healthy/control group. The main neuroimaging data are T1-weighted structural analyses (VBM); fMRI data are only referenced from prior work and an SSC-BOLD parameter from a subgroup (N=29) was used as a regressor, but the article does not present a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map or task-based fMRI contrasts. Therefore it does not meet I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task) nor I5 (reports at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I5. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). However the provided content does not specify participant ages or explicitly state that the sample are healthy adults aged 18–65, nor does it provide sufficient methods/results to confirm that at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported. Because I cannot confirm I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) and I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results) from the supplied text, the study cannot be included based on the current incomplete full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met from the available information. To make a final inclusion decision, please provide the complete full text (methods, participant demographics, and whole-brain results/tables/figures).

The study uses fMRI to probe social-related processing (images of group vs individual social situations) and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I3 and I4). However, the reported healthy-group task effects are inferred within a predefined composite ROI (frontopolar, IFG, temporal poles, TPJ) and statistical inference is ROI-constrained (FDR/FWE reported for ROI). The paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map or whole-brain-corrected healthy-group main effect; the only whole-brain–corrected finding reported was a correlation in the rMDD group. Therefore the study reports only ROI-based results with no qualifying whole-brain healthy-group task map, meeting exclusion criterion E2. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map).

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants (N=14 healthy adults, mean age 29.4) performed a task classifying point-light displays as social interaction (SI) versus non-social interaction (NSI). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SI-NSI contrast), with FDR-corrected results, cluster extent thresholds, and peak coordinates presented in tables and figures. The task probes social perception/understanding (social intentions/interaction). Thus the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study used task-based fMRI measuring face identity discrimination (a social perception task) and includes a healthy adult control group (CA; N=17, mean age ~31). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group activation maps for control groups are reported (e.g., mean z-score images and voxelwise ANOVA results showing activation in fusiform gyrus and amygdala for the CA group). Thus the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps for healthy/control group), and I6 (results clearly described in text and figures). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication: participants (healthy adult interns, mean age ~20.6) performed a social-related task (evaluating and deciding whether to recommend ideas), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (buzz, intention, salesperson effects) with voxelwise results, coordinates, thresholds, and corrected significance levels (reported in text and Table 1), satisfying I5 and I6. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Recommend retrieval of the complete article PDF to reassess inclusion once whole-brain healthy-group results can be confirmed.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation/violations of social expectations), involving an event-related task that manipulates stereotypical congruence. Sample: healthy adults aged 19–30 (N=18 analyzed) — meets age and health requirements. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects incongruent vs. congruent contrast; Table of coordinates and figures; FDR-corrected results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, age range appropriate).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that probes social-cognitive processing (imagining/mentalizing body-checking actions), meeting the review's social-related task definition. The paper reports a separate healthy control group (n=15) with group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and coordinates for the healthy group (figures and tables), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Potential minor uncertainty about one participant aged 17 is noted in the sample age range (17–34), but healthy controls are reported separately and fall within the adult range overall; therefore I include it with moderate-high confidence.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (observation of socio-affective touch) and reports results for a healthy, age-matched neurotypical adult group (n=21) separately from the ASD group. The paper provides group-level whole-brain task activation results for the social vs. non-social touch contrast and refers to figures and tables (including MNI coordinates) for the healthy/NT group (Additional file 1: Figure S2 and Table S2), satisfying the requirement that whole-brain healthy-group task effects be reported (tables/figures acceptable). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary results are provided but that is acceptable. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI experiment of self- and other-recognition (social-related processing: perception/understanding of self and others). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=35, ages 18–24) with group-level analyses reported. Whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses are described (SPM5), with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds, tables of peak coordinates and figures showing activations — satisfying whole-brain reporting. Results are presented for healthy participants (not limited to a subgroup). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures reporting). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text is not accessible (content available only via PDF; 'You do not currently have access to this content'), so core methods and results cannot be fully verified. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults investigating social-related processing (perception and evaluation of different laughter types). The sample comprises healthy adults (N=18, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts and conjunction analyses (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures) for healthy participants, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Tasks manipulate social-emotional processing (explicit vs implicit), meeting the social-related task criterion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Consequently, the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports fMRI of social cognition (empathy/Theory of Mind) using verbal narratives—clearly a social-related task. Sample comprises healthy adults (41 participants, ages 18–37). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (SnPM whole-brain analyses, corrected p<0.05) with coordinates and figures/tables. Reporting of whole-brain results in text, figures, and tables satisfies acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/Figures, enabling verification of criteria. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is suitable for inclusion in the review.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI on social-related processing (self/mother/president self-referential task). (I4) Includes a healthy adult control group (n=15, ages 31–58) reported separately. (I5) Reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps/statistics for the healthy control group (Figures and voxel-wise tests with whole-brain correction described). (I6) Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only analyses only, no resting-state/ connectivity-only focus, healthy-group whole-brain task effects provided). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining socio-emotional processing (empathy induction) using naturalistic campaign videos, with healthy adult participants (20 right-handed male volunteers, ages 20–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (CV > NV contrast) with FWE correction and provides tables/figures of significant clusters (STS, IPL), and links brain activation to behavioral measures. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants viewed approaching animated characters whose facial expressions (happy vs. angry) conveyed affiliation/dominance, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy young adults (n=10) within the adult range. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry) with MNI coordinates and cluster descriptions (table/figures), meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (i.e., core article content). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-affective mimicry task (SAMT) probing affiliation-relevant processes (affiliation/appeasement, self-other distinction). Participants were healthy adults (n=41 included in fMRI; mean age ~22.6, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (Incongruent>Congruent and masked contrasts) with cluster-level correction and tables of coordinates (Tables 2–4) and detailed methods for whole-brain SPM analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It employs task-based functional MRI to probe social-related processing (context-dependent social touch; affiliation/ social communication constructs), reports within-subject whole-brain voxelwise task effects and group-level contrasts with coordinates and cluster-level statistics, and includes a healthy adult sample (n=40 heterosexual males, mean age 25.8) with results reported for this healthy group. Whole-brain results are described in the text and coordinates are provided (supplementary tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article is complete for screening purposes. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (self- and mother-judgments) in healthy adult participants (Chinese college students, n=34 analyzed, ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses (self- vs celebrity and mother- vs celebrity contrasts), with group-level results described in the text and reported in Tables 2 and 3 (coordinate-based whole-brain activations and thresholding details). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. There are no ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-range, or non-empirical exclusion issues. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates social processing (in-group vs out-group action perception). fMRI was performed during a social/affiliation task (action–judgment and passive viewing) meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adult volunteers (ages reported 17–43, mean >21) and analyses report group-level results for the healthy sample, meeting I4 (majority are adults within 18–65 and results reported at the group level). Whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects contrasts are reported (single-video and paired-trial contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and tabulated/figured results, satisfying I5 and I6. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

The study satisfies I3 (uses fMRI during a social task — multi-round trust game) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–50, with control-group results reported). However, it does not provide an unmasked, within-group or main-effect whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain voxelwise results reported are exploratory between-group contrasts (control > patient) with peak coordinates. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map) is not met, and exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect) applies. ROI analyses are present but do not satisfy the whole-brain requirement. Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E4; I3 and I4 were met, I5 not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of laughter perception involving social-evaluative processing (explicit laughter type categorization vs. implicit counting), which directly addresses social communication/social perception constructs. The sample comprises 18 healthy adults (mean age 26), satisfying the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (multiple contrasts such as CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and presents tables/figures of whole-brain results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only-connectivity-only results, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within age range, and this is an empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion recognition in healthy adults (meets I3: task is social perception/understanding of others; and I4: sample are healthy adults 18–65). However, the paper’s whole-brain results are reported only as between-group contrasts (LDA > HDA and HDA > LDA). The manuscript does not report an unmasked, within-group or overall healthy-group whole-brain task activation map (e.g., main effect of task or within-group Emo_Emo > Neu_Age) clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no within-group/healthy-group whole-brain map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used fMRI with a social-perception task (satisfies I3) and included a healthy adult control group with separate analyses (satisfies I4). However, the paper reports only background/intrinsic seed-based functional interaction (connectivity) analyses and does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (seed-based/resting-like connectivity analyses only, without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). fulltext contains methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults investigating social-reputation processing (a social-related task). The sample consists of 28 healthy young adults (14M/14F; mean age 21.1), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (contrasts, thresholding at voxel p<0.001 and cluster-level FWE p<0.05) and provides tables/figures of activation (e.g., Table 1, Fig.3). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=10 males, age 22–32) that investigates neural responses to social interactions using point-light biological motion stimuli. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., (atypical upright + atypical inverted) − (typical upright + typical inverted)), with multiple-comparisons correction and tables/coordinates of activated clusters. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria: use of fMRI during a social-related task (I3), healthy adult sample reported separately (I4), and whole-brain group-level task-evoked results provided (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study (Spunt & Lieberman, 2013) used task-based functional MRI during social-cognitive action observation (why/how task) addressing perception and understanding of others. This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based functional MRI to examine social-related processing (viewing and evaluating political candidates’ faces) and associated emotional/cognitive responses, satisfying I3. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (causal attributions/self-responsibility and self-serving bias) in healthy adults. Methods: fMRI task-based attribution paradigms with healthy right-handed male volunteers (n=12; ages 20–51). Results: group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported (fixed-effects analyses with voxelwise correction, tables of peak coordinates and figures for internal vs external attributions and self-serving vs non-self-serving contrasts), with additional random-effects ROI checks. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and figures/tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a virtual-reality social cognition task (face-to-face attribution using avatars) and reported task-evoked, whole-brain, group-level activation maps. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a social-related task (affiliative vs nonaffiliative social scenarios). The sample consists of healthy adults (final N=27, mean age ~27), and analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with SPM8 reporting FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures. The study used task-based fMRI of social processing (viewing emotional faces) and includes a healthy adult control group (TD; mean age ~29.7), satisfying I3 and I4. This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (pseudo-interactive joke task) examining self/other effects and action-outcome contingency in healthy adults. The sample comprises 38 healthy adults aged 19–29. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., SELF vs OTHER; Group vs No laughter; interaction effects) with SPM thresholds and FWE cluster correction, and presents coordinate tables and figures of activation (including ventral striatum, mPFC, auditory cortex). Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study directly investigates social processing (mutual/direct vs averted gaze) using a virtual-reality task (meets I3). The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=16) reported separately from the PTSD group (meets I4). Results are presented in whole-brain tables/figures and ROI analyses complement them (meets I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: audiovisual integration of non-verbal emotional signals / social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample: n=24, ages 18–41). However, it violates exclusion criterion E2: the reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI)-based along individually mapped STS measuring points and the results are presented as contrast estimates for these ROIs (MPs). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI of social-related processing (maternal response to child affect) and reports whole-brain task-evoked results with coordinates/tables, so it satisfies I3, I5, and I6. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I4 not met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social/emotional perception (viewing fearful vs. neutral body gestures), includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=12), and provides group-level whole-brain activation analyses and contrasts (conjunctions, between-group comparisons, tables of coordinates and thresholded maps) for the control group. The methods, results, and connectivity analyses are fully reported in the provided full text. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathic decision-making (social processing: perception/understanding of others) in healthy adult participants (N=32, mean age 22.8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study uses a social-related task (viewing angry/neutral faces) in healthy adults (I3, I4 satisfied), it does not report a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. The paper reports ROI analyses (FFA and amygdala percent signal change) and seed-based PPI whole-brain connectivity results (sex-by-stress interactions), but no unmasked, voxelwise healthy-group task activation contrast (e.g., faces>fixation) is presented. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (seed-based connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports primarily between-group/interactions without an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). The study uses event-related fMRI during evaluative judgments tied to social cognition/theory-of-mind processes (meets I3). This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction involving reactive aggression using a competitive reaction-time task in healthy adult participants (mean age 28.6). All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, age outside 18–65, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study explicitly investigating perception of socially relevant facial expressions (social communication/perception of others). The study uses task-based fMRI during perception of biological motion, which is a social-related processing task (perception/understanding of others). This empirical fMRI study used a task where healthy adult participants viewed funny vs non-funny cartoons (social-communication/relevant social processing domain: humor appreciation), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (regression of STCI cheerfulness with BOLD) with stereotactic coordinates and statistics. This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (charitable giving) involving social cognition (empathy, perspective-taking). It tested healthy adult participants (n=22, ages 19–38). This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural responses to communicative vs noncommunicative vocal sounds (a social-communication paradigm). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (college students) that uses a social-related task probing the mirror neuron system via observation of goal-directed hand actions (relevant to 'Perception and Understanding of Others'). This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (recognition of ‘vitality forms’) in healthy adults. Sample: 19 healthy adults (ages 21–29) meeting the adult age criterion. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=12, mean age 29.4) that used a social-related task (viewing goal-directed vs non-goal-directed biological motion to probe perception/understanding of others’ actions/intentions). This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (effects of empathic social responses) in healthy adults. This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (self-referential moral processing during intergroup competition), conducted in healthy adults (N=21, mean age ~23). This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 19.1), using task-evoked BOLD during social-related tasks. This study reports an fMRI experiment examining cooperation vs. competition (a social-related task). Participants were healthy adults (N=12; ages 21–28). This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing using live bidirectional conversation (human–human vs human–robot), performed in healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 25.8). This fMRI study investigates social-related processing (matching emotional faces/scenes) in healthy adult participants (15 males, mean age 26.7), using task-evoked BOLD responses. This study reports an event-related fMRI task probing social interaction (SI) recognition using point-light displays (social-related processing), includes a healthy adult group (n=16, ages 20–41), and presents group-level whole-brain task contrasts (SI > NM) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster/FWE-corrected results for the adult group. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a video-based Theory of Mind (social cognition) task (MASC) in healthy adult participants (N=18; ages 20–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (GLM results with cluster thresholds, tables of coordinates, and figures) and also presents model-free T-PICA components; whole-brain results are clearly described for the healthy sample. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (face perception/attention), so I3 is satisfied. However, the sample consists solely of chronic traumatic brain injury (TBI) participants (no healthy adult control group reported separately), so it fails I4 (no healthy adult group reported). Consequently, there are no healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps to include, so I5 is not met. The provided full text is complete. No listed exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met. Therefore the study must be excluded because it does not meet required inclusion criteria I4 and I5.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on available content: Inclusion met: I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related task—emotion inference about others). Inclusion not verifiable / thus not met: I4 (sample age 18–65 and clear healthy adult group reported separately is not specified in abstract), I5 (paper must report at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for healthy group — abstract reports brain regions but does not confirm whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps or provide coordinates/tables). Because key inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be confirmed from the truncated content, the study is excluded pending full-text inspection.

The paper reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (perception/discrimination of affective vocalisations across species), with healthy adult participants (N=19, ages within 18–65). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task results (a species contrast human > chimpanzee > macaque) with MNI coordinates and associated figures/tables, and describes methods, results and discussion in full. Acoustic and arousal covariates were included and whole-brain mixed-effects group analyses (FLAME) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses fMRI during a social-related task (social phobia-related word processing) (I3 met), the fMRI analyses and reported whole-brain statistical maps are restricted to a patient subsample (N=25) and focus on amygdala ROI correlations with methylation. The paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map for a healthy/control group, nor separate healthy-group whole-brain results. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E2 (only ROI results/no whole-brain results) and E4 (no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect; only patient-group analyses and correlations reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no healthy-group fMRI results reported separately), I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain map), I6 (not applicable). Thus the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on healthy-group whole-brain fMRI task activation.

This full-text reports an fMRI social judgment task (Social > Perceptual Judgment) in healthy adults and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected cluster table and coordinates) clearly from the healthy sample. Participants were healthy adults aged 21–43. Whole-brain activation maps/coordinates are reported in Table 1 and figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside 18–65, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study of implicit facial emotion processing (a social perception/communication task), reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and contrasts for healthy adult controls separately. The methods and results detail within-group activation maps (e.g., face vs fixation, intensity trends) and group activation figures/tables for controls, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The healthy control sample is adult (mean age 27) and reported separately. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study is an fMRI task study of emotional face processing (meets I3) but includes only patients with bipolar disorder (no healthy adult control group reported), so it does not meet the required sample criterion (I4). It also does not provide a whole-brain task activation map for a healthy/control group (I5 not met). This paper reports between-group contrasts within a clinical sample (EPO vs saline) without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect, so exclusion criterion E4 applies. Additionally, the provided full text appears incomplete (abstract/metadata only).

Full text incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study appears to be an fMRI investigation of social communication in a second language, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is met. However, key information cannot be verified from the provided content: participant ages (required for I4: healthy adults 18–65) are not reported, and it is not possible to confirm that at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map is reported (I5). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Because the full text is not available to confirm I4 and I5, I exclude this record pending retrieval of the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study of third-party punishment, a social cognition task involving evaluation/understanding of others (meets I3). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 26) within 18–65 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation results (Decision Phase: Experimental > Control; q(FDR)<0.05) and parametric whole-brain analyses, with coordinates and thresholding described (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain task activations are reported (not ROI-only), the study is not limited to connectivity-only analyses, includes healthy adults, and is original empirical work. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self- vs other-referential processing) using the Visual–Verbal Self-Other Referential Processing Task, satisfying the review’s scope. Sample: 20 healthy adult women (ages 18–52) are reported and analyzed separately, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked results are reported (SPM8 preprocessing, group contrasts, tables of clusters, and voxelwise statistical maps/figures), satisfying the whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it's empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This empirical fMRI study uses a social task (ultimatum game) with healthy adult participants (young adult group, ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (one-sample t-tests and full-factorial ANOVAs; maps thresholded and regions reported in figures and Table 1) clearly identified for the healthy adult group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study used simultaneous PET-fMRI in mothers viewing films of infants and reports resting-state (intrinsic) connectivity and PET-derived dopamine responses related to bonding. Inclusion: I3 (uses fMRI in a social/affiliation context) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 21–42) are met. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation map (own-infant vs unfamiliar-infant) from the healthy group; fMRI results focus on resting-state/seed-based intrinsic connectivity analyses and ROI-based PET analyses. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only seed-based/resting-state connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: audiovisual speech perception/social communication) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=15, ages within 18–65). However, it does not report a whole-brain, group-level task activation map that is explicitly and unambiguously identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone. The reported whole-brain results are a main effect of congruency across groups and group-by-congruency interaction/between-group contrasts; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task map (or control-only contrast) is presented. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (bystander effect; witnessing an emergency) using a task during MRI and examines neural responses to group size. Sample: healthy adult participants aged 18–27 (N=17, one excluded), meeting the healthy adult criterion. The analyses include single-subject GLMs and a group-level random-effects whole-brain GLM with parametric contrasts; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps and summarized in tables/figures (Tables 1–3, Figs), not ROI-only. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) The fMRI task involves observation and execution of hand gestures (observation of others’ actions), which falls under Perception and Understanding of Others; (I4) Sample comprises 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 24); (I5) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain analysis reported at p<0.001 uncorrected with peak coordinates and rendered SPMs) clearly from the healthy group; (I6) Whole-brain results are presented as peak coordinates and figures and described in text. Full text is complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social gaze processing in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (amygdala and inferior occipital gyrus) and does not present any unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or results. All reported significant findings are from ROI-constrained analyses (FWE-corrected within ROIs). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Exclusion criterion E2 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4): it uses task fMRI probing theory-of-mind and reports data from healthy adult participants. However, the manuscript presents ROI-based MVPA results and does not clearly report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group in the provided full text. The methods describe individually defined ROIs (first-level localizer) and ROI-based classification tests, consistent with ROI-only analyses. Because the paper does not clearly provide a whole-brain, group-level task activation map (voxelwise results) as required, it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Therefore it must be excluded for failing inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (not truncated).

The full text describes an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (understanding others’ emotions) using 22 healthy adult participants (ages 19–32), meeting the review objective. The task is clearly social (perception and understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (How>Why, Why>How, Why>Fixation) with statistical thresholding (FDR) and tables/coordinates, and includes figures and detailed methods/results, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The sample falls within the 18–65 range and analyses are reported for the healthy group. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task maps, between-group-only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social-related task (perception of biological motion), reporting group-level whole-brain analyses and results (significant cluster in right pSTS correlated with social-network diversity). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 20) who performed social-related tasks (inferring preferences and categorical age judgments). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (random-effects analyses), with coordinates, cluster sizes, figures and tables of activations (mPFC and other regions). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adult within-range sample, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI experiment probing social cognition (linking person perception and person knowledge) using task-based imaging; healthy adult sample (N=21, mean age 24.6, within 18–65) is reported; the paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (univariate contrasts and tables of coordinates, thresholding, and figures) clearly identified for the healthy/control group. Qualifying whole-brain results are reported in text, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task map, non-healthy age groups, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (26 American, 26 Chinese, 26 Iranian; ages within 18–65) who read social narratives and made judgments about protagonists’ values—constituting a social-related task (perception/understanding of others, moral cognition). The Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses and group-level contrasts (e.g., stories vs rest, protected-values vs non-protected) with cluster correction; results are reported as whole-brain effects in the main text and figures. Thus it meets I3 (social task), I4 (healthy adults), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This record is a non-empirical review article (Japanese) and presents an overview of social neuroscience topics rather than original fMRI data. Only abstract/metadata are provided here; no methods, participants, or results reporting original healthy-adult fMRI experiments are present. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no reported fMRI during a social-related task on original data), I4 (no reported sample of healthy adult participants with separate results), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I6 (no whole-brain results reported). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata/review content available), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (social addressment) in healthy adults, meeting the review objective. Sample: 37 healthy adult participants (mean age 25, range 20–39) — satisfies age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (main effects and interactions) with MNI coordinates, cluster thresholds, conjunction and interaction analyses — satisfying whole-brain evidence and reporting of coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study investigates supramodal representation of facial and vocal emotions (social communication/perception), using a whole-brain task-based fMRI design in healthy adults. Sample: 24 healthy right-handed adults age 18–34 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM results with FDR-corrected statistical maps and coordinate tables (meets whole-brain reporting). The task is social-emotional (integration of facial and prosodic emotions), satisfying the review’s social-related construct. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

Full text is incomplete (only title/metadata and empty body provided). Cannot verify inclusion criteria: I3 (whether the study used fMRI during a social-related task) not verifiable; I4 (whether a healthy adult group 18–65 was included and reported separately) not verifiable; I5 (whether at least one group-level whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked map is reported) not verifiable; I6 cannot be assessed. No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 can be confirmed from the available content. Therefore the study is excluded due to incomplete full text preventing assessment of required inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of self- and other-referential (social) processing in healthy adults (N=18, ages 19–29), meeting the review focus. The methods report group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM8) with results shown for whole-brain contrasts ( Tables 2–3; whole-brain FWE-corrected activations reported outside mPFC) and an mPFC small-volume ROI—thus providing whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (Theory-of-Mind contrast: TOM vs Random), satisfying social-related task requirement. Sample comprises 787 healthy adult participants (ages 22–>35) with HCP exclusion criteria, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The authors present group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (Cohen's d group maps and level-3 z maps), cluster tables, and figures showing activation and coordinates, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Supplementary material references and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants (N=41 healthy adults, ages 18–24) underwent BOLD fMRI while making decisions about selecting and sharing news articles (social communication/sharing, self- and other-related processing). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (select > content, share > content, share > select) with a corrected threshold (p < .05, k > 20) and provides tables/figures describing these results. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met. The full text content provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplemental material referenced but not required).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction perception, with healthy adult participants (N=14, ages 20–32). It includes group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (with coordinates and maps reported) demonstrating activation to social interaction contrasts. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social tasks (take-advice game and trust game) probing trustworthiness/honesty—clearly social cognition. Sample: 31 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.3), no neurological/psychiatric disorders. The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked results (searchlight MVPA, whole-brain univariate contrasts, cluster-level FWE corrections, coordinates, figures and tables) attributable to the healthy group. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, refs) is present. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The review objective is fMRI studies of social-related processing. Although this study uses fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (satisfying I4, I5, I6), the experimental task is isolated word/pseudoword repetition in the scanner without social interaction or social-communication context. The stimuli and contrasts target speech production, motor and memory processes rather than social-affiliation, interpersonal communication, or perception/understanding of others; therefore it does not meet I3 (fMRI during a social-related task). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using task-based sounds (footsteps) to probe social auditory perception and social cognition (mentalizing, socio-emotional processing), meeting the review’s focus on social-related processing (I3). The sample consists of 12 healthy adults aged 22–37, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and statistical maps/coordinates (contrasts such as STEP1+STEP2 – REST, STEP2 – NOISE2, tables of Talairach coordinates, and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of communicative (social) speech production in healthy adult participants (N=30; ages 19–31). Tasks explicitly target social communication (communicative vs. descriptive speech) and analyses used whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 group-level contrasts (reported in figures/tables with coordinates and cluster-level inference). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain group maps/coordinate tables are clearly reported for the healthy sample. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

The article reports task-based fMRI during a social perceptual/mentalizing task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes), with healthy adult participants (native Japanese and white American groups, ages 18–27) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (RME − GD) with coordinates and corrected statistics. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range-only samples) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-affective processing (viewing film clips of people in distress and using Compassion meditation/Reappraisal) in healthy adult participants (age range 45–62; n=15 long-term meditators). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Compassion > Watch-Negative; Reappraisal > Watch-Negative) with cluster-level FWE correction and detailed whole-brain results described in text, figures and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (cyberball) with healthy adult controls (20 female HCs) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial and two-sample t-tests) and cluster-level results. The paper provides within-group post hoc comparisons for the HC group and refers to t-contrasts in the Supplementary Data, and reports coordinates/clusters in the main text/tables, meeting the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked results. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social attribution (why/how task) in healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 21–46). It includes group-level whole-brain analyses (t-statistic images, conjunctions, cluster-corrected results) and reports clusters/tables from these voxelwise contrasts. The social task and contrasts directly address social processing, and whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and tables. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social working memory task (social trait ranking) in healthy adult participants (N=16, mean age 20). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric modulation by social load) with thresholding and figures/tables of activations, and links activation to trait perspective-taking. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state-only; not between-group-only; participants are within age range; paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing using an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma task (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–22 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters, VTA attenuation in women) and applies whole-brain thresholds and ROIs derived from those maps (meets I5). Whole-brain results are described in text and figures and supplementary analyses are reported (meets I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social interactive task (sequential Prisoner's Dilemma) to probe social/moral evaluation of others, meeting the review objective. Participants were healthy adults (mean age 25.6; n_scanned = 11) and results for the healthy group are reported separately. Group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported with tables of coordinates and described whole-brain contrasts (effects reported in ROIs and descriptively elsewhere), satisfying whole-brain task-evoked reporting. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not include a healthy adult group nor a social-related fMRI task. It reports fMRI activation and connectivity in patients with early-course schizophrenia (and schizoaffective disorder) performing a cognitive control (POP) task—not a social-processing task—so inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) are not met. Although whole-brain task activation and connectivity are reported, these are for the patient groups only; there are no group-level, whole-brain task maps reported for a healthy/control group, violating I5 and meeting exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group/patient results without a healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in adult mothers viewing own vs other child photographs and child behavior stimuli—clearly social/attachment-related processing. Participants are adult mothers (within typical adult age range), and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (voxel-by-voxel multiple regression, random-effects group analyses; coordinates and figures provided). Results for the (healthy) adult mother group are described directly in the text and figures/tables. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Although the sample is small and selective, none of the exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (explicit and implicit processing of emotional facial expressions), including a healthy adult control group (n=9, mean age 27±7). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (FPQ maps, ANOVA of voxel-wide BOLD signal changes) and describes control-group activations and contrasts (main effects and diagnosis × experiment interactions) in the text, tables, and figures (e.g., regions activated in controls such as left cerebellum and left amygdalohippocampal region). The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, healthy adults included, empirical with original fMRI data).

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social-related task (participants imagined encountering neutral faces in goal-relevant vs. goal-irrelevant social situations) and examines neural responses during encoding and recognition. Sample: healthy adults aged 20–36 (n=17 analyzed), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement.
