Whole-brain, group-level, task-evoked analyses are reported (random-effects second-level ANOVAs, voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction), with tables/figures of activations and coordinates; parametric modulator analyses and small-volume corrections are additionally described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

The article is a Personal View/review (non-empirical) and the provided full text is limited to abstract/metadata (no methods or results). It does not report original fMRI data from healthy adults, nor any group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (non-empirical paper). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (no fMRI during a social-related task reported), I4 (no healthy adult group data reported separately), I5 (no whole-brain group-level task activation maps), I6 (no reporting of whole-brain results in any format). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (perception of social interactions and crowd emotions) using a task involving viewing dynamic crowds, satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=16; ages 19–27), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVAs, cluster tables, whole-brain figures and coordinates) clearly from the healthy sample, satisfying I5 and the acceptable reporting formats in I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results (with whole-brain statistics and figures), and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

The study reports an fMRI task probing theory-of-mind/social understanding (social-related processing) with both patients and a healthy control group. It includes a healthy adult control sample (n=12, mean age 24.8) and reports within-group (healthy controls) whole-brain, group-level activation results (ANOVA, contrasts PInt/PSInt/CInt vs Ph-C) with coordinates and figures/tables. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholding are described; results for the healthy group are clearly presented (tables/figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or age outside range) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related visual processing (two-body facing vs nonfacing configurations), with functional MRI collected in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 24.1). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., dyads > single bodies; facing > nonfacing dyads) with statistical maps and cluster-level correction, and describes ROI and MVPA analyses. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of emotional prosody in voices, clearly addressing social communication/social-cognition (anger prosody) and attentional modulation, matching the review objective. Sample: 15 healthy right-handed adult participants (mean age 24.4), so a healthy adult group within 18–65 is reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 second-level random-effects t-tests, contrasts, cluster-level correction) with coordinates and figures/tables of activations (amygdala, STS, OFC, cuneus), fulfilling whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mental state inference/prediction) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–22). The task is social (mentalizing about others' states) and was performed during fMRI (I3). The sample consists of healthy adults within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight representational similarity analysis and voxelwise repetition-suppression analyses) with corrected inference and peak MNI coordinates (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (facial emotion recognition) targeting social perception/understanding (I3). The sample comprises 116 healthy adult men (mean age 24.7), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (e.g., FWE-corrected voxelwise statistics, reported clusters and MNI coordinates, and a whole-brain regression), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Results and coordinates are clearly described in the text and figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only or resting-state-only analyses, includes an appropriate healthy adult group, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports event-related fMRI during perception of emotional facial expressions (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others) in 14 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 29±6). The abstract states statistical parametric mapping identified activation in dorsal medial frontal cortex (pre-SMA), indicating group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 appear satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. However, only the abstract and metadata are provided here (no full methods/results sections), so the full text is incomplete and I cannot fully verify details (e.g., that whole-brain maps are reported unmasked and come from the healthy/control group). Fulltext_incomplete set to true to reflect this uncertainty.

The article reports an fMRI study of social learning (participants learned about others’ generosity), satisfying the review objective. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (initial N=30, final analyzed N=26; ages 19–37), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and parametric analyses (e.g., Gifter vs Lottery contrasts, SPE parametric maps), with voxel-wise thresholds and cluster correction; results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (sighted control group mean age ~32) that examines perception and understanding of others (voice identity and emotion), satisfying the review’s domain of social-related processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (univariate and searchlight MVPA) and provides cluster tables and brain maps; the text explicitly states the reported patterns were present in both blind and sighted groups when considered in isolation, and multiple whole-brain contrasts and coordinates are presented (Tables and Figures). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a theoretical/review-style paper (abstract only provided) discussing explanations of mirror-touch synesthesia and summarizing fMRI evidence; it does not present original fMRI task data from healthy adults or report group-level whole-brain statistical maps. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task reported), I4 (no report of a healthy adult participant group with task results), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results in text/tables/figures). Additionally, the provided full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata). Thus the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 25–49) that examines social-related processing (emotional sharing, empathy, perception/understanding of others) using a movie-viewing task. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (intersubject correlation maps, voxelwise GLMs linking valence/arousal to ISC, permutation testing with FDR correction) and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses task-based fMRI to investigate action observation, intention-reading and social cognition (simulation vs. evaluation of an actor’s toolmaking), which falls under Perception and Understanding of Others (social-related processing). Participants are healthy adults (Naïve n=11, Trained n=10, Expert n=5; right-handed; no neurological illness). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Toolmaking–Control, Acheulean–Oldowan) analyzed with SPM8, thresholded and reported with coordinates and figures, clearly attributable to the healthy groups. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of humor processing, which the authors frame as a social-related phenomenon (addresses social cognition/understanding aspects of humor and ToM). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=29, mean age 27), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (e.g., cartoons vs. neutral, parametric modulation) with coordinates and corrected statistical thresholds. Results for the healthy participants are reported separately and conform to whole-brain reporting standards. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy task effects, empirical fMRI data in adults). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete for screening purposes.

This fMRI study uses a social decision task and includes a healthy adult group (ages 21–22), so it meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) and I4 (contains a healthy adult sample). However, the paper’s whole-brain voxelwise results are reported for the combined sample (n=60) and via between-group contrasts (Young adults > Adolescents). The manuscript does not present an unmasked, within-group whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/adult group alone. Therefore it appears to report only between-group contrasts for adults rather than an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criterion I5 (a clearly identified group-level whole-brain map from the healthy adult group) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24, ages 22–39) investigating how collective/social schemas (collective memory) are represented during memory recall. The task engages social-related processing (collective/social knowledge, narrative comprehension, theory-of-mind-related dmPFC activity), meeting the review’s social-related task criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain searchlight analyses with TFCE-corrected results and ROI analyses, providing whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group. Full text including introduction, methods, results and discussion is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears to be an abstract-level summary and lacks key methodological details. I3 (fMRI during social-related task) is met: the study used fMRI to examine action recognition (perception/understanding of others). I4 (healthy adult sample ages 18–65) cannot be confirmed because participant ages and sample details are not provided. I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps) cannot be confirmed from the provided text; while regions are reported, it is unclear whether these derive from whole-brain voxelwise analyses or ROI analyses. Therefore not all inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study cannot be confidently included. fulltext_incomplete=true because core article content (methods, participant demographics, and full results) is missing or truncated.

This is an empirical fMRI study directly investigating simulation of others’ decision-making (a social-cognitive task) using task-based fMRI. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (36 analyzed; informed consent and ethical approval reported). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected cluster-level results and tables of coordinates (Tables 1 and 2) and figures, clearly described as coming from the healthy/control group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study probing perception/understanding of others' actions (auditory mirror system; semantic processing of heard actions), which falls under social-related processing. The fMRI subgroup comprises healthy adults (n=11, ages 21–29). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM5) with cluster-corrected maps and tables/figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an event-related fMRI study of social cognition (mind perception and gaze-cueing), tested in healthy adult participants (N=22, mean age 24.4). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (parametric whole-brain analyses with cluster correction, tables/coordinates and figures showing vmPFC, TPJ, fusiform, etc.). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply.

The full text reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 24.6) who viewed realistic first-person social interaction videos (reactive–aggressive, social-positive, neutral), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (contrasts with FDR-corrected thresholds, cluster info, and Talairach coordinates in tables and figures), meeting the whole-brain evidence reporting requirement. Results for the healthy group are presented directly. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion, indicating a complete full text. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI to measure social-related processing (empathy/perception of others for human and robot agents). (I4) The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–27, with results reported for this healthy group. (I5) The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses (including cluster-corrected results) and provides whole-brain group contrast maps (NeuroVault). (I6) Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text, figures, tables, and supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes healthy adult task activations, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (n=14, mean age ~25) performing observation and motor imagery of meaningful face and upper-limb movements, including socially meaningful gestures—this maps onto social communication/social-processing constructs. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM2 ANOVA) with voxelwise FWE-corrected results, figures, and coordinate tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used task-based fMRI of facial expression perception — a social communication/perception task — in healthy adult participants (n=24, mean age 25.2), meeting the sample and task requirements. The authors performed group-level mixed-effects analyses (FLAME) generating parameter-estimate maps for each expression and describe group statistical maps (faces > scrambled faces) that were spatially normalised to MNI; these constitute whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps. Results are clearly described and include group-level contrasts used to define ROIs and to register maps to MNI space. Analyses and reporting include methods and results (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-healthy sample) were met.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (communicative vs private intentions) in healthy adults (n=23, mean age 24). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt, interaction effects) with voxel coordinates and tables, and describes PPI connectivity as secondary analyses. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables and described in text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults. It uses simultaneous fMRI during an interactive communicative task (meets I3), recruited 54 healthy adult participants aged 18–27 (meets I4), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level inference and task-evoked effects (meets I5/I6). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of attachment-related social processing: mothers listened to their own infant’s cry (social/attachment stimulus). Participants are adult mothers (mean age 24.1), currently without diagnosable psychopathology, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts (own cry > control; own > other) with cluster-thresholding, tables of coordinates, and figures—meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Results for the (healthy) sample are clearly described. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Note: some mothers had a perinatal history of depression but none met criteria at time of scanning; authors report analyses controlling for depressive symptoms and retain full sample. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes / age-judgement variants) and reports task-evoked whole-brain activation results. The paper includes a healthy adult control group (n=25; age range 18–59) with results for controls described (healthy-control activations reported; Supplementary Tables S2 and S3) and whole-brain FWE-corrected analyses with thresholds specified. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain group-level reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports an fMRI study of social processes (empathy, perspective taking, attention) during a charitable donation task and complementary EmpaToM and attention tasks, satisfying the review topic. Sample: healthy adults (n=33, age 20–34), meeting the adult age range. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight MVPA, GLMs, group random-effects tests) with FWE-corrected voxel-level results and tables/coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, healthy adult group reported separately).

This is an empirical fMRI study that collected task-based fMRI during an explicit social-attitude (trust/distrust) control task. The sample is healthy adults (n=59–60; mean age ~20) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., trust>distrust, trust>age, distrust>age) with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures describing whole-brain results. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study tests social vs non-social reading passages and reports group-level whole-brain contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (N=26, ages 19–26). Whole-brain random-effects contrasts (Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) are reported with cluster-correction and peak coordinates (Table 1 and figures). The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others via Theory of Mind/moral judgment), satisfying I3. Sample meets I4. Whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported, satisfying I5 and I6. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study analyzes a social cognition task (social interaction vs random movement) using task fMRI and reports group-level voxel-wise activation analyses and maps (voxel-wise GLM and Figures/ROI activation results), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Samples are healthy adult participants from HCP and UCLA (ages 21–50 and 22–36 within 18–65). The paper includes whole-text methods, results, and figures describing group-level whole-brain task-evoked activations for the healthy samples. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) The task is social mentalizing (inferring others’ preferences/mental states) using fMRI; (I4) Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=64, ages 18–26); (I5) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (parametric modulation of BOLD by self–other discrepancy) with peak coordinates and cluster tables; (I6) Whole-brain results are reported clearly in text, figures, and Table 1. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/resting-state, and include a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of task-evoked social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, mean age 35.9) that used a social competition task contrasting human–human vs human–machine interaction to probe Theory of Mind and executive processes. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5) including contrasts (main effects and interactions), statistical thresholds, and tables/figures of activation coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, statistical analysis), Results (behavioral and fMRI results, tables), Discussion, and references. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (I5), and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI hyperscanning study of social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention), meeting the review objective of social-related processing. It reports data from healthy adult participants (mean ages 20–23, N reported) within the 18–65 range. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-level FWE-corrected maps, tables of coordinates, contrasts such as MG2–MG1, IJA, RJA) and describes task-evoked activations and inter-individual synchronization analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task maps, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The study meets inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses fMRI during social-related tasks (social distance trials comparing friends vs acquaintances); (I4) sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=15, ages 20–28); (I5) it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps from searchlight MVPA and RSA analyses (significant clusters reported and shown in figures/tables); (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. The full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Although conventional univariate contrasts yielded no significant voxels, the MVPA/RSA whole-brain group maps satisfy the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion met: E6 - article is labeled as a review ('REVISIÓN') and does not present original fMRI data in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: none (no evidence of I3, I4, I5, or I6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task reported), I4 (no healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps from healthy participants), I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results described). Full text appears incomplete (only metadata/label provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Princeton undergraduates, mean age 19.5) that uses task-based fMRI during social-cognition judgments (viewing social-group photographs and rating emotions), addressing perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and contrasts (subtractive and 3-vs-1), and lists activation peaks (mPFC, insula, amygdala). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the primary content inclusion criterion for this review: it investigates auditory attention and motion detection of human footsteps (an auditory-directed task) rather than social-related processing (e.g., affiliation, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 20–29), I5 (group-level whole-brain task contrast 'footstep minus rest' reported using random-effects SPM analysis), and I6 (whole-brain results reported and referenced in supplementary material). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (task is not clearly a social-related task). No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This fMRI study investigates creativity in an affective context using a reappraisal generation task involving socially relevant, anger-eliciting scenarios (perception/understanding of others) and a classic divergent-thinking task. Sample: 45 healthy adult participants (ages 18–34). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (conjunction analysis and RGT>AUT, AUT>RGT contrasts) with voxelwise FWE correction and cluster thresholds; results are presented in tables/figures and correlated with performance. All required criteria are met: I3 (social-related task: reappraisal of others' behavior), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study examines theory-of-mind (implicit false-belief) processing — a social cognition task — using task-based fMRI and eye-tracking. Sample comprises healthy adults (mean age 22.7; analyses reported for healthy participants). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (explicit localizer belief>photo/map and implicit false>true belief SPMs) with peak coordinates and figures described in the text. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (i.e., full text appears complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study using a social cognition (Theory of Mind/mentalizing) task (visual jokes) — meets I3. The sample includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=13) reported alongside high-risk and patient groups — meets I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and within-group contrasts analyzed with SPM2; within-group activations for all groups (including controls) are reported in Table 3 and described in the Results — meets I5. Results are reported as whole-brain cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-only (E3), not limited to between-group contrasts without healthy-group task effects (E4), participants are adult (E5), and this is an empirical fMRI study (not E6). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables). Therefore include.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (direct and reflected self-appraisals; social cognition and perspective-taking), includes a healthy adult group (ages 22.6–30.4) with results reported separately, and presents group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (within-group contrasts and conjunctions for adults) with coordinates and figures. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and adult sample is within 18–65). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This manuscript is a narrative review summarizing the authors’ prior fMRI studies rather than an original empirical report presenting new group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy adults. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data in healthy adults) therefore applies. The paper does meet inclusion criteria I3 (discusses fMRI during social-related tasks) and I4 (describes/compares healthy adult participants in cited work), but it does not meet I5 (it does not report its own clearly identified group-level whole-brain task activation map for a healthy/control group). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-perception task (attending to facial emotion/age) (I3); tests a healthy adult sample aged 21–33 with results reported for the healthy group (I4); reports group-level whole-brain analyses (faces>objects random-effects localizer and whole-brain searchlight results with SnPM correction and tables/figures of clusters) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5); and whole-brain results are described in the text/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs only, not solely connectivity or resting-state, include within-group whole-brain task effects, participants are within the 18–65 range, and the article reports original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports an fMRI task probing social-related processing (compassion/empathy for others’ suffering) and tests effects on altruistic behavior, satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (age range 18–45) with results reported for the healthy groups, satisfying I4. The manuscript includes whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group-level analyses (Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC) and describes these maps in the text, satisfying I5 and I6. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present in the provided text; supplemental material is referenced but not required, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Thus the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=40 behavioral, N=34 fMRI; age range 19.5–32.7) using a social task (trust-game with eye/pupil stimuli) that probes social cognition (trust, theory-of-mind). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., pupil-mimicry > no mimicry; partner pupil change > static) with cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates, and refers to tables/figures/SI for activation maps and coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and detailed ROI and whole-brain analyses, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports only between-group contrasts (high-Mach > low-Mach) from whole-brain analyses and does not present an unmasked, within-group (healthy/control) whole-brain task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task — Trust Game), I4 (sample of healthy adult participants aged 19–30), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/coordinates). Inclusion criterion I5 is NOT met: no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain task effect reported for a healthy/control group (e.g., main effect or within-group contrast); reported results are contrasts between two healthy subgroups. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (cooperation/competition; self/other representations), meeting the review objective. Sample: healthy adults (n=24 after exclusions), ages 19–31, satisfying the adult age range. Whole-brain group-level task-evoked results are reported (family-wise error cluster-corrected whole-brain contrasts; Table 1 and whole-brain figures presented), and coordinates/contrasts are clearly described in text and figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods (including participants, task, imaging), results (behavioral and whole-brain fMRI), and discussion; supplemental materials are referenced but not required for main whole-brain results, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social communication-related processing (vitality forms in speech and action), meeting the review objective. Sample: 18 healthy adult participants (mean ages ~25–26), satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts and conjunctions (e.g., Vitality vs Control contrasts, conjunctions across tasks) with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results (tables/figures described), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Whole-brain results are clearly attributed to the healthy/control group. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Multifaceted Empathy Test) assessing cognitive and emotional empathy, satisfying I3. It includes a healthy adult control group (female, age-matched adults) reported separately, satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation results for the healthy/control group (main effects and tables of coordinates for cognitive and emotional empathy; see Tables 5 & 6 and figures), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain effects, participants within 18–65, and is empirical). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (reactive aggression provoked by human opponents) using a social interaction task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm). Participants were healthy adults (final N=15, mean age 22.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (multiple GLMs), with statistical maps/contrasts described and peak coordinates reported in Tables 1 and 2 and figures (thresholds reported). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

While this is an fMRI study with healthy adult participants (ages 20–36) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, the task does not target social-related processing as defined by the review. The experiment investigates hypnotic suggestion to induce and modulate pain (pain perception and cognitive control) rather than constructs such as affiliation, social communication, or perception/understanding of others or self in a social context. Although verbal suggestion is an interpersonal act, the study's aims, contrasts, and reported outcomes focus on pain circuitry and cognitive modulation rather than social cognition. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I6 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete for screening.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of person-knowledge retrieval (social cognition: perception/understanding of others). Samples are healthy adults (study 1: n=24, Mage=23.2; study 2: n=26, Mage=20.4), within 18–65. The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain univariate GLM results (e.g., “all memory > baseline”, voxel-level FWE-corrected P < 0.05) and reports coordinates/tables/figures of task activation maps. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3–I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 - participants are adolescents (three phases of adolescence) and no healthy adult (age 18-65) group is reported in the provided content. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 - the study used fMRI during a social-related task (Trust Game). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I4 - no healthy adult sample reported; I5 - cannot verify reporting of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map from the abstract; I6 - cannot confirm acceptable whole-brain result reporting. Additionally, the provided content appears to be only the abstract and references, so fulltext_incomplete=true (full text incomplete). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines abstract vs. concrete construal using Why-How and Categories-Exemplars tasks which engage social-cognitive processes (mentalizing/theory-of-mind) consistent with social-related processing (I3). Sample comprises 24 healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses with corrected significance thresholds and tables/figures of activations (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports an fMRI investigation of social exclusion (Cyberball), a social-related task (affiliation/belonging). Sample consists of healthy adults within the 18–65 range (n=20 analyzed). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports results with tables, coordinates, figures, and cluster thresholds (social exclusion vs fair play; contrasts by excluder gender), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This study meets the review objectives and inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during an explicit emotion-recognition paradigm (a social-related task) in healthy adult males (ages 21–33). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise (whole-slab) random-effects activation maps and statistical results (figures and coordinates are provided for voxelwise analyses, and whole-slab/ANOVA results and coordinates are reported), not limited to ROI-only results. Behavioral and neural results are reported for the healthy group separately. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=29, age range 18–28) that investigates representation of observed actions, a social-cognition-relevant process (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Observation > Neutral, Squeeze > No Squeeze, 2H DIFF > 2H SAME) with thresholded statistical maps, figures, and tables of peak MNI coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study reports an event-related fMRI experiment probing perception/understanding of others’ actions (social cognition) using a motion classification task (biological vs artificial). Participants are healthy adults (n=12, mean age 27.3), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 results thresholded with FDR correction, cluster tables and coordinates provided) and identifies regions correlated with behavioral measures; results are presented as standard whole-brain contrasts and tables. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical) apply. Hence the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

The study uses task fMRI of a social-cognitive visual perspective-taking task and reports results for a healthy adult control group (satisfies I3 and I4). However, the authors explicitly used an a priori combined region-of-interest mask and restricted analyzed voxels to that mask rather than performing/reporting a whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. Therefore the required whole-brain healthy-group task effect (I5) is not met, and the study reports only ROI-limited task results, triggering exclusion E2. Full text appears complete.

The study uses fMRI during tasks that include a social manipulation (peer observation during the Stoplight and Go/No-Go tasks), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 21–24 with exclusions for clinical/alcohol-use disorders, meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts (e.g., Risk>Safe, No-Go>Go) and provides thresholded and unthresholded maps via NeuroVault, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are presented in the main text and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Task) involving mental state recognition (I3). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=28) age-matched to patients, reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and describes within-group effects for controls (e.g., left MFG greater for mental state > age in controls), with whole-brain correction and results shown in tables/figures/supporting information (I5, I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (attributing awareness to others) in healthy adults. The methods and results report a group-level, whole-brain task contrast (H trials − E trials) with corrected thresholds and cluster coordinates (figures and Table 1), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=50; ages 18–49) with group results clearly described; thus sample inclusion is met. The paper provides introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full experimental details present), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This study is excluded because it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map for the healthy control group (exclusion E4). It does meet inclusion criteria I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task — cyberball social inclusion/exclusion) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=17, ages within 18–65). However, the full text presents primarily between-group contrasts (BPD > HC, NSSI > HC) and conjunction analyses; it does not present or describe a standalone whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given E4 is met, the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting I3 and I4.

Full text is paywalled/PDF-only and not accessible here, so core methods/results details cannot be verified. From the abstract the study uses task-based fMRI of emotional facial expressions (a social-related task) in a sample of healthy adults (n=12), which satisfies I3 and I4. However I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed from the available abstract/metadata. Because I5 cannot be verified and full text is incomplete, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded pending access to the full article. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are known to be met based on the available information.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotional prosody comprehension, a social-communication task (perception/understanding of others' emotional states). Participants: healthy adults (n=19, age range 18–51) within 18–65. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps and contrasts are reported (SPM8 analyses, corrected cluster maps, tables of coordinates and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of above criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical data present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (participants aged 19–42; N=16, 15 analyzed) that uses a social-perception task (gender perception from faces), which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (I3). The paper reports both ROI analyses and a voxel-wise whole-brain random-effects group analysis (contrast gender-different > gender-same) with reported cluster-corrected statistical maps (p<0.01), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Participants are healthy adults (I4). The whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures (I6). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical data present).

The study reports seed-based resting-state functional connectivity (left/right caudate nucleus) after listening to attachment narratives but does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from the healthy adult sample. Inclusion: I3 (fMRI study of social/attachment processing via narrative stimuli) and I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65) are met. Exclusion: E3 applies because only seed-based/resting-state connectivity analyses are reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Therefore I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met, and the paper must be excluded. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of empathy/social perception (perception of others' pain and perceived agency), addressing social-related processing. Sample: 26 healthy right-handed adult participants (mean age 24.4), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., (PCO+PCS)-(NPO+NPS) for pain main effect; social context contrasts; interaction contrast), thresholding and tables of coordinates (Tables 1–4) and figures, clearly identified as healthy-group results. Whole-brain results are reported and described in text and tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports unmasked healthy-group task effects). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, so is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From available content, the study uses fMRI with a social-related task (dynamic facial expression localizer), so I3 is met. However participant details and age range are not reported in the provided content, so I4 cannot be confirmed. The provided excerpt does not include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps or their descriptions, so I5 (and I6) cannot be confirmed. Because key inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]>). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met/unknown: I4, I5, I6. Full text incomplete=true.

This study is excluded because it does not investigate a social-related task (I3 not met). Although it includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (I4 met) and reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps for the control group (I5 met) presented in text/tables/figures (I6 met), the experimental paradigm is a monetary-reward continuous performance task (reward achievement), which does not target social processes (e.g., social communication, perception/understanding of others, affiliation). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (task addressing social-related processing). Therefore the paper does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test; affective Theory of Mind), satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (H; n=18) reported separately from clinical groups, satisfying I4. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses and state that single-group (one-sample t tests) contrast images were computed for each of the five groups; between-group and within-group (group-level) whole-brain results are described with cluster-level FWE correction and ROI SVC for the amygdala, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and sufficient for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an original task-based fMRI study that explicitly examines social cognition (social reasoning/theory-of-mind texts and videos), satisfying I3. The sample comprises 45 neurologically normal adult participants (ages 19–23), satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses including GLM, random-effects results, multiple-comparison-corrected statistical maps, and peak coordinates in Appendix A, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and appendices. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy task maps, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study is excluded because it reports resting-state fMRI connectivity analyses (MDMR) rather than task-evoked fMRI of social processing, so it meets exclusion criterion E3 (resting-state analyses only). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (contains a healthy adult comparison group; results reported for healthy participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task — study used resting-state fMRI), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group). Full text appears incomplete here (only abstract/highlights/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (Trust Game) in healthy adults (N=18 analyzed; ages 18–22), satisfying the sample criterion. The task is explicitly social (reciprocity/trust) and uses functional MRI during task performance. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and regression analyses with coordinates and tables (e.g., defect>reciprocate, regressions showing ACC, rTPJ, insula; MNI coordinates and AlphaSim correction), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed an interactive social rating task while one member was scanned. Healthy adult sample (students, mean age ~24) is reported and data are reported for the scanned healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (clusterwise FWE correction across the whole brain) with reported activations in tables/figures (e.g., Tables 2/3, Figures 3/4) and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=60, ages 18–60) that uses task-based fMRI during social-related stimuli (observation of mouth actions/communicative actions across species) addressing social perception/communication. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and between- and within-group contrasts (SPM analyses, FWE-corrected maps, tables and figures) clearly identified for the healthy groups (omnivores, vegetarians, vegans). Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because inclusion criterion I3 is not met: the fMRI paradigms used (verbal fluency and Hayling sentence completion) probe verbal executive function/response inhibition, not social-related processing. Inclusion criteria met: I4 — a healthy adult control group (mean age 27) is reported; I5 — the paper reports group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group activation maps for the healthy/control group; I6 — healthy-group whole-brain results are described in the text and shown in figures. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no social-related task). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based functional MRI study of social processing (self vs. close-other personality trait judgments and memory), in a healthy adult sample (N=13, ages 19.4–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM5, thresholded statistical maps, and tables of coordinates for contrasts (e.g., self>syllables, old/same>new) and similarity interactions. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This full-text reports an fMRI task probing social semantic judgments (social vs. animal function concepts), with healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 29.4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, whole-brain and ROI-corrected results) with tables of coordinates and figures, and explicitly attributes activations to the healthy/control group. The article includes complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and details of image acquisition and analysis. There are no exclusionary features (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (stereotype/social-category judgments) in healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 19–28). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (social > non-social and non-social > social) with multiple-comparison correction and region tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. It is empirical original fMRI data, not ROI-only or connectivity-only, and participants fall within the 18–65 range. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=27, mean age 27) using a social-perception task (viewing others' facial expressions) relevant to social communication and perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., canonical disgust vs neutral; canonical disgust vs distaste) with thresholding and tables of cluster coordinates (Table 2) and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (imaging acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task effects). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be included in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception), meeting the review focus on social-related processing (I3). Sample comprises healthy adults (ages 18–32) with results reported for the healthy group (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts with cluster thresholds and Talairach coordinates presented in tables and figures (I5,I6). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial decision-making) in healthy adult participants. Inclusion criteria met: I3 - the study uses task-based fMRI during mentalizing, empathy-for-pain, and prosocial tasks; I4 - sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=32, mean age 22.7); I5 - the paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain second-level contrasts (e.g., Mentalizing > baseline; Dissimilar > Similar) with cluster-level correction; I6 - whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This article reports an empirical fMRI study using a social task (collaborative vs competitive interactions) during effort production, with healthy adult participants (N=32, ages 18–39). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM random-effects, clusterwise FWE correction) with activation tables and figures/coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, includes within-group healthy adult whole-brain task activations). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and the study is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of facial emotion recognition (a social cognitive task) that includes a healthy adult control group (n=14) reported separately. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses: the Whole Brain Analysis section explicitly describes significant clusters for NT controls (NTOXT>PLA) and refers to a table of activated clusters, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text reports an empirical fMRI study using a social task (speed-dating paradigm) where healthy adult participants (scanned N=38; ages 19–31) viewed partners and learned romantic decisions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM8) with thresholding and tables/figures for contrasts (e.g., yes vs. no, Match vs. Unrequited, prediction-error correlates), satisfying requirements for whole-brain results. Core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a naturalistic social task (video-based mentalising) probing social cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=22, ages 19–46) reported separately, and presents whole-brain, voxelwise within-group task contrasts (ToM > physical inference) for the control group with cluster-corrected results reported in tables/figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text inaccessible (paywalled); only title, authors, and metadata available. Cannot verify that the study used task-based fMRI of social processing (I3), that it reports a separate healthy adult group aged 18–65 (I4), or that it presents whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results for the healthy/control group (I5/I6). Because the full text is incomplete, inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed and the study must be excluded from the review at this stage. No specific exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied based on the available information.

This is an fMRI study of empathy for pain (a social cognition/Perception and Understanding of Others task) in healthy adult participants (males aged 18–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (whole-brain FWE-corrected results for condition contrasts and group comparisons) and describes these results in the main text, figures and tables. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full; supplementary material is available. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI of action observation/perception of others (social cognition); (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (n=20, ages 20–34); (I5) reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (conjunctions and voxelwise contrasts, thresholded and reported across the whole brain) and peak coordinates/tables; (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text and reported as coordinates/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not limited to other age groups, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating emotional prosody (social communication) in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 24.8), meeting the review’s sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (emotional > neutral prosody) with cluster-corrected results described in text, tables, and figures (right STG cluster, Table 2, Figures 1–2), satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. The task is clearly social-related (social communication/perception of others’ emotion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion E2 met: the paper reports ROI-based (small volume correction) and a priori ROI analyses and presents results primarily within specified ROIs; there is no clear report of unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: dynamic facial expression processing) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages reported within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group) and consequently I6 (acceptable whole-brain results in tables/figures is not satisfied because reported coordinates derive from ROI/SVC analyses rather than an unmasked whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (why/how mentalizing vs sensorimotor aspects of actions) in healthy adults (ages 21–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (conjunctions and main effects), with cluster-extent correction and tables/figures of activation peaks and coordinates. The healthy/control group results are reported directly (no exclusive focus on clinical groups), and Study 2 reports ROI and whole-brain analyses replicating Study 1. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (Experiments: N=25, ages 19–27; N=14, ages 18–23). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extents, tables of regions/coordinates, and whole-brain multivariate searchlight results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social reciprocity using a Trust Game (task-based fMRI) in a healthy adult sample (age 18–30). Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results are reported (univariate contrasts with cluster-correction, tables of activated regions, and figures), and whole-brain ICA-derived network results are also provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM/ICA analyses), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social gaze/joint attention in healthy adults. The sample includes healthy adult participants within 18–65 (behavioural N=10, ages 18–41; fMRI N=12, ages 18–40). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2; contrasts such as gaze-shift vs no-movement and condition contrasts; tables/figures of activated loci are referenced), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Results are presented as group-level task activation maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study investigating mental state attribution (social cognition) using a task manipulating perceived agency (Composer vs Computer). Participants were healthy adults (analyzed N=12; ages 21–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Composer > Computer) with voxelwise coordinates, corrected cluster thresholds, tables and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (dynamic audio–visual emotion perception), meeting I3. The sample comprises healthy adults aged 18–33 (Study 1) and 18–23 (Study 2), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (multiple whole-brain contrasts, thresholds, and tables/figures of activations), satisfying I5 and I6. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and empirical fMRI data are presented). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study that manipulates social competition (a social-related task involving social comparison/mentalizing) and measures task-evoked brain activity. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (female, age 18–35). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses and contrasts (competition > no competition and within-condition performance-related effects) with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates described in text/figures/tables. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (nonverbal dyadic interactions) in healthy adults. It reports task-based fMRI with event-related design, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPM8), and presents voxelwise contrasts and coordinates for healthy participants (e.g., contingent vs mirrored, rigid vs smooth), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 23–33 (n=21 after exclusions). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=7, ages 20–35) that used task-based fMRI while participants read sentences that include social content. The analyses report group-level, voxelwise results (factor analysis identifying brain voxel clusters and group-level maps/figures and Supporting Information with cluster locations) and use these whole-brain regions for modeling and cross-participant predictions. Thus it meets: I3 (fMRI during social-relevant sentence processing), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results/clusters reported), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables/SI). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition, which falls under social-related processing (Perception/Understanding of Self). Participants were healthy adults (n=10, mean age 26.9), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self vs other; other vs self) with cluster-corrected thresholds and tables of MNI coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text includes methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Behavioral recording issues are noted but do not negate the reported whole-brain fMRI group results. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full text reports an fMRI study that directly contrasts social vs. non-social stimuli using a simple valence appraisal task (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adults (N=14 analyzed; ages 23–50), satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (social > non-social) with voxelwise statistics, cluster thresholds, FDR-corrected results, conjunction analyses, and tables/figures—meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and acceptable formats for reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and healthy-group whole-brain maps are presented. The provided full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Although the independent sample is small (noted as a limitation), all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply, so the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult males (ages 18–35) using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm), which is a social-related task. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (high > low provocation) with FWE cluster correction and reports peak coordinates and cluster tables/figures. Healthy-group results are clearly described. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of gestural social communication (charades) in healthy adult participants (mean age 27.5; n=18 analyzed), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps derived from task data (between-brain Granger-causality maps and GLM analyses described and thresholded at the group level and shown in figures/SI), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The task is explicitly social communication/gesture understanding, fulfilling the fMRI social-related task criterion. Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the provided full text, so the full text appears complete. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (impression updating/perception and understanding of others) in healthy adults (N=21, ages 18–31). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (task, participants, imaging acquisition and processing), Results (whole-brain contrasts, interaction effects) and Discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and cluster coordinates (e.g., L2>F3 contrast, updating-by-condition ANOVA) with multiple-comparisons correction and Talairach coordinates. Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results) and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition (perception/expectation about others on warmth and competence dimensions) in healthy adult participants (undergraduates, mean age 20.4). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects), corrected thresholds, and Talairach coordinates for multiple activation clusters (e.g., putamen, caudate, STS), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation reporting. The constructs map onto the review’s social processing categories. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.
