This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a social-related task (perception/recognition of self vs. others’ body parts), meeting I3. Participants are described as healthy adults recruited for the experiments (I4). The paper reports group-level voxelwise contrasts for localization (body vs objects, objects vs body) with Talairach coordinates, cluster voxel counts and tables/figures, i.e., whole-brain task-evoked results reported at the group-level (I5; acceptable coordinate/table reporting per I6). The main analyses include ROI timecourses, but these are based on ROIs defined from group whole-brain contrasts, so the study is not ROI-only. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines pain empathy (a social-related construct) using task-based fMRI and reports both ROI and whole-brain analyses. It includes a healthy control group of adults (inclusion criteria 18–60) with results for the control group reported separately. The paper presents group-level, within-group whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Self vs Other and Effective vs Not Effective) for controls in the whole-brain analyses (Supplementary Table S1 and figures), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants that examines social cognition/mentalizing (perception and understanding of others) using a passive-viewing social task. The sample consists of healthy adult men (n=21, ages within 18–65). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (voxelwise threshold p<.001, AlphaSim cluster correction) and lists brain regions and tables/figures of results (whole-brain contrasts and coordinate tables). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants in age range, empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study explicitly investigating social cognition (impression formation about people vs objects), meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (N=14; ages 18.3–23.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trial types) with voxelwise thresholding and coordinate tables/figures. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

EXCLUDED because the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (I5 not met). While the study used fMRI during a social-related task (viewing rival football matches) and included healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 are met), its main analyses use ROI/parcellation-based intersubject correlations across 55 atlas regions and report region-wise statistics rather than voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps. This effectively makes the results region/ROI-based without providing unmasked voxelwise group maps or coordinate-based whole-brain contrasts. Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI/parcellation analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results) applies. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no voxelwise whole-brain task map reported). Exclusion criteria met: E2.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a social gambling task manipulating beneficiary (self, friend, antagonist), clearly addressing social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (ANOVAs) with coordinates and figures/tables of activation (including small-volume corrections) for main effects and interactions, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants examining face perception and changeable aspects of faces (gaze, expression)—constructs relevant to social communication (I3). The Methods describe eight healthy observers and ethical approval; participants are healthy adults (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts/localiser analyses with Talairach coordinates, thresholding, and figures/tables of activations (satisfies I5 and I6). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: masked fearful/happy eye stimuli (social cues) during task fMRI with pharmacological manipulation. Sample: healthy adult participants (male, mean age ~24; N=43 analyzed), meeting age and health criteria. Whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses are reported (exploratory whole-brain results with reported clusters in pulvinar, ACC, OFC, and supplementary tables S1–S3), in addition to ROI analyses; within-group (placebo) whole-brain contrasts (Fearful>Happy) are clearly described. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references, supplementary results are referenced).

This fMRI study examines social decision-making (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma), a social-related task involving perception/understanding of others and affiliation/trust. Participants were healthy adults (final fMRI sample n=35; ages reported mean 24.6, SD 4.5, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (multiple whole-brain GLM contrasts, cluster-size corrected maps, tables/figures of significant clusters and coordinates), clearly identified for the healthy participant groups (prosocial and proself). Whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are violated. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of action imitation/observation— a social-related task tapping perception/understanding of others—conducted in healthy adults and schizophrenia patients. The paper reports within-group, whole-brain/random-effects analyses for the healthy control group (e.g., significant activations, corrected cluster thresholds, and peak Talairach coordinates in Table 2 and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Healthy control results are reported separately from patient results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of in-group/out-group facial expressions; relevant to perception/understanding of others). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (final N=26; mean age 21.2 years), within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-level inference and peak MNI coordinates reported; results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. Whole-brain results (interaction contrast and main effects) are provided rather than only ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study using a social-interaction task (virtual handshake) probing social rejection, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=16, mean age 27.4) reported separately alongside a clinical group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts for the healthy/control group (refusal vs acceptance) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction and provides regional results (tables/figures). Hence it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (persuasion/understanding others) using a task where celebrity faces modulate processing of objects, meeting the review's social constructs. Sample: healthy adults (young females, n=24, ages ~21.8) within 18–65, with group results reported separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects, whole-brain thresholds, cluster correction) with tables and figures of activation clusters; small-volume corrections are additionally reported but whole-brain results are present. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The article reports an fMRI study of a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) — a social processing paradigm (meets I3). Sample consists of 30 healthy adult participants drawn from a university community (mean age 21.2), reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects and exploratory whole-brain voxel-by-voxel correlations) with thresholding and reported activations/coordinates and figures/tables (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind: cooperation vs deception) in healthy adults (n=13, ages 22–38). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (exploratory whole-brain ToM vs non-ToM; direct contrasts between conditions) and presents coordinates, figures, and tables of activation peaks. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI experiment of social perception (observation of biological motion and social involvement) using a task requiring participants to judge facing-towards vs away — directly relevant to social-related processing. Sample: 16 healthy adults (mean age 22.75), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses with stereotaxic coordinates and statistical thresholds (p<0.05 FWE, cluster and peak levels) and tables/figures of results, clearly identified for the healthy group. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study explicitly investigates social preference (a social-related task) using task-based BOLD fMRI (meets I3). The sample is 21 healthy adults aged 23–51 with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Preference > Gender, task vs. baseline) with thresholding and tables of stereotactic coordinates (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results (behavioral, activation maps, PPI), discussion, and references; it appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not an ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range-age-only, or non-empirical paper. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that examines social judgments (assessing ambiguous social interactions) while acquiring task-evoked BOLD data. Participants: 20 healthy adults (age range 23–39), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise contrasts) with FDR correction, tables and statistical maps for task effects (e.g., rough > smooth, rough > none) clearly from the healthy group. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI addressing social cognition/mentalizing) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=12, mean age 21). However, the reported neuroimaging results are restricted to an anatomically defined ACC mask with small-volume correction (SVC); the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map or whole-brain corrected results. Thus it effectively reports ROI/SVC-limited results only and does not satisfy the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Exclusion is based on E2 (only ROI/SVC-limited results reported).

This study uses resting-state fMRI and independent component / network connectivity analyses (no task-based social processing paradigm). Exclusion E3 applies: only resting-state analyses are reported and there is no healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Inclusion I4 (presence of a healthy/control group) is satisfied, but I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) and I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map from healthy/control group) are not met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines vocal emotion recognition with task-based fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps in detail, satisfying I3 (social-related fMRI task), I5 (whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). However, the sample consists of children and adolescents (ages 8–19) with no separate healthy adult (18–65) group reported, so it does not meet I4. Exclusion criterion E5 is therefore triggered (only participants outside the 18–65 adult range; no adult subgroup reported). Full text appears complete.

This study used task-based fMRI of social processing (social closeness judgments), satisfying I3. However, it does not report a healthy-adult (18–65) group analyzed/reported separately: the sample spans ages 12–30 and the fMRI results appear to combine adolescents and adults (age was not treated as a variable of interest in the fMRI analyses), so I4 is not met. Critically, fMRI results are reported via ROI-based analyses (beta extraction and regressions within anatomical ROIs) rather than an unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map; no whole-brain healthy-group task maps or coordinates are presented for the fMRI task, so I5 is not met. Therefore the paper violates exclusion E2 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results) and E5 (participants outside 18–65 without a separately reported healthy adult subgroup). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2, E5.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (trustworthiness judgments) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the manuscript reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses of extracted percent signal change and does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or whole-brain contrast tables/figures for the healthy/control group. Therefore it does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social communication (gaze following and finger pointing) in healthy adult participants (N=17; ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (gaze-following vs baseline, finger-pointing vs baseline, and subtraction contrasts) using random-effects analysis, with coordinates, figures, and cluster-level correction. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of self-face recognition, which qualifies as social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Self). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–24) with group-level analyses reported. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Morph 50% recognized as self vs. friend; Morph 100% vs. 60%) with thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and lists activation coordinates in the text/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this study uses fMRI during a social attribution task and includes a healthy adult control group (satisfies I3 and I4), the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported imaging results are primarily between-group contrasts (patient vs control) and subsequent percent-signal-change comparisons within identified clusters. Therefore it fails to meet I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map) and I6 (acceptable whole-brain results for the healthy group). This corresponds to exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (judgments of pride, a self-conscious social emotion, vs joy) in healthy adults. The sample comprises 16 healthy adult participants (mean age ~21), satisfying the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (contrasts: pride−neutral, joy−neutral, pride−joy), with reported voxelwise results, tables of peak coordinates, and figures; appropriate thresholding and conjunction/regression analyses are described. Reporting of whole-brain group effects in tables/figures meets the reporting requirement. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating theory of mind/social processing using a social-related task (stories about agents vs objects) and a ToM localizer. The sample is healthy adults (N=24; ages 25.7±4.2) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects task-evoked analyses (voxel-wise P<0.001, cluster-wise FWE-corrected) with peak coordinates and tables for Background and Outcome contrasts, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (maternal perception of own child’s facial emotions), meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3—uses task-based fMRI probing social/empathic processing (own child facial emotions); I4—includes a healthy adult control group (CON mothers without lifetime mental disorder) within adult age range; I5—reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps identified for groups, including a CON group within-group familiarity effect (medial frontal gyrus) and other whole-brain results (with coordinates and FWE-corrected p-values); I6—whole-brain results are clearly reported with coordinates/p-values in text/tables. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain analyses are reported (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are presented (so E2–E4 not applicable). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore include study.

This is an fMRI study using social-emotional stimuli (angry and happy faces) and a neutral control, with an implicit gender identification task in healthy adult participants (N=30, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., main effects of stimulus type and interaction contrasts assessed with FWE-corrected whole-brain and ROI analyses) and provides coordinates/tables and figures for whole-brain results. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6); no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates this is an fMRI study of social decision-making with healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the available content does not allow verification that the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5/I6 cannot be confirmed). Because the full article (methods/results) is not present, I cannot determine whether results are limited to connectivity/ROI analyses (which would invoke E2/E3) or whether unmasked whole-brain task maps are reported. Cannot include without full-text confirmation.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (emotional face perception during a gender-discrimination incidental task) in healthy adult participants (30 right-handed volunteers screened for psychiatric history). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked effects (e.g., main effect of fearful vs. neutral faces and all faces vs. baseline) and whole-brain comparisons (noted as whole-brain results at p < .001 uncorrected and SV-FWE corrected ROI results), clearly derived from the healthy/control sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI experiment of social-related processing (integration and perception of others’ emotional expressions from faces and voices), meeting I3. Sample: 24 healthy adults (mean age 26), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise contrasts and FWE-corrected maps and coordinates (e.g., conjunctions, interaction contrasts, whole-brain figures/tables), satisfying I5 and I6. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, final N=14; mean age 23.6) that used task-based fMRI while participants viewed socio-emotional two-person interactions (violent conflict) with an orthogonal attentional task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., focus on aggressor vs victim; all conditions vs baseline), statistical maps, cluster correction, figures, and coordinate tables relating activations to personality traits. Thus it meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining processing of pupillary (social) signals during an implicit eye-observation task, meeting the review’s scope for social-related processing (I3). The sample comprises 14 healthy adult participants (mean age 22), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (whole-brain corrected cluster threshold for main effects, coordinates and tables for activations), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-adult sample, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full article content is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of facial recognition (perception/understanding of others), a social-related process. It tested healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 19–36). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects GLM, cluster-corrected contrasts) and lists Talairach coordinates and clusters for activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The study uses fMRI with an explicit social-reward task and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper reports primarily between-group (controls > cocaine users) contrasts and ROI-based small-volume corrected results; it does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Table 2 shows whole-brain analyses for the between-group contrast only. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect), so it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI task study of social cognition (Theory of Mind) so I3 is satisfied. However, although healthy adult controls were included, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The authors created component maps from the combined sample (n=36) and report between-group contrasts (ASD vs control) and task-related ICA components, but no unmasked/control-only whole-brain task activation map is provided. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I4 (results for healthy group reported separately) and I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task map). It thus meets exclusion criteria E3 (only connectivity/ICA-based results without a healthy-group whole-brain task map) and E4 (reports between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (dynamic and static facial expressions) using a task that probes perception and understanding of others. Participants are healthy adults (ages ~25–26; N=24 in Experiment 1, additional samples in Experiments 2–3) meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with multiple-comparison correction and provides coordinates/tables of significant clusters (satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of social cognition (prediction of others’ behavior; theory-of-mind and deontic reasoning) in healthy adults (participants aged 18–44). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial models, cluster- and voxel-level corrected results) and provides tables/coordinates and figures of activations (Tables 2 and 3; whole-brain and small-volume results). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects, participants within 18–65, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of explicit social judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness) on vocal stimuli, fulfilling the review scope. Participant sample: 44 healthy adults, ages 21–60, meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts and conjunctions with cluster-level FWE correction and MNI coordinates (tables and figures), clearly identifying healthy-group task effects. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete, including introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24 analyzed, ages 19–31) using a social-related task (familiarity judgments of personally familiar, famous, and unfamiliar faces) relevant to perception/understanding of others and social attachment. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., P1–Cp1, P2–Cp2, P1–F1, repetition suppression contrasts) with tables and figures of activation and cluster-corrected thresholds, clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults within age range, empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adult participants (N=42, ages 23–40) using a task probing understanding of self and a romantic partner (social cognition/affiliation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (one-sample t-tests, ANOVA) with voxelwise FWE correction and tables/figures of activations. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study of anticipatory interpersonal touch (social-related processing/affiliation) in healthy adults. Sample: 16 healthy right-handed adults aged 20–34 (meets age and healthy sample criteria). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task activation contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts, cluster-corrected maps, Talairach coordinates, tables/figures) clearly from the healthy participant group. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range ages) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion (E3): This study reports only resting-state fMRI analyses (graph theory of MENT and MNS) and a behavioral Theory-of-Mind task administered outside the scanner. It does not include any task-evoked fMRI during a social-related task nor report a whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (no whole-brain task-evoked healthy-group statistical map), I4 (participants include minors aged 12–17 and no separate healthy-adult (18–65) subgroup analysis reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not match the meta-analysis requirement for task-based whole-brain healthy adult fMRI data and is excluded.

Only the article abstract and metadata were provided (full text incomplete). Abstract indicates an fMRI study of social communicative prosody, so inclusion criterion I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is plausibly met. However, the provided content does not allow verification of critical requirements: participant sample details and age range (I4), and reporting of group-level whole-brain task results or maps/coordinates (I5/I6). Because the full text (methods and results) is not available, I cannot confirm these inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Therefore I exclude this record pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (sighted n=14, congenitally blind n=8; ages within 18–65) that uses task-based fMRI to probe perception/understanding of others’ actions (mirror-system activation) via auditory and visual stimuli and motor pantomime. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., familiar action sounds vs environmental sounds; motor pantomime vs rest) with cluster correction and provides statistical maps and coordinates. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of joint attention (a social cognitive task) that includes healthy adult control groups (NT matched-control n=14; independent ROI control n=22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the neurotypical/control groups (e.g., RJA vs SA, IJA vs SA) with coordinate tables and statistical maps described in the text and figures. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for controls), and I6 (acceptable reporting via coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study uses fMRI with a social-empathy task and includes healthy control adults, but the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The reported whole-brain results focus on group-by-age interactions and between-group differences; healthy-group-specific voxelwise activation maps (one-sample T maps for controls) are not presented. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task map (I5 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (includes healthy adult participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map), I6 (no clearly described healthy-group whole-brain results in acceptable format). Exclusion criterion applied: E4 (reports primarily between-group interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social influence (expert advice) on decision-making, meeting the review topic of social-related processing. The sample includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45) reported separately alongside adolescents. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and provides peak coordinates for significant effects (e.g., vmPFC, DLPFC, TPJ), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Results for the healthy adult group are presented and discussed (behavioral and neuroimaging findings), and whole-brain results are reported in main text and supplementary materials. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of emotional speech comprehension (affective sentence classification), which falls squarely under social-related processing (perception/understanding of others' emotions). The sample comprises 51 healthy adults (ages 18–53), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with SPM maps, cluster peaks and coordinates, figures, and tables—meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating neural correlates of persuasion (a social-cognitive/mentalizing process), meeting the review objective. Healthy adult samples are reported (Study 1: N=15, mean age ~20.8; Study 2: N=14, mean age ~22.1; Study 3: N=27, mean age ~20.1), all within 18–65. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (persuasive vs unpersuasive) with voxelwise thresholds (p<.001 uncorrected, 5-voxel extent) and tables/figures of coordinates and conjunction analyses, clearly identified for the healthy/control groups. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range OK, and empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating theory-of-mind/emotion/pain judgments (social cognition) in healthy adult participants (N=46 females, age 18–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (univariate GLM second-level tests with whole-brain maps and cluster thresholds) and multivoxel pattern analyses with normalized maps and whole-brain results presented in figures/tables. All relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes adults within 18–65, and is an original empirical fMRI study. Full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Figures/Tables. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full text reports an fMRI study of social-intention understanding (observing cooperative vs affective social interactions), involving 27 healthy adult participants (ages within 18–65). The task is clearly social (perception/understanding of others), and the paper presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, full-factorial; FWE-corrected results reported; tables of coordinates and figures provided). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adults reported separately, empirical fMRI data present).

This fMRI study examines emotion processing (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group age 18–65 (I4). However, the full text reports whole-brain results as (a) a main effect across all subjects and (b) between-group contrasts (siblings vs controls) and cluster coordinates for these contrasts, but it does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map specifically identified as coming from the healthy/control group (no within-group healthy-control whole-brain map reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criterion E4 (reporting only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect) is met. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E4.

This is an fMRI study of animacy perception and social cognition using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 26.6). The methods report whole-brain, random-effects group analyses with voxelwise thresholds and tables of coordinates and figures for group-level activations (parametric contrasts by subjective animacy and movement patterns). The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others/mentalizing), results are reported for the healthy adult group, and whole-brain maps/coordinates are provided in text/tables, satisfying inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study used task-based fMRI to probe social-related processes (fan identity, self-referential processing, perspective-taking/mentalizing) during recall of basketball plays, meeting the social-processing requirement. Participants were healthy adult males (mean ages ~20–22), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM5 random-effects analyses, tables and figures of activations, and SVC ROI procedures), and results are presented in tables/figures, meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the article should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of emotional perspective taking (empathy) — a social-related task — in healthy adult participants (26 right-handed adults, mean ages ~24), meeting the sample age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SELF- and OTHER-task vs. baseline) with FWE-corrected maps and tables of MNI coordinates and cluster peaks, satisfying requirements for whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of methods and outcomes. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, resting-state-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study reports an fMRI task manipulating self-referential processing and perspective taking (social cognition), and explicitly describes group-level activations in distinct medial prefrontal cortex regions, indicating whole-brain task-evoked results. The sample appears to be healthy adult participants (standard for this type of J Cogn Neurosci study). Thus inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation map reported), and I6 (results described) are met. However, the provided content appears to be an abstract/summary rather than the complete full text, so critical details (exact participant ages, full methods, explicit statement of whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported statistical maps/tables) cannot be fully verified. Therefore I include the study but flag fulltext_incomplete=true and assign moderate confidence.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults examining neural responses to social stimuli (masked emotional faces) in relation to attachment avoidance, satisfying the review objective. The sample comprises 51 healthy adults (age range consistent with 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests and regressions) with coordinates and thresholding details for main effects and correlations, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-action perception using two experiments with healthy adult participants (Exp1 N=20, Exp2 N=20 with one exclusion), ages within 18–65. The tasks probe social-related constructs (perception/interpretation of social actions). The paper reports group-level whole-brain searchlight RSA and univariate analyses, with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tabulated Talairach coordinates (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy sample). Results and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are fully present in the provided full text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of auditory emotion perception (social communication/perception of others) in healthy adults. It used task-based fMRI with a sample of 22 healthy adults (ages 19–36). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain contrast for the voice localizer ([vocal > non-vocal]) used to define the TVA (cluster-level corrected whole-brain results reported), and task activation results are reported with coordinates and ROI/SVC-corrected peaks; thus whole-brain results and coordinate reporting meet I5 and I6. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply: although ROI/SVC analyses are used for the main experiment, the study does not report only ROI results and includes whole-brain localizer maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical dyadic fMRI study (dfMRI) of face-to-face eye contact—a social interaction task—conducted in healthy adults (19 pairs, ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM analyses and paired t-tests to derive exogenous/endogenous activation maps, includes cluster tables and MNI coordinates (Table 3, figures), and describes voxelwise activation maps used to define the CCRI. The study is not ROI-only, not solely connectivity/resting-state, and provides healthy-group task activation maps. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusions.

The study uses task fMRI of social processing (emotional face perception) and includes a healthy adult control group, but it does not clearly report an unambiguous whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. The full text presents whole-brain patient maps and patient-vs-control contrasts (tables described for patients and between-group comparisons) but no clearly identified, unmasked healthy-group main-effect (controls vs baseline) whole-brain statistical map or table of coordinates. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/no accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (clear healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study is excluded because it does not report a group-level whole-brain task activation map specifically for a healthy adult group (age 18–65). While it uses fMRI for social processing (empathy/sympathy) in a healthy sample (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain group analyses across the full sample (I5 satisfied) with conventional reporting (I6 satisfied), the sample is mixed-age (7–40 years) and the paper does not present separate adult-only (18–65) group results or contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (at least one group of healthy adult participants reported separately) is not met. No exclusion criteria E2–E6 (ROI-only, connectivity-only, adult-only outside range, between-group-only without healthy-group map, or non-empirical) are directly met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (multiround trust game) conducted during 3T fMRI and reporting behavioral and neural responses to social interactions. The sample includes a healthy adult control group (n=21, ages 18–47). The paper presents whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and second-level whole-brain analyses for each group (figures and cluster/table results are reported for the healthy control group), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task effects. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain activations, participants within 18–65, and is empirical).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self, reflected self, close-other evaluations) using a task that probes social self-perception and peer perspective-taking, satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=19, ages 22–31) reported separately from the adolescent group, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (2×4×3 repeated-measures ANOVA), corrected for multiple comparisons with cluster thresholds, and reports peak coordinates and cluster tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not truncated), so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (mental simulation of personally familiar others), meeting the review’s task domain (I3). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=23 analyzed, ages 18–27), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and random-effects t-test results, corrected for multiple comparisons, and provides whole-brain maps and tables (satisfying I5 and I6). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation (Social-Reg), a social-related task (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (females aged 22–32; results reported for the healthy group) meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures of results (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and core analyses (task fMRI, resting-state ICA, conjunctions) are reported. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study using naturalistic social-emotional film stimuli (social conflict), with healthy adult participants (N=25 analyzed, mean age 26.3) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (voxelwise z-thresholding, cluster correction) with region results in text, tables, and figures. Continuous valence and conflict ratings were regressed against BOLD and conjunction/PPI analyses were performed. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related emotional face-processing task (I3), reports data from a healthy adult sample (98 participants, ages 18–30) (I4), and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results (faces > ovals) with exploratory unmasked whole-brain analyses and supplemental tables/figures (I5). The paper’s whole-brain results are clearly described in the main text and supplemented by tables/figures, satisfying acceptability of supplementary reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion available. Accordingly, include this study in the review.

The study reports an fMRI task involving social-related processing (fearful face perception), with a healthy adult control group (N=13, age mean 25.6, within 18–65). Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts for the control group are reported (main effect of faces; linear contrasts), with coordinates and figures presented for control-group activations (tables and SPM results). Although small-volume correction was applied to a priori social-brain ROIs, the authors state a global whole-brain threshold (p<0.001 uncorrected) and report group-level activation maps/coordinates for the healthy group, satisfying whole-brain reporting (and acceptable coordinate/table reporting). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion based on lack of a reported healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. The study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: implicit facial emotion processing) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group reported separately). However, the paper reports seed-based effective connectivity (PPI) results and between-group connectivity differences (patient vs control) without presenting an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group in the current paper. Although a control-group peak was used to localize the amygdala seed and the authors reference Hall et al. (2008) for further activation details, the present manuscript does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task map (in text, tables, or figures). Therefore exclusion criteria E3 and E4 apply.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study of social-related processing (allocentric social hierarchy and alliance judgements). Sample comprises 22 healthy adult males (mean age 24.2), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain second-level random-effects analyses with family-wise error (FWE) correction and provides activation maps and coordinate tables (figures and Table 1), clearly reporting healthy-group task-evoked effects. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical) are met. Full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete.

This fMRI study involves a non-social visual attention task in pediatric participants (boys/adolescents), not a social-related task in healthy adults. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (participants outside the 18–65 adult range). Inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are met (the paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps for the control group, with coordinates/figures). However, inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) are not met, so the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (maternal attachment/affiliation) using task-based fMRI stimuli (own infant vs stranger infant). Sample includes healthy adult mothers aged 22–37, satisfying the adult healthy sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and voxelwise contrasts (own infant>stranger infant) presented in figures/tables and described in the text (whole-brain GLM), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Results for the healthy group are reported (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a social-related task (ecologically valid social interactions/oral examinations with an actor during encoding and subsequent retrieval of those socially relevant events), satisfying I3. The fMRI sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=21 in the imaging experiment; participants are students, ages within adult range), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activations (e.g., bilateral retrosplenial cortex, medial prefrontal cortex, hippocampal region; left posterior hippocampus interaction reported with FWE correction), satisfying I5. Results and maps/coordinates are described in the text and figures/tables (acceptable reporting), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are healthy adults, and paper is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore, include the study.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=16, ages 20–31) that used a task probing perception/recognition of other people (voice-face identity matching), i.e., social perception. The study reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses (random-effects GLM) and presents voxel coordinates and statistical maps (with ROI-based FWE correction) for task contrasts and connectivity; results are clearly presented for the healthy participant group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported maps/coordinates), and I6 (maps/coordinates reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses fMRI with a social cognitive (cognitive empathy/emotional perspective-taking) task and includes a healthy adult control group, but the imaging results reported are primarily between-group (schizophrenia vs control) whole-brain contrasts. The paper does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map/statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (only between-group contrasts and percent signal change by group for clusters derived from between-group differences). Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect.

This study reports an fMRI task engaging social-related processing (imaginary sentence completion about mother/father), includes a healthy adult control group (n=15, mean age ~28) and provides whole-brain group-level task activation results for the control group (voxelwise results reported in Table 2 and described in text). The manuscript contains full methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=98, mean age 20.7) that uses task-based fMRI to probe social cognition (judgments about self, friends, and strangers). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., self > Bush, friends > strangers) with whole-brain maps and thresholding described and displayed, and also provides ROI analyses. Whole-brain results for the healthy sample are clearly reported in the text, figures, and coordinate-based descriptions. The study therefore meets the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults with whole-brain group results.

This is an fMRI study of social appraisal (preference judgments of emotional faces), including a healthy adult control group (n=21) and reporting group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and maps. The paper provides within-group control results (activation maps and cluster tables for PREF>GENDER across valences), plus control-group PPI connectivity findings and figures/tables describing whole-brain corrected clusters. The task is clearly social-related (appraisal of others), meeting I3. A healthy adult sample is reported separately, meeting I4. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for the healthy/control group are presented (tables/figures), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult humans (male participants, ages 21–39) that used a social-related task (dynamic investigator feedback—negative vs positive social feedback) during fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects contrasts, corrected thresholds) and presents activation tables and figures for the healthy sample. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, figures, and references).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social-affective processing (compassion/empathy) using the Socio-Affective Video Task (SoVT), a social-related task. Sample includes 94 healthy adult females (ages 18–35). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activations (e.g., HE vs LE contrasts, FWE-corrected results) for the healthy participants, with results presented in text, figures, and tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study used task-based fMRI of face perception/recognition (perception/understanding of others — a social processing construct), tested healthy adult participants (ages reported in 18–65 range across experiments), and performed group-level mixed-effects (FLAME) analyses to derive group patterns for each viewpoint condition (i.e., group-level whole-brain pattern maps used in MVPA). Results are reported in the main text with figures and tables linking behavioral and neural data. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range only samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, and I5 (and reporting format acceptable under I6).

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports task-related results primarily as between-group contrasts (patients vs healthy controls) rather than providing an unmasked, whole-brain, within-group task activation map for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: facial expression discrimination task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, ages 18–60 reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map identified as coming from the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports task-based fMRI (Cyberball social exclusion) in healthy participants, including a separate healthy adult group (n=16). It includes whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (exclusion>inclusion and inclusion>exclusion) with results reported at the whole-brain level (tables and figures) and cluster-level FWE correction. The social-task is directly relevant to social processing (social rejection/affiliation). The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly examining perception/understanding of self (detection of visual feedback ownership/self vs other), a social-related construct within the review scope. Sample: healthy adult participants (n=16, 1 excluded for motion -> healthy group reported; ages 20–28) satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps), thresholded SPM results with tables/figures/coordinates and discussion of whole-brain effects, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (core content present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review objective and is included.

This is an fMRI study of emotion perception from dynamic avatars (socially relevant: perception/understanding of others). Sample: healthy adults (N=19, ages ~28), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., perceived emotional > perceived neutral; parametric maps; figures and cluster-corrected maps), with coordinates and maps described. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). Therefore it satisfies social-task fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining social-related processing (self-related and mentalizing/social cognition) during an article-reading/sharing task (meets I3). The participant sample consists of healthy adults (ages 18–24) with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses and maps (see SI whole-brain analyses, Fig. S3 and Table S5), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary whole-brain reporting; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an fMRI study of joint attention (social communication/perception) using task-based whole-brain analyses in a healthy adult sample (final N=13, mean age 24.85). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., RJA−RJAc, IJA−IJAc), conjunctions, corrected statistical maps and tables of coordinates, satisfying requirements for whole-brain reporting. The sample is within the 18–65 range and healthy controls are reported separately. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based functional MRI during a social-related paradigm (emotional empathy / emotional egocentricity bias), with group-level analyses in healthy adult participants (right-handed female undergraduates within adult age range). The paper provides whole-brain, random-effects task-evoked activation contrasts and reports peak coordinates and corrected/uncorrected maps (fMRI1 and fMRI2 results, tables and figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task effects. PPI connectivity analyses are present but are not the sole reported results. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of rapid fearful face processing (a social-related task: perception/understanding of others’ emotions), including a separate healthy adult control group (n=25) matched on age and IQ. The paper reports group-level task activation for the control group (within-group effects) and direct group comparisons. Although ROI analyses are described, the manuscript also states that whole-brain analyses were conducted using FLAME and refers to Supplementary Table 1 and Appendix Figure S1 showing significant clusters for within-group and between-group effects, with results for the control group clearly reported. Thus the study provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps for healthy adults. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary analysis description) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not report a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked activation map. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (paper reports only seed-based/ROI functional connectivity analyses during a task and network reconstructions, without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related construct: self-referential processing/perception of self). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported); I4 (uncertain/likely not met — sample are aMCI patients and age-matched controls, likely older adults; no ages reported to confirm a healthy adult sample within 18–65). Full text appears complete. Because failure to provide a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map (I5) and reliance on seed-based connectivity alone (E3) violates the review inclusion requirements, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory-of-mind/belief processing) in healthy adults. Sample: healthy adult participants (N=22 analyzed; mean age 24.4) meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM results from an explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph), with reported voxelwise statistical map/peaks (Fig.2A and Talairach coordinates), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Whole-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the supplied content. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, contains within-group whole-brain task contrasts, healthy adult group reported).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults. It uses a task manipulating perceived sender (friend vs computer) during presentation of text messages, which taps social communication/understanding (I3). Participants are healthy adults (female, age 19–28) and reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (univariate contrasts and whole-brain searchlight MVPA/MVCA) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tables of significant clusters (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is original empirical data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of explicit facial emotion identification (a social cognitive task: perception and understanding of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (22 female HCs; mean age 31.7) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) ‘faces minus animals’ contrasts for the HC group (one-sample t tests; figures and tables of coordinates and maps are provided), satisfying the requirement for healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy maps). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This task fMRI study used interpersonal (natural) touch delivered by another person, a social-related paradigm relevant to social communication and perception. Participants were healthy adults (n=8, ages 22–39). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise spatial maps (group ICA components thresholded at z=2.5) and present these maps and task-related component time courses with statistical comparisons across touch types. The paper includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. It is not ROI-only, not purely resting-state/connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group whole-brain task-related maps; thus it meets inclusion criteria. Confidence is moderate-high because the group maps derive from ICA (data-driven) rather than a conventional GLM contrast, but they are group-level voxelwise task-related maps and satisfy the review requirements.

The provided full-text is incomplete: it contains only metadata (title, authors, keywords, references) in the HTML head and lacks core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because of this, I cannot verify critical inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/cannot be confirmed: I3 (cannot confirm that the paper reports functional MRI task-based results for a social-related task from methods/results), I4 (cannot confirm participant sample includes healthy adults 18–65 or separate healthy-group reporting), I5 (cannot confirm the paper reports at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group). No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) can be determined from the incomplete text. Recommendation: obtain the complete article (methods and results) to reassess eligibility.

Although this fMRI study uses a social-related self/other perspective-taking task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (I4), the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group alone. Most whole-brain contrasts reported are between-group comparisons (ASD vs TD) or combined-group maps; the healthy-group whole-brain activation map is not clearly presented as an independent, voxelwise TD group result. Therefore exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect) is met.

This study reports an fMRI task of self-referential processing and perspective-taking (Perception and Understanding of Self), which falls within specified social-related constructs. It includes a healthy control group (reported separately) and reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy/control group (e.g., VMPFC activation in HC). Whole-brain statistical maps and contrasts are described, with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and within-group results presented. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult control group reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps for healthy controls), and I6 (whole-brain results acceptable as reported). No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an original fMRI task study using romantic and sexual visual stimuli (social/affiliation-related constructs). Participants were healthy adult men (n=20, ages 22–50). The methods specify whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME random-effects, Z=2.3, cluster-wise thresholding) and the Results present group-level whole-brain contrasts (sexual>neutral; romantic>neutral; within-group and between-group contrasts) with tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range within limits, and this is empirical original data). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) using healthy adult participants (men and women ages 18–22). The paper reports task-evoked whole-brain analyses and group-level contrasts (e.g., CC vs CD; drug vs placebo) with cluster-corrected thresholds and lists regional results in text, figures and supplementary tables, satisfying reporting requirements. All required inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social stimuli (fearful and calm faces), includes a clearly described healthy adult control group (age means ~39–40, within 18–65), and presents group-level, whole-brain within-group activation results for the control group (described in the text, shown in figures and reported in tables of coordinates). Reporting format meets acceptable formats. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (naturalistic social videos) in a healthy adult sample (N=37, mean age 24.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction) with FWE-corrected results and accompanying tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review objective.

This is an fMRI study of perspective-taking/theory-of-mind (social cognition: perception and understanding of others). It reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other) with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of results. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=16, mean age 22.4) with results reported for the healthy group. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical paper issues).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (theory of mind/social exchange) in healthy adults (N=12 analyzed; mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (story and card contrasts; SPM2; tables/figures/coordinate clusters reported) for the healthy participant group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study used a social-related task (facial emotion discrimination), includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately, and presents whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (within-group contrasts and maps for controls, e.g., sad>neutral and other contrasts; SPM2 results reported with thresholds). Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are adults, and this is empirical fMRI data). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study acquired resting-state fMRI in healthy adults (N=20) and used meta-analytic coactivation (MACM) and behavioral decoding to characterize LIPL subregions. It does not report any original task-based fMRI experiment or within-study, group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from the healthy sample. Although the authors report that some subregions are associated with social cognition via MACM/decoding, those are meta-analytic inferences rather than task-evoked maps from the study's healthy participants. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (only resting-state/seed-based/meta-analytic connectivity without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample) is met; I3 and I5 are not met.

Excluded because the paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group. It focuses on diagnosis effects and between-group contrasts/conjunctions (patient vs control) rather than presenting a clear healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during social-related tasks: theory of mind and empathy) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, n=20, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map identified as coming from the healthy/control group). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Although the study includes an fMRI task probing social cognition (RMET) and reports whole-brain group-level activation maps for the healthy participants, the healthy sample consists of older adults aged 51–84 (M=68.4) with no subgroup analyses restricted to ages 18–65. This violates the review's age inclusion requirement. Therefore the paper is excluded under E5 (participants outside 18–65 with no qualifying subgroup). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation reported for healthy group), I6 (results reported in figures/tables).
