Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65 not satisfied). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition (theory-of-mind) task (ToM vs control) in a sample of healthy volunteers (n=109). The methods report task design, imaging acquisition and preprocessing, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses: a one-sample t-test for the main ToM>control effect across all subjects and genotype regression analyses, with whole-brain multiple-comparison correction (FDR/FWE) and tables/figures of activation coordinates. Behavioral and connectivity results are also reported, and core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) are present, indicating a complete full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (emotion recognition and gaze integration), meeting inclusion. It uses task-based fMRI (I3) during a social communication/perception task (angry/happy faces with direct/averted gaze). It includes a healthy younger adult group (mean 20.65; age range reported 17–27) satisfying the requirement for a healthy adult sample in the 18–65 band (I4) — the sample is largely adult and reported separately by age group. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (PLS whole-brain results with peak coordinates and figures) for the healthy groups (I5) and provides coordinate tables and figures (I6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20 analyzed; mean age ~24.6) that directly investigates social-communication processes (recognition and imitation of communicative/social gestures). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM analyses, Monte-Carlo cluster correction) with coordinates and figures/tables of activations (e.g., IPL, mOFC, mPFC), clearly identified as healthy-group task contrasts. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Although this fMRI study uses a social cognition task (Sally-Anne variants) (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately (I4), the paper reports only between-group (typically developing > ASD) whole-brain contrasts and region-of-interest analyses derived from those group comparisons. The full text does not provide a clearly identified unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map (one-sample healthy/control group whole-brain results) or coordinates/figures explicitly labeled as the healthy-group main effect. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete = false).

This paper reports an fMRI hyperscanning study using a joint attention task (a social-related task) and provides group-level analyses. It includes a large healthy adult sample (80 HCs; ages within 18–65) reported separately from clinical groups. The methods and results describe whole-brain task-related analyses and contrasts (INT>NoINT) and explicitly state that results were obtained for the whole brain and are reported in figures/tables/supplement, satisfying requirements for voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy/control group. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating perception of others' eye gaze (a social-communication cue) in healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (face vs control; clusters identified with z>4, cluster sizes and Talairach coordinates reported) and contrasts for task conditions (attention to identity vs gaze; averted vs direct gaze), with results described in text, tables and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title/abstract and metadata (fulltext_incomplete=true). The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (perception of racial ingroup/outgroup faces) and reports data from healthy adult participants, meeting I3 and I4. However, the abstract does not clearly report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group (I5 not met). The abstract emphasizes an ROI-based analysis of amygdala voxels, and no whole-brain results are provided in the available content, meeting exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Because the full text is incomplete and whole-brain results cannot be verified, the study cannot be confirmed to satisfy the whole-brain evidence requirement and is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (N=10) using social-related tasks (empathy and forgiveness judgments) and the abstract reports group-level activations in multiple brain regions, consistent with whole-brain task-evoked results for healthy participants. However, only the abstract and metadata are provided here (no full methods, participant ages, or detailed results/mapping), so I cannot fully verify voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps, exact age range, or analytic details. Inclusion is therefore provisional pending access to the complete full text.

This is an event-related fMRI study that explicitly investigates social evaluation (trustworthiness) of faces (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (14 analyzed; ages 18–30) meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, random-effects SPM analyses and provides whole-brain task-evoked results (contrasts, coordinates, figures and tables) that are clearly from the healthy/control group (meets I5 and I6). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and supporting analyses (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses are not limited to ROI-only, are task-evoked (not resting-state or connectivity-only), report within-group healthy-task effects rather than only between-group contrasts, and are empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social causal attributions (self vs other; self-serving bias), using task-based whole-brain voxelwise analyses in healthy adult participants. Sample: 12 neurologically healthy adults (males aged 20–51) meeting the age range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain fixed-effects results with voxelwise correction, tables of coordinates and figures, and additionally examines self-serving vs non-self-serving contrasts; results are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study examining implicit social judgments (acquired moral status via a sequential Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Sample: healthy adults (scanned N=11; age range 21–36), satisfying the age/sample criterion. Analyses: group-level, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (one-sample t tests across subjects) using SPM2 are reported; whole-brain results and tables of coordinates are provided (with ROI and whole-brain reporting), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The task is socially relevant (cooperation/defection; perception and understanding of others). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 27.2) who watched video clips of social interactions, satisfying the social-related task requirement. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (relational vs. alone; relational vs. rest) with correction for multiple comparisons and cluster reporting (figures and Table 1), meeting whole-brain evidence standards. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates processing of social gaze (a social-related task) using task-based BOLD fMRI (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (young adults, n=8 in fMRI portion), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level voxelwise/whole-brain activation maps (across-subjects t-statistic activation maps visualized on a standard brain; voxel-based analyses described and thresholded), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results (I5). Reporting of whole-brain results in figures and text meets the allowance for coordinate/figure/table reporting (I6). Although an ROI approach was used for primary analyses, the authors also performed and reported voxel-based group-averaged activation maps, so the study is not limited to ROI-only results. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

Study is an fMRI experiment of social interaction (cooperation vs competition) in healthy adults (12 participants aged 21–28). It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise contrasts (cooperation vs independent, competition vs independent, direct comparisons) with statistical thresholds and tables/figures described. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study directly examines social-related processing (evaluative judgments of guilt and embarrassment, linked to social cognition/Theory of Mind) using a task during fMRI, in a group of healthy adult participants (N=19, ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects contrasts (guilt minus neutral; embarrassment minus neutral) with thresholded statistical maps, coordinate tables, figures, and regression analyses, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The provided content is only abstract/metadata (PDF-only notice); core full text (methods, participants, results) is not available, so key inclusion criteria cannot be verified. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study reports fMRI experiments of social cognition). Inclusion criteria not met/cannot be confirmed: I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65 not reported in available content), I5 (no verifiable report of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps in the provided text), I6 (unable to confirm that whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplements). No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 are clearly met based on available information. Because essential information is missing and required inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, the study must be excluded pending access to the full text. Full text appears incomplete in the materials provided.

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task addressing perception/understanding of self), conducted in healthy adults (N=10, mean age 26.9). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (self > other and other > self) with cluster-corrected statistical maps and tables of MNI coordinates, and describes preprocessing/GLM/registration procedures. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-cognitive processing (impression formation of people vs objects), satisfying the review objective. Participants were healthy adults (N=14; age range 18.3–23.7), meeting the sample inclusion requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trial types; voxel-based threshold P<0.001) and provides MNI coordinates and tables of activations, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just an abstract), so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self-face recognition = Perception/Understanding of Self). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=12, right-handed males, mean age 19.36) meeting the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., self vs familiar, familiar vs unknown, unknown vs scrambled) with SPM-based random-effects analyses and figures/tables of activations. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 24.4) examining neural responses to angry vs. neutral prosody—a social-communicative/emotion processing task relevant to social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise contrasts and coordinates for main effects and interactions (e.g., amygdala, STS, OFC, cuneus), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind and empathy) in healthy adults (N=13; mean age 24.9), using a task that probes perception/understanding of others. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2 random-effects; voxelwise thresholds and tables of coordinates/figures are provided). Healthy adult results are reported separately and meet age range. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults examining social-related processing (virtual characters, gaze and socially relevant vs arbitrary facial expressions). Sample: 18 healthy right-handed adult males (mean age 25.9) — meets adult healthy sample requirement. Whole-brain acquisition and group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (SPM2; contrasts, coordinates, tables and figures; reported main effects and interactions with stereotactic coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. The task is explicitly social (social communication, self-involvement, joint attention). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and references. Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study that tests perception/understanding of self (detection of visual feedback ownership), satisfying the review construct. Sample: healthy adults (n=16, ages 20–28) — meets age/sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (Aa–As, Pa–Ps, and their comparison) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds, with results presented in tables/figures and discussed — satisfies whole-brain evidence and reporting criteria. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–32) that investigates spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception (a social-cognition task—perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects group contrasts) with tables and Talairach coordinates for significant clusters (e.g., APC, STS, anterior insula), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The sample and results for the healthy adult group are reported separately and clearly. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

Provided full text is incomplete (only summary/abstract present). While the study uses fMRI to examine perception of faces (a social-related task), the manuscript excerpt does not report participant details (age range, healthy adult sample) nor confirm group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures for the healthy group. Therefore I cannot verify inclusion criteria I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on available text, but because core full-text content (methods/results) is missing, the study cannot be confirmed eligible. Request full article text to reassess.

The paper reports an event-related fMRI study using a social interactive (competitive retaliation) task in healthy adults (16 healthy male participants, mean age 28.6). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (SPM2 random-effects t-statistics, tables of activations and coordinates, conjunction and parametric analyses). Results for the healthy sample are presented (not limited to a narrow subgroup). The task probes social processes (interaction, perception/understanding of others, empathy/compassion). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants (healthy adult undergraduates, mean age 19.5) viewed images of social groups and made affective/social judgments, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and contrasts (subtractive and 3-vs-1), providing whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy sample. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete, including methods, results, and discussion, enabling verification of analyses and healthy-group whole-brain findings.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of social semantic processing (participants judged meaning relatedness of social concept word pairs vs animal function concepts). Sample: 26 healthy adult participants (mean age 29.4), satisfying the healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., social vs. animal; positive vs. negative social concepts) with tables of coordinates, figures, and corrected statistics, clearly from the healthy cohort. Methods and results include whole-brain analyses (voxel-level thresholds, correction), ROI analyses, and parametric regressions; therefore whole-brain evidence is present and clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate social-related processing (facial emotion recognition; social communication/perception of others), includes a healthy adult sample (29 right-handed adults, ages 20–35) reported separately, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected maps and tabulated coordinates/ROIs. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical).

Full text appears incomplete (no participant ages/demographics or explicit whole-brain statistical maps reported). This is an fMRI study using a social exclusion (Cyberball) task, reporting whole-brain, group-level task-evoked contrasts. The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=16, ages within adult range) alongside adolescents. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses for the main effect (exclusion>inclusion) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and coordinates (Table 2), and further reports age-group interaction and post-hoc within-group tests (including adult t-tests and coordinates). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI (I3), contains a healthy adult sample (I4), presents whole-brain group-level task activation maps/coordinates (I5), and reports results in tables/figures/text (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Note: adult-specific whole-brain maps are reported as within-study contrasts and post-hoc tests; main whole-brain maps are reported for the combined sample but adults are a healthy group with separable reported results.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based social cognition paradigms (judgments about self, friends, and strangers) directly addressing perception/understanding of others and self. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=98; mean age 20.7), meeting the age and population criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., self > Bush; friends > strangers) with whole-brain maps and ROI analyses; results and thresholded maps are described and displayed, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group activation reporting. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social processing (empathy/sympathy) using task-based fMRI (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy participants including adults within the 18–65 range (ages 7–40, so adult participants 18–40 are included; meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (PCS–NPS and PCO–PCS) and correlation analyses with age, with coordinates and activation maps (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity/resting-only, no clinical-only sample, and it is an original empirical study). Note: analyses are performed on the full healthy sample (mixed ages) rather than an adult-only subgroup, but the study still provides whole-brain, group-level results from a healthy participant cohort that includes adults, satisfying the review’s inclusion criteria.

Full text provided is limited to abstract, references, and metadata (full article methods/results not present). The study investigates adolescents (three phases of adolescence) using fMRI Trust Game, so it meets I3 (fMRI during a social task). However participants are adolescents (not adults 18–65), violating inclusion criterion I4; thus exclusion criterion E5 applies (participants outside age range). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot fully verify whether whole-brain group-level healthy-adult maps are reported (I5). Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting the adult-sample requirement and due to incomplete full text for verifying other criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face individuation (perception/understanding of others), a social-related process. The sample is healthy adults (N=15 final; mean age 24.8), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analyses for the individuation task (ANOVA with voxelwise threshold and cluster correction) and provides whole-brain figures and coordinate tables (e.g., Figure S1, Table S1), meeting the whole-brain reporting requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social processing (observation and categorization of social interactions vs non-interactions using point-light displays). The sample is healthy adults (N=14, mean age 29.4), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SI vs NSI contrast) with FDR-corrected voxelwise results and peak coordinates/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI of humor processing (a social-cognitive task involving theory-of-mind/incongruity resolution and social/emotional appraisal), in a healthy adult sample (N=29, mean age 27, 18–65). It provides group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (within-group contrasts, parametric modulation, conjunctions) with corrected results and tables/coordinates referenced. Thus it meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social impression-formation task probing violations of social expectations; (I4) the sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=18 after exclusions; ages 19–30); (I5) it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (incongruent > congruent) with FDR-corrected cluster results and coordinates; (I6) whole-brain results are reported in tables, figures, and text. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (they include whole-brain analyses), not connectivity/resting-state only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study directly examining social-related processing (representation of social interaction/social context vs. solitary) during an episodic memory task, using task-evoked BOLD contrasts. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24, ages 18–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (contrasts, thresholding, cluster correction) with coordinates and activation tables/figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text not available (only abstract/metadata and note that PDF is paywalled) so core methods/results cannot be fully verified. From the abstract the study used fMRI with dynamic social interaction videos (meets I3) and sampled 20 young adult volunteers (meets I4). However I cannot confirm the presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported for the healthy group (I5) nor the exact form/location of whole-brain results (I6) because the full article (methods, results, tables/figures) is inaccessible. No exclusion criteria are directly met based on the abstract alone. Because I5 (and thus I6) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the full paper.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment explicitly probing social-related processing (allocentric social hierarchy and social alliance judgements) in healthy adult participants (n=22 males, mean age 24.2). The Methods and Results describe whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with voxelwise contrasts and tables of coordinates and figures; thresholding is reported (p<0.05 FWE, extent=30), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The sample falls within the 18–65 range, and healthy-group effects are clearly presented separately. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (decisions to help family; mentalizing/affiliation constructs), meeting the review objective. Sample comprises healthy adults (N=25; Mage=20.2, range within 18–65) and results for this healthy group are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Costly-Donation vs Noncostly-Reward) with tables of coordinates and figures, and describes preprocessing/analysis and PPI results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of self-face recognition (perception/understanding of self), meeting the review construct of social-related processing. Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–24) and results are reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM; thresholds given) with reported coordinates and clusters (e.g., MPFC, PCC, precuneus), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group effects, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly examines viewing/observing virtual social interactions and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps (Figure described based on data from 15 participants) showing activity in social cognition regions (STS, mPFC, amygdala). The methods describe MRI acquisition and standard whole-brain preprocessing/analysis (SPM), satisfying requirements for task-based, whole-brain healthy-group results. Participant recruitment is described as based on age/health and the results reference 15 participants, implying a healthy adult sample. Ages are not explicitly listed in the provided excerpt, so there is minor uncertainty about the exact age range (18–65), but overall the study satisfies the review objective and the other inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social processing (eye contact and mimicry), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=20; mean age 23), satisfying the population criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (multiple contrasts, random-effects analysis, cluster-level FWE correction) with results presented in Table 1 and Figures, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; whole-brain results are reported as coordinates and figures (acceptable per I6). The study also includes connectivity analyses (DCM) but crucially provides unmasked, whole-brain task activation maps rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only; not resting-state/seed-only; not between-group-only; participants within 18–65). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of social perception in healthy adults (romantic partner vs roommate), so inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages ~18.7) are met. However, the paper’s statistical approach is ROI-focused: group-level SPM{t} maps were corrected for multiple comparisons within a priori ROIs (8-mm spheres) and the caudate finding was from an ROI/exploratory analysis. The manuscript does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map (or whole-brain correction/cluster results) for the healthy group—results are reported only within predefined ROIs. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported with no whole-brain results). Because I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the review.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates an fMRI study of face/voice perception (social-related processing), so I3 is met. However I cannot confirm that participants are healthy adults age 18–65 (I4) because ages/health status are not reported in the abstract, nor can I verify that the paper reports at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from the healthy group (I5). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Because key inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, I exclude pending receipt of the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social-related processing (stereotype/social-category judgments) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 19–28). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ‘social’ > ‘non-social’ and ‘non-social’ > ‘social’) with cluster correction (P < 0.05, corrected) and presents peak coordinates, figures and tables. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-emotional processing (audiovisual facial and vocal emotion integration), using a task that assesses social communication/perception of others. Sample: 24 healthy adults aged 18–34 (within 18–65). Analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (conjunctions and contrasts such as CAV>ICAV, reported with FDR correction, tables of activation clusters, and figures). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social competition (human vs machine) that explicitly manipulates a social/ToM context during task performance (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=14, mean age 35.9), satisfying the adult healthy-sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., I> C, H>I+C, interaction [H(I>C)]>[M(I>C)]), cluster thresholds, and tables/figures of activated regions, providing unmasked whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-healthy-only results; full methods, results, and discussion are present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball exclusion) in healthy adults (n=20 analyzed; ages ~25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (social exclusion vs fair play and contrasts by excluder gender), with tables/figures and coordinate reporting. Methods, results, and ROI analyses are provided in full. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: It uses functional MRI during a social task (ultimatum game) probing social decision-making. I4: Participants are healthy adults (male volunteers aged 23–28), with group results reported. I5/I6: The paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses (offline whole-brain SVM classification across subjects) and provides discriminating volumes with MNI coordinates and p-values (Tables/Figures), which constitute voxelwise whole-brain evidence clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results (including tables of coordinates and figures), and discussion, so the full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (13 right-handed males, mean age 28.2) using a task that probes perception of others' actions (point-light biological motion) — a social-related construct (I3). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts (canonical vs. scrambled biological motion) with corrected voxelwise results, coordinates, tables, and figures (satisfies I5 and I6). The healthy adult sample is explicitly reported and analyzed (I4). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only analyses, not a between-group-only contrast, and participants are within the 18–65 age range. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining socio-affective touch (CT-targeted affective touch), which is a social-related task relevant to affiliation/attachment and social perception. The sample comprises 22 healthy adults aged 19–35. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain RFX GLM task contrasts (arm > baseline, palm > baseline, and arm > palm) with FDR and cluster correction, and provides tables/figures of voxelwise results and coordinates. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This fMRI study investigates emotional prosody comprehension (social communication/perception of others) in healthy adult participants (n=19, age 18–51). It reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (emotional vs neutral; complex vs simple emotion) with voxelwise inference and cluster correction, and provides coordinate tables and statistical maps described in the text. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s social-processing objective and satisfies inclusion criteria for task type, sample, and whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers using a social group (team membership) manipulation and an action–perception task to probe social processing and in-group bias. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., action videos vs fixation; own-team vs other-team; decision contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides stereotactic coordinates and figures. The sample comprises healthy adults (age range includes 17–43 but the group analyzed is healthy adults and results are reported at the group level), and both behavioral and fMRI within-group results for the healthy participants are presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets criteria for fMRI of social-related processing in healthy adults and reports whole-brain healthy-group task activations.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (social working memory) in healthy adults. The task required participants to mentally rank friends on trait dimensions during fMRI, meeting I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task). The sample comprises 16 healthy adult participants (mean age 20), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric effects, whole-brain thresholds, coordinates in tables/figures and supplemental material), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Overall, all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of empathic (social) decision-making in healthy adults. It reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation and connectivity analyses (GLMs, PPI) with results described in the text and reported at whole-brain corrected thresholds and in tables/figures. Sample: 32 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLMs), Results, and Discussion, so core article content appears complete. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI to investigate processing of communicative vs noncommunicative vocal sounds (a social-communication task). The sample consists of 20 healthy adults (mean age 22), meeting the healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (vocal > nonvocal; communicative > noncommunicative) with voxelwise thresholding and peak coordinates (tables and figures), not limited to ROI or connectivity-only results. Full text includes methods, behavioral ratings, acoustic controls, preprocessing, and whole-brain results with coordinates, so the full text is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met.

This is an empirical BOLD fMRI study that explicitly examines social perception (affiliation vs. isolation) during an event-related task where participants made pleasantness judgments while scanned. The sample includes a younger healthy adult group (N=16, mean age 20.75) within the 18–65 range, with results reported for younger adults and direct between-group comparisons. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM; thresholds and extent reported) and tables/figures of activation (conjunctions, contrasts, and peak coordinates), thus providing whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy (younger) group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study examined self-referential (social) processing using the VV-SORP-T (a social cognition task involving self vs other and valenced words). Sample: 20 healthy adult women (ages 18–52) meeting the 18–65 requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked BOLD contrasts analyzed with SPM8 and presents group maps, coordinates, tables and figures (e.g., Tables 2–4, Figures 2–4), clearly from the healthy participant group. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses or connectivity/resting-state-only approaches. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social evaluation/impression formation using a task with social (interpersonally meaningful and irrelevant) and non-social conditions. It includes a healthy young adult group (ages 20–29) meeting the 18–65 requirement, and reports group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts: social vs non-social; social-meaningful vs social-irrelevant), conjunction analyses, and corrected cluster results presented as tables/figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 present), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, includes eligible age subgroup, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of impression formation/updating (social perception of others), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=24; ages 18–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (interaction L2>F3 by consistency; L2>F3 contrasts within target types) with thresholding and cluster correction, and presents results in tables/figures (Supplementary Tables and Figures). Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective (social-related processing) and satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adults (n=51, ages 18–53) that uses a social-related task (emotional sentence classification involving theory-of-mind/mentalizing), reports group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) with corrected voxelwise maps and coordinates, and provides full methods and results. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 23.6) using a social/empathy paradigm (threat to self, friend, stranger with hand-holding). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (conjunction analyses, whole-brain higher-level contrasts, voxelwise covariate analyses) clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control sample. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-context processing (effect of expert advice) that includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45). The full text reports task-based fMRI with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (thresholding, cluster-correction) and lists peak coordinates and clusters for valuation-related contrasts for the groups. Results for the healthy adult group are reported separately alongside adolescent groups. The task involves social information (advice from an expert) relevant to social cognition constructs. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines neural synchronization during viewing of emotion-laden movie clips—a social-related paradigm probing perception/understanding of others’ emotional states (empathy/mentalizing). Sample: 16 healthy adults aged 25–49 (within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain ISC maps and voxelwise GLM analyses relating valence/arousal to ISC with FDR-corrected voxelwise statistics and figures/tables of coordinates. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=94 female, ages 18–35) that used a social-affective task (Socio-affective Video Task) probing responses to others’ distress (compassion/empathy). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation contrasts (e.g., HE vs LE; parametric modulations) with results reported at P<0.05 FWE and coordinate tables/figures, and also reports training-related group comparisons; thus whole-brain healthy-group task effects are clearly presented. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study investigating how healthy participants learn to simulate others' decision-making (a social cognition task addressing perception/understanding of others), satisfying the review objective. The paper reports data from healthy adult participants (n=36 after exclusions) and describes experimental methods and analyses. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported (cluster-corrected maps, Tables 1 and 2, and whole-brain analyses described in Methods/Results), and coordinates/tables are provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples) are met based on the provided text.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (affiliation and power motives) in healthy adults. Methods report task-based fMRI with movie-clip stimuli designed to elicit affiliation vs power, inclusion of 17 healthy adult male participants (age 18–65), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (affiliation>control, power>control) with reported activation clusters and MNI coordinates. Results are presented for the healthy sample (no clinical subgroup issues). The paper reports whole-brain group statistical maps and coordinate tables (not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Sample is male-only but within the adult age range and reported separately as the healthy group.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social interaction perception (cooperative vs affective scenes), with healthy adult participants (N=27, ages in mid-20s). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (main effects and direct contrasts; p<0.05 FWE-corrected and tables of coordinates), clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control sample. Behavioral task and methods, as well as introduction, results, and discussion are present, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception using naturalistic audiovisual clips and GLM task analyses. N=19 healthy adult participants (ages 21–34) were scanned while viewing clips annotated for multiple social features. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects one-sample t-tests; p<0.05 FDR corrected) comparing social vs. non-social features and feature-specific contrasts, with results presented in figures/tables and described in text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI social-related task in healthy adults with whole-brain group maps. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of affiliative/attachment-related social processing using a task with written social scenarios (affective/kinship content). Sample: healthy adults (final N=27; ages within 18–65), with demographics and exclusion of neurological/psychiatric disorders reported. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (affiliative vs nonaffiliative; valence contrasts) with FWE correction and coordinates/tables (Table 2, figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining maternal neural responses to infant cry—a social/attachment-related task—using a sample of adult mothers (mean age 24.1) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked group-level analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, cluster thresholding, coordinates reported in tables/figures) for contrasts such as own cry > control and own > other, clearly described as coming from the healthy sample. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies I3 (social/attachment fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures described in text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/perspective taking) in healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Sample: 18 healthy adults aged 21–31, satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement. The authors report second-level, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (paired t-tests, two-sample t-tests, conjunctions) with cluster- and peak-level FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates, satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly presented (contrasts Self vs Other, View-Pain vs View-No-Pain, good vs bad performers). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical original data). The provided full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is included in the review.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social reasoning (theory-of-mind / emotion/moral stories and videos) in a healthy adult sample (N=45; ages 19–23). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (random- and fixed-effects analyses), reports peak coordinates (Appendix A), and shows task vs. rest and domain contrasts across the cortex. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full; analyses are not limited to ROIs or resting-state/seed connectivity alone. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI social-related tasks in healthy adults with whole-brain group maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-only, non-healthy age group, non-empirical) are met.

This study uses task-based fMRI to investigate perception of emotional facial expressions (a social-communication/social-perception task), includes a healthy adult sample (n=23, ages 24–34), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster-wise correction and figures/tables showing activations. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, empirical data). Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI data collected during a social cognition task (action observation with why/how/what/how instructions), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses and provides cluster coordinates (Table 1) and notes that whole-brain results and supplemental methods are available, satisfying I5 and I6 (whole-brain results are described in the supplement). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within the 18–65 range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplemental material is referenced but its absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This is an fMRI study of visual perspective taking/theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults. The sample consists of right-handed healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22.4), meeting the 18–65 age requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other; conjunctions), with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of results/coordinates. Results for the healthy/control group are reported directly (not limited to an ROI or subgroup). The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, imaging, analysis), results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 24) that investigates neural responses during observation and execution of others' actions — a social-related process (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level task-evoked analyses, including ROI and whole-brain analyses (whole-brain results reported at p<0.001 uncorrected with peak coordinates and clusters), and provides coordinates and figures of activation maps. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task results), and I6 (coordinates/figures clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses task-based fMRI probing social cognition (contrast of interactive vs. observational social scenes) in a healthy adult sample (N=22, mean age 25), satisfying construct and sample criteria. The authors report group-level statistical analyses using whole-brain RFX ANOVA and describe at least one unmasked, whole-brain (exploratory) finding (early visual areas/V1) in the text. Although much of the inferential reporting focuses on ROI small-volume-corrected results, a group-level whole-brain task analysis was performed and an unmasked whole-brain effect is described, meeting the requirement for whole-brain evidence as acceptable when reported in text. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study manipulating social vs. nonsocial information (trustworthiness of faces) during an n-back task, testing social working memory. Participants were healthy adults (initial N=16; imaging analyses N=14; mean age 22). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2x2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster-corrected results and tables of peak coordinates for main effects and interactions. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range ages, non-empirical) are met.

This empirical fMRI study uses a social task (viewing others in pain; empathy/perception of others), scans healthy adult participants (N≈36, mean age ~21), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FDR-corrected whole-brain results, tables/figures) clearly identified for the healthy/control groups. The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study (with an accompanying ALE meta-analysis) that directly investigates social/person-related processing (familiar/famous faces, social closeness judgments). Participants are healthy adults (final sample N=15, mean age 22.3), satisfying the age and sample requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (random-effects GLM contrasts such as Faces_friends vs Faces_novel, Faces_famous vs Faces_novel) with coordinates, tables, figures, and corrected thresholds; thus whole-brain evidence is available in standard coordinate/tabular form. The tasks clearly map onto social-related constructs (perception/understanding of others, affiliation/social closeness). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face-gender perception (a social perceptual process: Perception and Understanding of Others). Participants were healthy adults (N=16, ages 19–42), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports a whole-brain random-effects voxel-wise group analysis (contrast gender-different > gender-same) with cluster-corrected results (p<0.01) and lists activated clusters (right collateral sulcus, left precuneus, right lateral occipital gyrus). Full methods, ROI and whole-brain results, and discussion are present in the provided full text, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an event-related fMRI study of interpersonal (social) conflict and sharing decisions, involving healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5). The task probes social cognition/decision-making and mentalizing (social-related constructs). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects contrasts, conjunctions) with figures and tables of activations for contrasts such as Human (Conflict > No Conflict) and Computer (Conflict > No Conflict), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures; supplementary methods are referenced but not required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This fMRI study investigates abstract vs. concrete mindsets using two tasks (Why-How and Categories-Exemplars) that engage social-cognitive processes (e.g., mentalizing, action understanding). It reports data from a healthy adult sample (N=24, ages 18–27). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts are reported (e.g., How>Why, Exemplars>Categories, conjunctions), with SPM analysis, thresholding, cluster correction, tables of regions and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines attractiveness comparisons (a social perceptual judgment—perception and understanding of others) using task-based fMRI. Participants were healthy adult women (N=25, mean age 23.46), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction), conjunctions and coordinates for task contrasts, and ROI analyses as supplemental; whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This is an fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults: (1) It uses task-based fMRI probing learned social roles following a cyber-ball social interaction and face perception tasks (meets I3). (2) Sample is healthy adults (15 participants, age 24.1±3.8) (meets I4). (3) The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain searchlight analysis testing pre- vs post-learning pattern similarity and reports significant, whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters in superior temporal sulcus with MNI coordinates (meets I5 and I6). Although the primary analyses are ROI-based MVPA, the reported whole-brain, corrected searchlight results satisfy the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise group-level effects. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study that directly assesses social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults (ages 18–27 and 18–23 across experiments), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical; individual mental > individual physical), with tables of regions and figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical study).

Full text presents an fMRI study of social processing (romantic interest/rejection in a speed-dating paradigm) satisfying the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3—uses task-based fMRI targeting social constructs (affiliation/attachment, perception of others); I4—healthy adult participants reported separately (scanned group N=38, ages 19–31); I5—group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts are reported and thresholded (SPM8, voxelwise P<0.001 with cluster FWE control) with tables of coordinates; I6—whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text. No exclusion criteria appear to apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult group whole-brain maps). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI task probing social communication/communicative intentions (relevant social construct), uses a healthy adult sample (N=23, mean age ~24, within 18–65), and provides group-level whole-brain task activation contrasts and coordinates (e.g., main effects and interaction contrasts with voxelwise thresholds and tables/figures). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not a truncated abstract). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (handholding with friend/stranger/alone) in healthy adults (mean age 23.6). The task is clearly social/affiliation-related, and the paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (threat vs safe) identified via cluster-wise voxelwise analysis (Z>2.3, cluster p<.05) and subsequent ROI-based extractions; results are reported across whole-brain ROIs and statistical tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (laughter perception) in healthy adults (N=18, mean age 26). It employed task-based fMRI with social-related tasks (explicit laughter-type categorization) and an implicit task, satisfying the social-related fMRI requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses (with FWE cluster correction) and provides tables/figures of whole-brain activations and contrasts (CSL vs TIC, CAT vs COU), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The sample consists solely of healthy adults within 18–65. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; contains whole-brain task activations in healthy group; not resting-state/only connectivity; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-communicative gesture observation and imitation in healthy adults. It reports task-based whole-brain group analyses (voxelwise contrasts, Monte-Carlo cluster correction) with MNI coordinates and contrast statistics, clearly from the healthy/control participants (n=20 reported). The paradigm targets social communication/communicative intention, satisfying the review objective. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (images of human suffering; regulation strategies targeting perception/understanding of others), includes healthy adult participants (ages 18–45) with results reported separately for the healthy trainee groups, and reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group-level analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; right IPC and DLPFC clusters reported whole-brain corrected). Whole-brain results are described in the text and corrected for multiple comparisons. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age out of range, non-empirical) are violated.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (gambling for self, friend, antagonist) that probes affiliation/other-understanding and reward responses. Sample: 31 healthy adults aged 18–26, reported separately and meeting the adult age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (one-way and 3×2 repeated-measures ANOVAs) with results described in text, figures, and Tables of coordinates; small-volume corrections and whole-brain thresholds are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/mentalizing: participants (healthy young adults, mean age ≈20.5) were scanned while encoding ideas they might recommend (a social-communication task). The sample meets the healthy adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (explicitly states 'whole-brain analyses' with thresholding and reports coordinates in Table 1 and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, materials, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, statistical analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’), using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., how vs what) with MNI coordinates and corrected statistics (PFWE), tables and figures describing activation maps. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms probing theory-of-mind and emotion understanding (social processing). Sample: 46 healthy adult participants (female, ages 18–31) satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests with cluster correction), with tables and whole-brain figures describing activation maps and coordinates. Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses and healthy-group effects are clearly reported. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study uses fMRI of a social-evaluation task (meets I3) and reports whole-brain voxel-wise developmental analyses across a healthy mixed-age sample. However, it does not present a group-level, whole-brain task activation map explicitly identified for a healthy adult-only group (age 18–65). The analyses focus on continuous age predictors and developmental (child–adolescent–young adult) effects rather than an unmasked adult within-group activation map. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E4 (no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect for adults). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants (n=21 healthy right-handed adult males, ages 23–33) watched animations of dyadic nonverbal interactions and rated naturalness during fMRI, satisfying the requirement for a social-related task (I3) and a healthy adult sample (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., CS+CR+MS+MR > scrambled; main effects and interactions) with cluster-level correction and tabulated peak coordinates, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Behavioral and fMRI Results, Discussion, and Conclusions (fulltext appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation using task-evoked BOLD responses in healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 19.1). It employs an ecologically valid social task (impression formation of real confederates) during fMRI (I3 satisfied), reports results for a healthy adult sample within the 18–65 range (I4 satisfied), and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., form impression > sequencing) with cluster-corrected voxelwise results and coordinates reported in tables (satisfying whole-brain evidence requirement I5 and acceptable reporting formats per I6). The paper also provides coordinates/tables and descriptions of statistical maps. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social perception task (passive viewing of point-light biological motion), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult sample (n=48, ages 20–35) with results reported for the healthy adult group, meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task-evoked contrasts (biological > scrambled motion; Sex×Condition ANOVA) with tables/figures and cluster-corrected thresholds, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain activation maps, adult sample within 18–65, and is empirical).

The article reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=31–45, ages 19–28), employs social-related tasks (eye-gaze, self-propelling motion, and implicit mental-inference role-play), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and results (e.g., E–O, S–X contrasts, voxelwise regression, tables/figures of activation peaks). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. The study uses task-based fMRI in a social cognition paradigm (third-party punishment; inference of others’ intentions and moral responsibility), fulfilling I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 26, range within 18–65), fulfilling I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and statistical results (mixed ANOVA on β parameters; whole-brain FDR threshold q<0.05) with coordinates (Talairach x,y,z) for regions such as R TPJ and R anterior insula, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study using social stimuli (traffic-awareness videos) designed to elicit socio-cognitive processes (mentalizing/empathy), meeting the review’s task-domain requirement. Participants are healthy adult volunteers (ages 19–30), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) and presents whole-brain analyses for the control (safe driver) and dangerous driver groups (figures and text describing whole-brain results), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete for screening.

This study uses task-based fMRI with a social stimulus (face viewing) addressing social perception/understanding of others, includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–37) reported separately in group descriptions, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., whole-brain regression results and tables/figures such as Table 3 and Fig. 5). Whole-brain results are clearly reported for the healthy participant sample. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of attribute framing during social evaluation (self and reflected perspectives), meeting the review topic of social-related processing (perception/understanding of self). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–41) and group results are reported for this healthy sample. The methods and results describe whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses and report group-level contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frame; frame-inconsistent vs frame-consistent) with peak coordinates, cluster thresholds, and rendered figures. Thus the manuscript provides clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The provided content is incomplete (only abstract, metadata, and references; core methods/results not present). Inclusion criteria: I3 satisfied (fMRI during a social-related task — approachability judgments of faces).
