I4 likely satisfied (healthy adult participants implied) but sample details are not present in the excerpt. I5 (reporting at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map) cannot be confirmed from the truncated full text: although the abstract mentions activations, the full methods/results/tables or coordinates are not available to verify whole-brain voxelwise reporting. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are demonstrably met from the excerpt. Because I5 cannot be verified due to incomplete full text, I must exclude pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social processing (emotional egocentricity bias) using task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants. The paper reports multiple group-level whole-brain task analyses (fMRI Experiment 1 whole-brain exploratory analyses and additional analyses in fMRI2, with SVC informed by fMRI1; whole-brain methods and results are described), and presents behavioral and fMRI results for healthy adult samples (female undergraduate participants, ages within adult range). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies the review's inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of social-related processing in healthy adults and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (Dynamic Social Gesture task) in healthy participants, meeting the review objective. I3: The task probes social processing (social vs nonsocial gestures, actor-orientation, face-visibility). I4: The sample is a group of healthy young adults (N=20; mean age 21.4) within the 18–65 adult range (note: one participant’s age is reported as 16.9, but the analyzed group is presented and treated as a healthy adult sample). I5: Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported (TFCE with permutation testing; figures and tables of activations). I6: Whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study that used a social-related task manipulating collaboration and competition while measuring effort (handgrip) with fMRI (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=32; ages 18–39) with exclusions for neurological/psychiatric conditions (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM8 GLM, clusterwise FWE correction) and tabulated/figure activations (e.g., Table 1, whole-brain contrasts and parametric maps), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: participants made social coordination judgments of ambiguous interactions while scanned. Sample: 20 healthy adult participants (ages 23–39), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (ANOVA and post-hoc t-tests) with results corrected for multiple comparisons (FDR) and tables/figures of activations (e.g., rough > no priming; masked analyses), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Behavioral and neuroimaging methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, resting-state/connectivity-only, outside age range, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This paper is a structural MRI (voxel-based morphometry) study in healthy adults investigating grey matter volume correlates of moral sentiment proneness. While half the sample previously participated in an fMRI study and the authors used individual SSC-BOLD values from that prior work for secondary correlations (subgroup N=29), the present article does not report any group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI statistical maps from healthy participants. It therefore fails the key inclusion criteria requiring an fMRI whole-brain task activation map (I3 and I5). The sample is healthy adults (I4 met). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly met by this manuscript.

This empirical fMRI study investigates live verbal social interaction (social communication) using simultaneous fMRI in pairs of healthy adult participants (22 right-handed women, mean age ~27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task effects (second-level voxel-wise t-tests, cluster-corrected results; figures and supplementary tables described) for talking, listening, and inter-individual coupling. Tasks are social-related (verbal communication), the sample is healthy adults within the 18–65 range, and whole-brain group results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only sample, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports task-based fMRI of explicit social judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness) on vocal stimuli in healthy adults (N=44, ages 21–60), matching the review's social-processing constructs. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM8; cluster-level FWE correction; tables of MNI coordinates and conjunction analyses), and results are clearly from the healthy/control sample. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy using naturalistic video stimuli and behavioral ratings, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample comprises 27 healthy adult participants (mean age 34.07), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM results, voxelwise contrasts, conjunction analyses, MNI coordinates, and figures (i.e., whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps) clearly for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplemental material is linked. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognitive processes (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) using task-based fMRI (I3). The sample consists of 15 healthy adult males aged 18–40, meeting the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The authors report group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, voxel-wise thresholds with cluster correction, conjunctions, and peak coordinates for contrasts and interactions (I5, I6). Group-level main effects and condition contrasts for the healthy participants are clearly described in the text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete for screening. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during a social task (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) probing social cognition and trust. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 24.6; screened for MRI), satisfying the age/sample requirement. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with corrected statistical maps and cluster-size thresholding, with contrasts and clusters reported in the text/figures/tables. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, imaging, analysis), results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This article is a narrative review (non-empirical) and does not report original fMRI data in healthy adults. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no functional MRI during a social-related task reported), I4 (no healthy adult participant group reported/analyzed), I5 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked statistical maps reported). The provided content appears to be limited to abstract/metadata (fulltext_incomplete is set true). Based on these points the study should be excluded.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (familiar vs unfamiliar faces; social cognition/attachment constructs) in a patient and an age-matched healthy control group. The control group (n=13) whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (partner>unfamiliar and faces>baseline) are reported with coordinates and FWE-corrected cluster results, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Healthy control results are reported separately from the patient. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. One minor uncertainty is that controls are described as older adults (mean age 64.5 ±5.7), near the upper bound of the 18–65 inclusion range; ages are not provided as an explicit range, so a small proportion may exceed 65 — reflected in moderate confidence. Overall, the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate exclusion criteria E2–E6.

Meets all inclusion criteria: This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Ultimatum Game) involving social decision-making (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult group (ages 19–28) reported separately (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (unfair–fair contrasts), one-sample t-tests and between-group ANOVAs with reported activation maps/tables for the adult group (I5), and results are clearly described in the text and figures/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, healthy adult whole-brain maps provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (free online imitation) in healthy adult participants (23 right-handed females, ages 18–30). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (imitating vs rest, being imitated vs rest, observation vs rest) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE) and provides activation tables/coordinates and figures. It also includes PPI connectivity analyses, but these are supplemental to and do not replace the whole-brain task maps. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

(a) Exclusion criterion met: E3 — the study reports only ICA (a data-driven connectivity/ decomposition approach) and does not present a conventional group-level, whole-brain task activation map or voxelwise GLM contrasts for the healthy group. Although ICA spatial maps are shown, the paper lacks an unmasked whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (e.g., main effect or within-group contrast) reported as voxelwise activation. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: natural touch from another person) and I4 (healthy adult sample, N=8, ages 22–39). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map shown) and I6 (acceptable reporting formats for whole-brain results not applicable because such results are not provided). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This paper reports an fMRI faces-versus-houses task targeting face perception (a social-related process: perception/understanding of others). The sample includes healthy adults (N=57 behavioral; subset N=22 with fMRI) within the 18–65 range. The authors performed whole-brain, second-level SPM analyses and report group-level activation maps/clusters (Tables/Figures) including suprathreshold voxel counts in bilateral fusiform gyri for the healthy group (faces vs houses contrast). Results are reported as group-level, voxelwise task-evoked effects and described in the text/figures/tables. The full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a social processing task (social distance trials using participants' friends vs acquaintances) and other distance domains. Participants were healthy adults (N=15; ages 20–28). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight MVPA and RSA mapped to standard space, group t-tests, conjunction analyses) with tables/figures of significant clusters (e.g., right IPL) and FDR-corrected thresholds. Full article text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study uses task-based fMRI of social processing (social closeness judgments) and includes healthy adult participants (ages 19–30), so I3 and I4 are met. However, the paper reports fMRI results using region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (mean beta extraction from anatomically defined ROIs and small-volume corrections) rather than providing an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map for the healthy group. No whole-brain task activation maps or voxelwise results for the healthy/control group are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of self and reflected peer-evaluations) that includes a healthy adult group (N=19, ages 22–31). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (2×4×3 repeated-measures ANOVA with age group as between-subjects factor) and corrected voxelwise/cluster thresholds (AlphaSim; p<0.005, k=64), and notes separate within-age-group analyses (with additional results in Supplementary Materials). Thus it satisfies: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly described, including supplementary materials). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (bystander effect) using a social-related task (viewing emergencies with varying group sizes) while performing a color-naming task. Sample: healthy adult participants aged 18–27 (N=17 initially; one excluded for technical failure) meeting the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (random-effects GLM, parametric maps, contrasts) with cluster correction and tables/figures of results. Whole-brain results are clearly described and reported. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (causal attributions involving self, other, situation) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–41). The task is social/mentalizing in nature (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults within 18–65 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (ANOVA, contrasts, conjunction; whole-brain thresholding and FWE-corrected clusters are reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range is appropriate, and this is an empirical fMRI paper. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables referenced). Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (attribution of awareness to another), conducted in healthy adult participants (n=50; ages 18–49) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (group fMRI contrast H trials − E trials, Fig. 3, Table 1) with corrected thresholds. The methods and results include whole-brain analyses projected to cortical surfaces and Talairach coordinates, satisfying the reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, mean age 20.7) that uses functional MRI during social tasks (Cyberball and a modified Dictator Game) addressing social processing (punishment/forgiveness of excluders). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Exclusion no ball > Inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality) with coordinates and cluster tables/figures. Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social (interpersonal) touch anticipation in healthy adults (N=16, ages 20–34). It uses task-based functional MRI with group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses (contrasts, conjunctions, cluster-corrected results) reported in the text, figures, and tables. The sample is a healthy adult group within the 18–65 range and results for the healthy participants are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range sample) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of self-referential (social) processing (conceptual and agentic self/other recollection). Participants were healthy adults (n=18; ages 19–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation results (conjunction and old>new contrasts) with FWE-corrected clusters and coordinate tables, in addition to ROI analyses; whole-brain maps/coordinates are clearly presented as coming from the healthy sample. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processes (intergroup competition; self-referential moral processing) in healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 23). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables/figures of whole-brain results (Tables 1 and 2; corrected p<.05), and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. The task probes perception/understanding of self in a social context, meeting the review objective. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study tested facial color processing (face perception), which qualifies as social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others / Social Communication). The sample comprises 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.24), meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (natural-colored face vs natural-colored scrambled image) with figures and coordinates (P < 10^-3 uncorrected), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results and ROI analyses are also provided, and whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation; not connectivity-only; healthy adult group reported). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is included.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social feedback processing (a social-related task: perception/understanding of self and others). Participants are healthy adults (German and Chinese groups). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (SPM analyses with FWE-corrected clusters and tables of coordinates) and describes these results in the text and tables. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (interactive rating task) in healthy adult participants (mean age ~24, n=20 scanned). The task is clearly social (communication of emotional arousal between interaction partners) and maps onto social-related constructs (social communication, perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (clusterwise FWE-corrected over the entire brain; Tables and Figures show activations in insula, DLPFC, amygdala, ventral striatum), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study presenting realistic social-interaction video stimuli (first-person perspective) and measuring task-evoked BOLD responses in a sample of healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and conjunctions (FDR-corrected maps, cluster thresholds) with peak coordinates and figures (glass-brain views and tables of Talairach coordinates). Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the text. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I6 (coordinates/figures acceptable). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age-appropriate, empirical). Full text appears complete. No exclusions applied.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (10 males, ages 22–32) that examines processing of social interactions using point-light displays. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts (atypical vs typical displays) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of activation foci (coordinates), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task probes perception/understanding of others (unattended social context), and healthy-group results are reported separately. Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognitive processing (imagined triadic social interactions) in healthy adults, reporting whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts. The sample comprises 19 healthy adult participants (age mean 26.5, within 18–65). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain results (conjunctions and contrasts) thresholded at p<0.05 FWE and provides tables/figures of activations and connectivity analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not just abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, patient-only, or non-empirical paper). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adult participants (N=28, mean age 25) using a social task (Ultimatum Game) and reports group-level task contrasts. However, the second-level analyses were performed within a restricted anatomical mask comprising 16 bilateral ROIs (wfu_pickatlas) rather than as an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Therefore the paper reports only ROI-restricted results and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map required by inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a social-interaction task (fMRI-adapted Taylor Aggression Paradigm) presenting opponent facial expressions; sample comprises healthy adult participants (32 analyzed, mean age 23.3); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (angry>neutral) with cluster-wise FWE control and tables/figures of whole-brain results. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing: participants played a competitive matching-pennies game against human and non-human agents after brief social interactions (a social-related task engaging mentalizing). Sample: healthy adults (n=16 analyzed; ages 18–25), meeting the adult healthy-sample criterion. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (GLM, random-effects second-level one-sample t-tests; voxelwise p<.001 with cluster-level FWE correction reported; coordinate tables and figures provided). Results are clearly reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-task, non-healthy age groups, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a social task (impression formation of others varying in financial and moral status), satisfying the social-processing requirement. The sample is healthy adults aged 19–31 (n=20 males), meeting the age and healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANOVA) with tables and figures of activations (Table 1, Fig. 3) and describes thresholds and cluster reporting, fulfilling the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map; these results are clearly attributed to the healthy participant group. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group effects, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 22.7; final MRI n=16) that employs a social cognitive task (implicit false-belief/Sally–Anne movies) during BOLD fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts with voxelwise SPM results and peak coordinates (e.g., belief > photo/map; false- > true-belief). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. The paper therefore meets the review objective (fMRI of social processing) and satisfies inclusion criteria: use of fMRI in a social-related task (I3); healthy adult sample reported separately (I4); group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and coordinate tables reported (I5); and whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables (I6). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text provided appears incomplete (only highlights, abstract, abbreviations, and metadata). Based solely on available content: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) is clearly met. However, critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified: I4 (participant ages and confirmation of healthy adult sample) is not reported in the available text, and I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed because methods/results and tables/figures are missing. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be determined from the truncated content. Because necessary information to confirm all inclusion criteria is lacking and the full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full-text access.

This is a task-based fMRI study that used traffic-awareness campaign videos designed to elicit empathy (social/emotional processing), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample comprised 20 healthy adult males (ages 20–28), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (campaign vs neutral videos) with family-wise error correction (p<0.05) and peak coordinates/tables, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are clearly described in the text. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition using healthy adult participants (ages 20–31). However, the reported neuroimaging results are ROI-based (FFA, OFA, aTL, STS PPI) with significance assessed using ROI-based FWE correction; the authors explicitly state there were no significant whole-brain results at P<0.05 FWE without the covariate. The paper therefore does not present an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group. This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain evidence). Hence excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=26, ages 18–39) that used a social-related task (perception of biological motion) and reports group-level whole-brain task analyses. The Methods and Results describe whole-brain analyses (biological-motion selectivity correlated with social-network diversity) with multiple-comparison correction and report a significant cluster in right pSTS, fulfilling the requirement for a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked map. The sample meets the healthy adult age range. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=50, ages 18–29) that used an explicit social-related task — labeling others’ emotional facial expressions — addressing perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE) and whole-brain regression analyses with FWE cluster-level correction and tables/coordinates, clearly coming from the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, age range within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–33) that investigated social-sharing/affiliation by having friends view emotional and neutral pictures either 'together' or 'alone'. The paper reports task-evoked, group-level voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects GLM) with whole-brain thresholds (P<0.001 uncorrected, cluster-level correction via AlphaSim) and reports whole-brain significant activations (e.g., DLPFC, precuneus, emotion main effects) in addition to ROI results (VS, OFC). Behavioral and fMRI results are clearly reported for the healthy adult sample. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults. It used task-based fMRI while participants received text messages they believed came from a friend or a computer (social-related task). The sample comprised healthy adults (female, ages 19–28) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM maps, cluster results, Table 2) and provides coordinates and figures. All four inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/sole connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants in age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (social tie formation in a repeated public good game) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (scanned group n=25, ages ~22). The paper reports multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and coordinates (parametric effects of social tie, impulse, contribution magnitude), with cluster-wise FWE correction and detailed GLM methods and results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (mutual understanding) using a dyadic interactive task (meets I3). Sample consists of 54 healthy adult participants (27 pairs), ages 18–27 (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., whole-brain search for BOLD dynamics, cluster-level correction, localization of rSTG) and presents results in text/figures (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (joint attention) in healthy adults (N=13, mean age 24.85). The task is clearly social (interactive joint attention) and uses task-evoked fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., RJA − RJAc, IJA − IJAc), conjunction analyses, FDR-corrected statistical maps and tables of coordinates (Table 2, Figures 4a–d), clearly attributed to the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract/metadata (conference abstract) without methods, participant details, or results. Inclusion met: I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related eye-contact interaction per abstract). Inclusion not met / cannot be verified: I4 (no participant/sample details to confirm healthy adults aged 18–65 or separate healthy group reporting), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or reported results in the abstract), I6 (unable to verify whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met, but because the full text is incomplete (fulltext_incomplete=true) key eligibility criteria cannot be confirmed, so the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study engaging healthy adult participants (N=37, mean age 25) in an explicit social communication task (feeling addressed by actor gestures/body orientation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (main effects and interactions) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level correction, and presents behavioral and imaging results across the healthy sample. All inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, age range appropriate, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines perception of social interactions (congruent/incongruent person dyads) in healthy adult participants (N=12, ages 21–31). It uses task-based functional MRI during a social-related perceptual task (sex-categorization of dyads). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses with voxelwise thresholding (p<.001) and cluster-based correction (p<.05), and provides tables/figures of peak coordinates (Table 3, Figs. 6–9). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI study that investigates perception of emotions and interactions in crowds (social-related processing). Sample: 16 healthy adult participants (ages 19–27). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were conducted (random-effects ANOVAs) with cluster-corrected results reported in tables and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (deception in strategic interactions; ToM/social cognition) using an interactive sender–receiver task, meeting the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=34, ages 21–32), satisfying the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results: Bayesian second-level probability maps and voxelwise contrasts, with coordinates and tables/figures for multiple contrasts (e.g., deception vs. truth), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are reported in tables of coordinates and figures. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, imaging, analysis), Results (behavioral and imaging), and Discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=18, ages 18–44) using a social cognition task (prediction of others' behavior; ToM and deontic reasoning), meeting the review objective. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds reported; tables of activations described), and coordinates are provided. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using dyadic fMRI during an eye-contact task (a social-processing paradigm). Sample: 19 pairs (38 individuals) of healthy adults with ages reported (mean 22, range 18–33), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM for tasks A and B, paired t-tests for exogenous/endogenous contrasts), with thresholding, cluster listings and atlas-based coordinates (Table 3, Figures 3–5). Whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and tables. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; includes task activation maps; not resting-only or connectivity-only; not between-group-only; is empirical with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures, tables). No exclusions identified.

This paper is a non-empirical/theoretical review discussing explanations of mirror-touch synesthesia and referring to existing fMRI evidence, but it does not present original fMRI data or report methods/results from a healthy adult fMRI task. Only abstract/metadata are provided here (full text incomplete). It therefore fails to meet the required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it does not use functional MRI during a social-related task with original data (I3 not met), does not report a healthy adult sample with task data (I4 not met), and does not provide group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I5 not met). Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data in healthy adults) applies. Full text is incomplete (only abstract available).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social attribution that used a social/nonsocial why/how task, reporting brain activations for social processing. Sample: healthy adults (N=19; ages 21–46) meeting the adult age criterion. The paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses (conjunctions, cluster-corrected maps and tables/figures of activations) clearly reported for the healthy participant group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (social-affective mimicry task manipulating affiliation-relevant cues: emotion and group membership), with healthy adult participants (N=41; mean age ~22.6, range within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (Incongruent>Congruent and condition-specific contrasts) analyzed in SPM8, cluster-level multiple-comparison correction, and tables of local maxima coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Behavioral and imaging results for the healthy sample are reported clearly. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social incentive delay task (social reward condition) in healthy adult participants (N=63, ages ~20–36) and reports group-level task-evoked activation results. The paper provides whole-brain results (e.g., whole-brain FWE-corrected activations for reward outcome and mentions whole-brain analyses in Tables 3 and 4), with contrasts clearly described for the healthy/control group (social > monetary, reward > neutral, etc.). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social working memory and perspective-taking (social-related tasks) in healthy adults (N=25, mean age 21.56). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunction, SWM vs CWM contrasts) with cluster tables and figures, and uses random-effects inference; results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, enabling assessment of eligibility. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Meets all inclusion criteria: This is an event-related fMRI study of social processing (observing eye contact and gaze following), involving healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 24.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts and lists/describes multiple whole-brain contrasts and cluster results (with tables and figures), analyzed with SPM8 and corrected thresholds. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 19–31) investigating social cognition/perception (ToM, faces, biological motion, voices, language) using task-based BOLD fMRI. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise activation analyses (mixed-effects group maps, peak MNI coordinates in Table 1, and figures) clearly from the healthy/control participants and provides whole-brain GLM modeling and coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI in healthy adults with reported group-level voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=17, ages 21–46) that examines neural responses during a Why/How action-understanding task tied to mentalizing/social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (cluster-forming threshold P<0.001, cluster-level FWE correction, with whole-brain results described and reported in Supplementary Tables and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group only, participants in range, and empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=30, mean age ~24) that uses social-emotional tasks (gender identification of angry and happy faces vs neutral shapes), satisfying the review focus on social-related processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain and ROI analyses; main effects and contrasts are described and reported in text/tables/figures), thus providing whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so material is complete for screening. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports fMRI during an interactive social/mentalizing task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) addressing attachment and theory-of-mind, satisfying I3. Sample comprises 164 healthy adult subjects, meeting I4. The abstract and highlights describe task-evoked neural activations across the mentalizing network and correlations with attachment dimensions, indicating group-level whole-brain task activations (voxelwise results), satisfying I5. Reporting of network regions in text/abstract meets I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) appear to apply. However, the provided content is truncated (only abstract/highlights/metadata visible) and the full manuscript (methods/results details and explicit whole-brain statistical maps/tables) is not present here; therefore fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is reduced. Full text should be reviewed to confirm that whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinate tables are explicitly reported for the healthy group and not limited to ROI or between-group contrasts.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI task probing a social-related process (spontaneous imitation/urge to imitate), includes a healthy adult sample (N=37, ages 18–25), and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked results with statistical thresholds, tables and figures (coordinates and corrected cluster-level inference). Whole-brain task activation maps and parametric modulation results for the healthy group are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (undergraduates aged 18–21) that used a social-related task (viewing social vs. non-social scenes) and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (social>non-social; FDR corrected, p<0.05) with tables/figures and ROI follow-ups. The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical map reported), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

The study is an empirical fMRI experiment investigating social reputation (a social-related construct). Sample: healthy adult participants aged 20–24 (N=28), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., positive vs. neutral, negative vs. neutral), with thresholding and a table of brain regions/coordinates (i.e., whole-brain evidence from the healthy group). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social cognition paradigms (EmpaToM manipulating empathy and Theory of Mind), satisfying the review topic. The sample comprises healthy adult participants within 18–65 (N=25 in Exp1a, N=65 in Exp1b, N=178 in Exp2; mean ages reported), meeting the sample criterion. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., emotionally negative > neutral videos; ToM > nonToM questions), thresholding procedures, tables of activation peaks, and figures clearly attributed to the healthy/control sample. Coordinates and whole-brain contrasts are reported, fulfilling acceptable reporting formats. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (gaze-following toward political in-group/out-group personages), satisfying the review’s social task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=28, ages 18–29/36 reported), meeting the age and healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent interference effect) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level correction, and presents results in tables/figures and text. Thus whole-brain healthy-group activation maps are available. ROI analyses are also reported, but whole-brain results are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, age within range, and empirical fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a validated Theory-of-Mind (social) task (moving triangles) with healthy adult participants (n=20; ages 24–64). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ToM > Random; ToM > Baseline) with thresholds and cluster-level correction, and provides coordinates/figures/tables of activations (right TPJ, IFG, occipital regions). Results from the healthy control group are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of negative emotion processing using IAPS images (viewing emotional pictures) and effective connectivity (Granger causality) between amygdala and dmPFC. Although the sample comprises healthy adults (N=46, ages 18–45) and the paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (HA− > NTR contrast) and coordinate data, the primary task is affective/emotion processing rather than a social-related task as defined by the review (affiliation/attachment, social communication, perception/understanding of self or others). The task does not require explicit social cognitive operations (e.g., mentalizing, theory-of-mind, social interaction, attribution), so it does not meet I3. Therefore the paper fails inclusion criterion I3 despite meeting I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of empathy for pain manipulating minimal group membership—a social-related task (empathy/Perception and Understanding of Others). Sample: 30 healthy adults aged 18–35 (meets adult healthy sample requirement). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses are reported (main effects of pain, condition, and pain×condition interaction) with tables of activations and coordinates. Results for the healthy sample are clearly presented. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5 and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, males, age 23.6±4.1) that used a social-related task (watching dyadic violent interactions with manipulated attentional focus), meeting the review’s construct scope. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., all conditions vs baseline; focus on aggressor vs victim) with voxelwise maps and cluster-corrected statistics presented in figures/tables, and discusses trait correlations and connectivity. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3, I4, I5, I6), and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages 19–26) performing a reading task that manipulates social content (Social vs Non-social) and assesses theory-of-mind—a social cognition construct, satisfying the review objective. Group-level whole-brain random-effects contrasts are reported (Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-level correction and peak voxels/clusters presented in Table 1 and Figure 1, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Behavioral measures relate fiction exposure to ToM and are linked to neural activity. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=28, ages 30–50) that explicitly examines social stimulus processing (implicit social content defined by images of humans) alongside self-referential processing. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and direct contrasts), corrected results (FDR p<0.05) with cluster extent and peak coordinates, conjunction and interaction analyses, and tabulated/figure results. Methods, results, and discussion are fully present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using a social-related task (Cyberball social exclusion), with healthy adult participants (university students, final N=42, ages consistent with 18–65). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (exclusion vs. inclusion) and reports whole-brain analyses and thresholds (P<0.05 FWE) and tables/figures of activations. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age ~21) using a social perception task (passive viewing of in-group/out-group facial expressions addressing racial prejudice and disgust), satisfying social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (2×2 ANOVA, whole-brain contrasts, corrected cluster results) and provides coordinate tables/figures and ROI follow-ups. No exclusion criteria are met: results include whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), include task-evoked activations in the healthy sample (not only connectivity or between-group contrasts), and participants are within 18–65. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an fMRI study using a social-content task (valence classification of agentic vs communal trait words) in healthy adult participants (N=42; ages 18–25). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 (GLM contrasts, conjunctions) with AlphaSim cluster correction and reported group-level activation/deactivation results (figures and tables of coordinates are referenced). This satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social communication (speech-act comprehension) in healthy adults. The full text reports an experiment with healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 18–41) performing a social-communicative task (Naming vs. Requesting), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, random-effects task contrasts (e.g., Request > Naming) with FDR-corrected whole-brain results and tables/figures describing coordinates and statistics, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social interaction (joint attention and mutual gaze), in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~21–23). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (SPM analyses, cluster- and voxel-level statistics) and coordinate tables/figures are provided. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI social-task studies in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is an fMRI study using a dynamic social gestures (DSG) task that directly assesses social-related processing (social vs nonsocial gestures) in healthy participants. The sample comprises healthy young adults (mean age 21.41, range 16.9–25.7), so the group includes adults within the 18–65 range and is reported as a healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (FLAME group analysis, cluster-corrected Z>2.3, p<0.05) and provides coordinates and figures/tables for results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met; analyses are whole-brain task activations (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), and the paper is empirical. Note: one participant is slightly under 18 (16.9), but this does not trigger exclusion E5 since the group is a healthy adult sample and results are reported for that group.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=60, mean age ~20) that uses a social task (explicit control of interpersonal trust/distrust) satisfying the review’s social-related construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (whole-brain contrasts, FWE-corrected thresholds, tables/figures) for the healthy sample and provides ROI and connectivity analyses as supplementary. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. I3: It uses task-based fMRI during social-related tasks (round-robin face-viewing with person-judgment localizer; constructs include perception/understanding of others, affiliation). I4: Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 28.7, within 18–65). I5: The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects parametric whole-brain regression, FWE-corrected results; Table S4, Fig. S1). I6: Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and described in text/SI. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age range appropriate, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, SI described).

This is an fMRI experiment on social cognition (empathy/compassion) in healthy adults (N=26, mean age 30.3). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts with FWE-corrected clusters and tables/figures (e.g., Tables 1 & 2, Figure 3), clearly from the healthy/control group. Therefore it satisfies I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task results), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social communication/interaction in healthy adults (N=29, ages 18–27). The task manipulates perceived live vs. recorded speech and examines neural responses during story listening (a social-related task). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Live Story > Social Story; Social > Standard) thresholded and cluster-corrected, with figures/tables describing voxelwise results and ROI-localizer-defined analyses. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported for the healthy group; I6: whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–27) using a social cognition / mentalizing task (participants judged scenarios to evoke 60 mental states). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (searchlight MVPA maps, network-level analyses, and univariate whole-brain regression/t-test maps), with cluster correction and tables/figures of voxelwise results (main text and SI). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample in 18–65 range), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps from healthy group), and I6 (results reported in main text and supplemental figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social learning (learning about others’ generosity) using a task-based fMRI paradigm (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (initial N=30, analyzed N=26; ages 19–37; meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLMs, conjunctions, contrasts, voxel-wise thresholding and cluster correction) with peak coordinates and tables/figures illustrating whole-brain results (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core analyses and results are reported in the main paper (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion/exclusion assessment: Inclusion met: I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-related task—live eye contact/dyadic fMRI). Inclusion not met / not verifiable from provided text: I4 (no participant/sample details confirming healthy adults age 18–65 or separate healthy-group reporting), I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map, coordinates, or clear whole-brain results are reported), I6 (no evidence that whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplement). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E2–E6 clearly applicable from the truncated text). Because essential inclusion criteria (I4 and I5) cannot be confirmed from the available content, the study is excluded pending access to the complete full text.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Exclusion reason: the abstract describes an ROI-targeted rt-fMRI/EEG correlation analysis centered on right pSTS, with no indication of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for a healthy adult group. Exclusion IDs met: E2 (appears to report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: neurofeedback/training of social communication/facial expression processing). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (no participant/sample details or confirmation of a healthy adult group reported separately), I5 (no report of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps), I6 (no evidence that whole-brain results are reported in any acceptable format). Because the provided full text is incomplete, this assessment is provisional; full-text access could change the decision if whole-brain healthy-group results are present.

This is an empirical fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (a social cognitive task) in healthy adults (n=22, 21 included; mean age 23.7), reporting group-level whole-brain task contrasts. The manuscript contains full methods, results, figures and tables describing whole-brain analyses (e.g., 3rdppA>1stppV, EFE>no EFE) and reports coordinates and cluster-level results (Tables/Figures), satisfying the requirement that healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps be reported. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment investigating processing of empathic vs. unempathic social responses (social cognition / social communication) in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 26). The methods include task-evoked, group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported clusters (FWE-corrected p<0.05) and tables/figures of activations. The sample is within the 18–65 range and results for healthy participants are reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task fMRI of perception of others' facial expressions in a healthy adult sample (meets I3 and I4). However, the reported analyses are primarily ROI-based MVPA (OFA, FFA, STS and anatomical ROIs) and summary univariate ROI results; the paper does not present a clear group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy participant group in the main text, nor tables of whole-brain coordinates or figures described as whole-brain contrasts from the main healthy sample. The independent group localiser (faces>scrambled) that produced group maps used a different participant set (n=83), so it does not count as a healthy-group whole-brain task map from the main sample. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting / no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly reported whole-brain group-level voxelwise task map).

The study reports an fMRI experiment using naturalistic social-evaluative videos (E.Vids), directly addressing social-related processing. Participants: a healthy adult sample (N=37; mean age 24.8, range within 18–65). The paper provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction analyses) thresholded and FWE-corrected, with tables and figures of coordinates/clusters. ROI analyses are present but whole-brain voxelwise results for the healthy group are clearly reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=30, ages 18–29) that used a social perception task (age judgments of Black and White faces) and later assessed social-evaluative outcomes (trustworthiness ratings and differentiation). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., Black>White contrasts) with coordinates and tables, and psychophysiological interaction (PPI) connectivity analyses. Whole-brain results are clearly reported and attributed to the healthy/control group. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This fMRI study investigates social processing (linking person perception and person knowledge), fitting the review’s social-related constructs. Sample: healthy adults only (n=21 analyzed; mean age 24.6 years), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (main effects and interaction; voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, and tables of results are provided), clearly from the healthy/control group. Whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and tables (satisfying acceptability of coordinate/figure reporting). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=24, mean age 25.7) using social (agent-behavior, agent-mental) and non-social story tasks designed to probe theory-of-mind and processing of unexpected events. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (voxel-wise P<0.001; cluster-wise FWE-corrected) with peak coordinates and tables described in the text (Background and Outcome segment contrasts). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task activation maps), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported with coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social judgment task (social dominance and trustworthiness), using healthy adult participants (N=23, ages 21–43). It presents group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) with FWE-corrected cluster results and a table of coordinates, clearly reported for the healthy sample. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s fMRI social-processing focus and all inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=25 analyzed, mean age 24) who performed tasks that explicitly probe social-related processing (a meaning-related rating task engaging social cognition and mentalizing versus a physical property task). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (meaning > physical; own > other; interaction effects) with tables of peak coordinates, thresholding and correction methods described, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social task (Cyberball ball-toss) examining social interaction and reward, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=31 analyzed; ages ~21), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps/contrasts with coordinates and cluster-level FWE-corrected statistics (e.g., ventral striatum and precuneus clusters), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (tables/figures). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical, age outside range) apply. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This task-state fMRI study investigates self-referential (social-cognitive) processing during an episodic memory retrieval task and includes a healthy control group, but it does not report a group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked activation map for the healthy/control group. The reported results are ROI-based correlation networks and seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps (connectivity analyses), not univariate whole-brain task activation contrasts. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (seed-based/ connectivity-only without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study involves self-referential/social-cognitive processing during fMRI). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map reported). Additionally, I4 (healthy adult age 18–65) cannot be confirmed from the full text provided (ages not reported explicitly), so I4 is not satisfied based on available information. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation (Social-Reg) using a psychotherapist to regulate participants' emotions—clearly a social-related task. Sample comprises healthy adult females (ages 22–32) with group-level analyses reported. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, outside age range, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes retaliation/provocation, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 22.3), satisfying the age and healthy-group criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results (random-effects group analyses) with statistical maps, Talairach coordinates, cluster statistics, and figures—fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range ages, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text as provided appears to be limited to highlights, abstract, keywords, and references; core article sections (full methods, full results, figures/tables) are not present. While the study reports fMRI during an interactive mentalizing (prisoner’s dilemma) task in healthy adult participants (n=195, fMRI subgroup n=163), and thus likely meets I3 (fMRI social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample), I cannot verify I5: that at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group is reported. The available text lists activated regions but does not include methods/results details confirming whole-brain voxelwise group maps (versus ROI analyses or subgroup-only contrasts). Therefore, because the full text is incomplete and I5 cannot be confirmed, I must exclude. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met based on available content.

This is an fMRI study of social processes (charitable giving; empathy and perspective-taking tasks) in healthy adults (N=33, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (searchlight MVPA and GLM contrasts) with tables/figures and corrected statistical thresholds, clearly identified as healthy-group effects. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-cognition task (EmpaToM) that manipulates empathy and Theory of Mind and reports group-level task contrasts. Sample: n=178 healthy adult participants (mean age 40.9, within 18–65) with no clinical subgroup reported. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (emotional vs neutral videos; ToM vs non-ToM questions/videos) using SPM8, with activation peaks/tables and PCA/DCM results. Thus the paper meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task contrasts reported), and I6 (results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

Full text provided appears incomplete (only highlights, abstract, abbreviations, and references). While the study uses fMRI in a social cognition task (meets I3), the manuscript as provided does not report participant characteristics or clearly state that the sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–65 (I4 not confirmed). Critically, the supplied content does not include methods or results showing a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinates (I5 not confirmed). No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available text, but because core article content (methods, participants, whole-brain results) is missing, I cannot verify all inclusion criteria. Therefore I exclude this record from the review at this stage due to incomplete full text. To include, provide the full article PDF or sections with participant details and whole-brain group results (figures/tables/coordinate lists).

Only abstract and metadata are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). The abstract indicates fMRI during a social learning task (I3 satisfied). However, essential criteria cannot be verified from the abstract: participant ages/healthy adult sample not explicitly reported (I4 not verifiable), and the paper’s report of group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps cannot be confirmed from the abstract (I5 and I6 not verifiable). No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract.
