Because the full text (methods, participant details, and whole-brain results) is not available, I cannot confirm that all inclusion criteria are met, so the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression updating (social cognition: perception and understanding of others), using BOLD fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=21; ages 18–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts (e.g., L2>F3, 2×4 ANOVA, targeted whole-brain contrasts), with corrected cluster thresholds and tables/figures of coordinates and statistical maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study of Theory of Mind/social cognition (REMICS task) in healthy adults (n=19, ages 20–53). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., SocAdj > PhyConf; Soc > Phy; Adj > Conf) with statistical thresholds, cluster correction, and tables of peak coordinates and t-values. Results are clearly attributed to the healthy/control group and presented in tables and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets all required inclusion criteria: it reports an fMRI task manipulation of social exclusion/performance evaluation (social-related task; Cyberball modification), includes a healthy adult sample (20 men, 20 women; mean age 27.8 within 18–65), and presents group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with voxelwise FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures (multiple contrasts, conjunctions, and tables of MNI coordinates). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and the study is empirical).

This article is a non-empirical review (labelled 'REVISIÓN') and does not present original fMRI data from healthy adults or report any group-level whole-brain task activation maps. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data) is met. No inclusion criteria are satisfied: it does not use fMRI during a social-related task (I3), does not report a healthy adult sample with separable results (I4), does not provide whole-brain group-level task maps (I5), and does not provide qualifying whole-brain results in tables/figures (I6). Full text appears incomplete (only metadata/label provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults: participants (N=34, mean age 22.2) watched a movie and analyses focused on neural responses to social interactions. The task is social-related (naturalistic movie viewing emphasizing social interactions), satisfying I3. Sample is healthy adults within 18–65, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise reverse correlation analyses and displays whole-brain maps/clusters (e.g., Fig. 3) with statistical tests, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This fMRI study investigates social perception of others (angry vs. joyful contexts) using a task where participants watched actors grasping objects with emotional context — meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of 20 healthy adults (ages 23–33), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (GLM, whole-brain FWE-corrected results, tables of coordinates and contrasts) clearly from the healthy group. Whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures (coordinates), meeting the reporting criterion. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-reference vs other-reference) in healthy adults, using a task that probes self/other understanding. The sample includes 110 healthy adults aged 19–31, meeting the age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (second-level random-effects ANOVA; results reported with whole-brain FWE correction and figures/tables), clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. Whole-brain results are reported in figures and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (college-aged/community adults, N=10 pilot, N=15 main) using social manipulations (acquaintance vs. random/computer) while participants perform social economic games (Prisoner’s Dilemma, Ultimatum/Welfare Game). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (first-/second-/third-level GLM in FSL/FLAME and SPM12) with thresholded statistical maps and coordinate tables (P<0.05 FWE, Z/T maps) and presents whole-brain contrasts for healthy participants. Reporting includes coordinates/tables and figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This report is an empirical fMRI study that probes attachment-related social processing (mentalizing/social cognition) using the Adult Attachment Projective Picture System, satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample is N=25 healthy adults (ages 19–26), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (attachment vs. neutral) with MNI coordinates and cluster-level correction, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are presented in text, figures, and coordinates. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=24, ages 19–31) using a social task manipulating cooperation and competition and ratings of self and others, directly addressing social cognition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (family-wise error cluster-corrected maps and peak coordinates in Table 1) and describes these as coming from the healthy sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (coordinates and figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma cooperation) in healthy adult participants (mean age ~21), reporting whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates/tables provided). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mental state attribution) using the Social Detection Task (naturalistic social scenes). The sample consists of healthy adults (n=38, ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects analyses (two-level GLM, full-factorial ANOVA) with family-wise-error correction and provides whole-brain results in Table 1 and figures (e.g., Social > Non-social contrast). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This empirical fMRI study examines emotion regulation (reappraisal) of angry faces — a social-related task — in healthy adult participants (N=60, age range 18–57). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry; Increase + Decrease vs Observe-angry) with tables/figures and cluster-corrected statistical thresholds. Results for the healthy group are reported explicitly. Resting-state analyses are supplementary but do not replace the task whole-brain results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment of prosocial learning (a social-related task), using a healthy adult sample (N=31, males aged 19–32). Group-level task-evoked fMRI results are reported, including parametric prediction-error contrasts and coordinates, with main effects reported at voxel-wise FWE whole-brain correction or small-volume corrections and supplementary tables/figures showing activation maps and coordinates. Thus the paper provides whole-brain group-level task activation results for healthy adults (with results reported in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical study).

The study reports task-based fMRI during social cognition paradigms (mentalizing, empathy, prosocial decision-making) in healthy adult participants (32 right-handed females, mean age 22.7), satisfying the sample criterion. It presents group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (e.g., Mentalizing > baseline, Dissimilar > Similar contrasts) with cluster-level correction and voxelwise thresholds, and reports coordinates and tables, fulfilling whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (mentalizing about friends vs kin) conducted in healthy adult participants (n=25 females, mean age 23.2). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (friend > kin contrast, kin > friend, and parametric linear analyses across network layers) with cluster-thresholding and tables/figures of activation coordinates. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results presented as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI task study using a Face Matching Task (fear and neutral faces) that probes social/emotional perception of others (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adults (n=10, mean age 25) reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests) and associated maps/tables (Supplementary Table S2 and Figures), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results from the healthy group (meets I5 and I6). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social processing (competition vs. noncompetition), using a social-comparison/mentalizing paradigm relevant to perception/understanding of others. The sample is healthy adults (n=20 females, age 18–35). The authors report group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., competition > no competition) with corrected cluster thresholds and peak coordinates, and describe results in text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication processes: participants viewed product descriptions varying in social-language content and underwent task-evoked fMRI while making recommendation judgments. Sample: healthy adult undergraduates (n=19, mean age 20.55) meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports both ROI and whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric modulators of LIWC Social Processes; whole-brain maps, cluster thresholds, Tables/Figures), with group-level random-effects results clearly described for the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, figures/tables, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an original fMRI study that tests social-cognitive processing (emotion recognition and gaze integration) using a task in the scanner. It reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (PLS results with tables/coordinates and figures) for healthy participant groups. The study includes a healthy younger adult group (range 17–27, mean 20.65) with participants predominantly within the 18–65 range, satisfying the requirement that at least one healthy adult group in the target age range is reported; whole-brain results are clearly presented. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study assesses social processing (empathy for pain) using a task in healthy adult participants (male, 18–40). It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical results (second-level random-effects analyses with whole-brain FWE-corrected maps reported for condition contrasts and group comparisons) and provides coordinates/tables/figures. Sample meets the age and health criteria. Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures (acceptable reporting per I6). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study investigates attribution of emotions to humans and non-human animals—clearly a social-cognitive task (Perception/Understanding of Others). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=18; age range 21–46), meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation analyses (e.g., Emotion>Expression conjunctions, Face>Scramble contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and whole-brain maps/tables described in text and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly reported for the healthy/control group. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and acceptable reporting per I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports fMRI during perception of emotional faces (a social-related task: perception and understanding of others), includes 40 healthy volunteers, and reports group-level neural responses (thalamus, temporo-parietal regions, amygdala, cerebellum) associated with task conditions, indicating whole-brain task-evoked results. However, the provided full text appears truncated (methods/participant ages and exact analysis details not shown), so I could not fully verify participant age range (18–65) or explicit statement that whole-brain voxelwise maps for the healthy group are reported. Therefore I include the study but flag the full text as incomplete and assign moderate confidence pending full-text verification of ages and whole-brain analysis reporting.

This is an fMRI study addressing social perception (decoding emotion and attention to faces), using dynamic face stimuli and tasks (emotion vs age), satisfying social-related task requirement. Sample: healthy adult participants (final n=25, ages 21–33) meeting the 18–65 criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (univariate random-effects faces>objects contrast and whole-brain searchlight analyses submitted to second-level one-sample t-tests with SnPM correction) and reports results in figures/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (I5/I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that tested social interaction (SI) recognition using point-light displays (a social-related task). It includes a healthy adult group (ages 20–41) and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (SI > NM) for each age group, including adults, with cluster- and FWE-corrected results and figures/tables describing activations. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided and appears complete. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for fMRI social processing in healthy adults, provides whole-brain activation maps/contrasts for the adult group, and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This PNAS study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 18–24) using an article-reading/sharing paradigm that probes self-related and social (mentalizing) processes—constructs within the review’s social-related processing domain. The paper includes group-level whole-brain analyses (SI: whole-brain searches, Fig. S3 and Table S5) clearly derived from the healthy participant samples and describes methods, results, and discussion in full. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/SI). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (retrieval of person/biographical knowledge; perception/understanding of others), using task-based fMRI and multivariate and univariate analyses. The samples are healthy adult participants (study 1: n=24, Mage=23.2; study 2: n=26, Mage=20.4), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (e.g., univariate GLM contrasts such as “all memory > baseline,” thresholded at voxel-level FWE P < 0.05) and presents coordinates/tables and figures of these effects. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social-cognition (mentalising/theory-of-mind) task comparing intentionality (mentalising) versus factual memory, directly addressing social-related processing. Sample: healthy adult participants are reported (Experiment 2: N=17, mean age 22 ±2.9 yrs), within 18–65. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., mentalising > factual; parametric modulation contrasts) with statistical thresholding and reports results in figures and a Table 1 of significant whole-brain responses. Whole-brain maps/coordinates and thresholding procedures are described. Full text includes methods, results and discussion. Therefore I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original fMRI study of social processing (pseudo-interactive joke task) in healthy adults (N=38, ages 19–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., SELF vs OTHER, Group vs No laughter, interaction/action-outcome contingency) with appropriate statistical thresholds and FWE cluster correction; results are presented in figures and tables. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task maps, out-of-range age groups, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This empirical paper reports task-based BOLD fMRI during decisions to select and to share news articles, which directly targets social-related processing (sharing, social cognition) and satisfies I3. The sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–24 (N=41 analyzed), meeting I4. The manuscript reports group-level whole-brain task-activation analyses (select>content, share>content, share>select) with FWE correction and cluster thresholds, and presents results in tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making in healthy adult participants. Neuroimaging methods and group-level GLM analyses are described; whole-brain, voxelwise results (random-effects group maps) are reported (thresholded maps and coordinate results; NeuroVault link provided). Participant ages (neuroimaging cohort 18–57; final N=62) fall within the 18–65 range and are healthy adults. The task involves social information and social influence, satisfying the social-related processing domain. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, neuroimaging analyses).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social behavior (Trust Game) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–30) that reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts and tables/figures of activation (e.g., Gave $1.5X vs Gave $0; Test condition contrasts) and ICA results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and figures/tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during a social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps/contrasts reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not limited to connectivity/resting-state only (E3) since univariate whole-brain activations are reported, not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within age range (E5), and this is original empirical work (E6).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of social cognition: participants imagined 20 personally familiar people in social situations (social simulation), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=23 analyzed, ages 18–27), meeting the age and healthy-sample inclusion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain searchlight and feature-selected analyses with random-effects t-tests and permutation-based multiple-comparison correction; results are presented as whole-brain maps/tables (voxelwise), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Hence the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=34 males, ages 19–31) that used a social-related task (observing others' social integrity threats to elicit fremdscham or schadenfreude), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts (SIT > NEUT) and explicitly states results thresholded at p<.05 FWE-corrected for whole-brain analyses within each group, with tables/figures of activation (meeting I5 and acceptable reporting per I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activations; healthy adult group reported separately). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind) in healthy adult participants (N=22 analyzed; mean age 24.4). The task is social-related (implicit/explicit belief processing). The paper reports a group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM for the explicit general-belief localizer (false-belief vs false-photograph) with results thresholded and reported (q(FDR)<0.05; peak Talairach coordinates provided), satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. Although the implicit ToM task analyses used an ROI approach, the explicit localizer provides the necessary whole-brain evidence. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the analyses and results are reported primarily as ROI-based MVPA and individually-defined localizer ROIs; the paper does not present a clear group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group in the main text (the localizer is used at the individual subject level and results are reported as ROI-based statistics). Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 and corresponds to exclusion criterion E2 (reports only ROI-based analyses with no whole-brain healthy-group task map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (heterosexual men, ages 22–50) that examines neural responses to romantic (affiliation/attachment-related) and sexual stimuli. The task involves social-related stimuli (romantic images), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults within the 18–65 range, satisfying I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group-level contrasts (e.g., sexual>neutral combined activation, romantic>neutral between-group and within-group contrasts), with whole-head analyses described in Methods and results presented in figures and tables, satisfying I5 and I6. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain task effects, and is empirical, so no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating affiliation/attachment-related processing (implicit attitudes toward adultery/monogamy and regulation of interest in extra-pair relationships) using task-based fMRI. Participants: healthy adult males (ages 20–32) meeting the healthy adult inclusion criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses for the IAT (incongruent vs. congruent; cluster-level FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates are reported) and provides coordinates/tables and discussion of whole-brain findings. Although the go/no-go analysis included an ROI constraint for right VLPFC, the presence of whole-brain IAT results satisfies the whole-brain evidence requirement. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social perception (perception of third-party social interactions) in healthy adult participants (N=14, ages 20–32). It includes whole-brain, random-effects group analyses (interaction > independent; animate > physical) with reported peak MNI coordinates and group maps, satisfying the requirement for a group-level, voxelwise healthy-group task activation map. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. The sample is within the 18–65 age range. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social person evaluation (impression-formation) in healthy adult participants (N=60 males, Mage 23.8), satisfying the sample criterion. The methods report task-evoked fMRI during a social task and include whole-brain analyses (exploratory whole-brain regressions with voxelwise thresholds and reported clusters, Figure 4 and Supplementary Material S4), meeting the whole-brain result requirement. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (point-light vs human-like walkers; judgments of facing toward/away), conducted in healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22.75). The paper reports group-level task-evoked voxelwise analyses (second-level contrasts) and provides stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding details (Table 1), meeting the requirement for whole-brain evidence; relevant results are described in the text and tables. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study used fMRI to investigate responses to attachment (social) narratives in healthy adults (n=23 males) but reports only resting-state/seed-based functional connectivity (CN seed) analyses of post-narrative rest scans. It does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked (task activation) voxelwise maps from the healthy/control group (no unmasked whole-brain task activation contrasts reported). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI study of social/attachment processing), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I6 (results reported with coordinates/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social communication/collaborative learning in healthy adults. It meets inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI during a social/communicative referential task (collaborative vs. individual vs. arbitrary conditions); (I4) sample consists of healthy adult participants (ages 18–33; n=70 after exclusions); (I5) reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical results (whole-brain contrasts, cluster-corrected, reported in Table 1 and figures); (I6) whole-brain results are reported as coordinates and figures and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=36) while participants viewed social interactions (cooperative vs affective), satisfying the review objective. The sample is healthy adults in the 18–65 range. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (parametric and categorical contrasts), corrected for multiple comparisons, with reported activation maps/tables and coordinates (random-effects group analysis), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Although the paper also includes effective connectivity (DCM), it additionally provides unmasked, whole-brain task activation results for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of joint action with direct haptic social interaction (leading, following, mutual) — a clearly social-related task addressing perception/understanding of others and social reward (I3). Sample comprises healthy adult dancers (n=18 after exclusion), ages within 18–65 (mean 40.4) (I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts with tables of Talairach coordinates and thresholding details (e.g., partnered > non-partnered; improvisation contrasts) consistent with whole-brain evidence (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it used task-based fMRI during a social-related task (perception/discrimination of affective vocalisations—social communication), included a healthy adult sample (N=19, ages within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (species contrast human>chimpanzee>macaque) with coordinates and statistical maps/figures/tables. The full text contains Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and whole-brain GLM analyses), Results (whole-brain activations with coordinates), and Discussion, so the provided full text is complete. There are no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range-age issues. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (Theory-of-Mind [TOM] vs Random contrast) in a large sample of healthy adults (n=787; ages 22–>35 within 18–65 range). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain task activation maps (Cohen's d and z statistic maps), cluster tables and cerebellar/whole-brain visualizations corresponding to the healthy group. Reporting formats include thresholded maps and detailed cluster coordinates, satisfying acceptable whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Supplementary materials; full-text appears complete for screening. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (self, friend, celebrity role judgments) relevant to Perception and Understanding of Self and Others. The sample comprises 37 healthy adult males (mean age 22.9), meeting the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (self vs. celebrity, friend vs. celebrity) and whole-brain regression analyses with coordinates and thresholding (p<.05 FDR, voxelwise p<.001), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Results are presented as tables of coordinates and figures. Although the paper also reports seed-based connectivity (gPPI), this is supplementary to, not a substitute for, whole-brain task activations. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an fMRI investigation of social decision-making (modified iterated prisoner's dilemma) addressing perception/understanding of others (ToM), satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. Sample: 20 healthy adults aged 23–38, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., COMP>COOP, conjunction analyses) with cluster-level multiple-comparison correction and coordinate reporting (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly addresses social-related processing by comparing social vs. non-social image conditions using a valence appraisal task. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI with social-related manipulation), I4 (healthy adult sample, N=14 analyzed, ages 23–50), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise social>nonsocial contrast with thresholding and cluster tables/figures), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical design). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Given the clear reporting of whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from a healthy adult group and the explicit social manipulation, the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotion perception (facial/vocal/bimodal) — a social-cognitive task involving perception/understanding of others’ emotions (meets I3). Samples are healthy adult university students (ages 19–24; 19.67 mean in Study 2), satisfying the healthy adult requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GLM, SPM8), with whole-brain results and cluster tables/coordinates and PFWE-corrected maps described in the text and figures (meets I5 and I6). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore include.

Only the abstract and metadata are provided here; the full text (methods, results, figures/tables) is not available. The abstract indicates the study used fMRI during a social decision task (meets I3). However participant ages are not reported in the provided content so I cannot confirm the 18–65 adult sample requirement (I4 not confirmed). Crucially, the provided content does not allow verification that at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked map for the healthy group is reported (I5 not confirmed). Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete information until the full text is available for review.

Full text not available (only abstract provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI study of social-communicative prosody, so I3 (fMRI during a social-related task) appears satisfied. However, the abstract does not report participant characteristics or age range (cannot verify I4: healthy adults 18–65) and does not provide clear information that group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps for the healthy group are reported (I5/I6 unverifiable). Because core article content (methods, participant details, whole-brain results) is missing, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria. No specific exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Full text incomplete, so study cannot be included at this stage.

This fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation) using task-based fMRI (meets I3). Sample comprises healthy adults (final N=31, ages 19–24) (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with coordinates and tables (e.g., SC vs SA, OA vs OC, SA vs Fixation; statistical thresholds reported and coordinate tables provided), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical data present). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

The study is an fMRI investigation of social evaluations (intelligence and friendliness) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–28), so it meets I3 (social fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, the authors explicitly report conducting ROI-restricted analyses (“search regions were restricted to these ROIs”) and present results from these ROIs; no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map for the healthy group is reported. Therefore it fails I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses reported). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It includes a social cognition (theory-of-mind) task among seven fMRI tasks (I3). The samples are healthy adults drawn from HCP (ages 22–36+; N≈100) and the UCLA dataset (mean age 31, range 21–50; N=114), satisfying the healthy adult sample requirement (I4). The authors report voxel-wise, group-level task activation analyses (voxel-wise GLM, group one-sample t tests, and figures of task activations such as Figure 1), providing whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group (I5). Reporting in figures and text is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain maps, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (I3): participants viewed attachment-related erotic scenes and fearful social scenes during task-based fMRI. Sample meets the healthy adult criterion (I4): 55 healthy young men (mean age ~24.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (I5/I6): whole-brain analyses with p<0.05 FWE-corrected results and ROI analyses are described for contrasts (erotic>neutral, fearful>neutral, erotic>fearful), with results presented in the main text and supplementary material. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion so is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=22, mean age 24.36) that used task-based functional MRI during a social-cognitive mind-perception task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise parametric analyses with cluster-based whole-brain correction and provides peak coordinates and cluster information (e.g., vmPFC, TPJ, fusiform), satisfying requirements for whole-brain reporting. The tasks address social processing (mind perception and gaze-cueing). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3 - task-based fMRI was used in an emotional face recognition paradigm probing social processing (perception/understanding of others' facial emotions); I4 - includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without ELM) reported separately; I5 - reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and whole-brain analyses (FWE-corrected) across groups and for each group, with control-group within-group effects described (e.g., medial frontal gyrus); I6 - whole-brain results are described in the text/tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This full text reports an fMRI task probing social-related processes (recall of autobiographical relationship episodes; meets I3). The sample is a healthy adult group (final N=35) with diagnostic screening (mini-DIPS) and sociodemographic characteristics described in Table 1, indicating adult participants (meets I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (self-relevant>control, other>control) with cluster-level inference (FDR correction) and tables/figures of significant clusters (meets I5 and I6). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met: whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group are reported (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

Full text unavailable (404 error on journal site). Cannot verify that the study meets inclusion criteria: I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked map for healthy group), or I6 (reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures). No evidence in the provided content to confirm any inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E2–E5) can be assessed from the missing full text. Per instructions, fulltext_incomplete=true and study is excluded because core article content (methods, results) is not accessible for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study examining audiovisual integration of emotional expressions (faces and voices), clearly a social-related task (social communication/perception of others). Participants: 24 healthy adults (mean age 26), within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and analyses (whole-brain RFX analyses with P<0.05 FWE-corrected; figures/tables showing rpSTS and other regions). Reporting satisfies acceptable formats (figures/tables, text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition: participants made face-based trustworthiness judgments and received feedback while undergoing task fMRI. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task — trustworthiness/impression updating), I4 (contains a healthy younger adult group aged 20–33 reported separately), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results — ANOVA and whole-brain analyses with tables/figures), and I6 (whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures). No exclusion criteria were triggered: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include within-group task activations. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses fMRI during a social cognition task (mental-state judgment/mentalizing), (I4) healthy adult sample reported (N=28 after exclusion, ages 18–22), (I5) reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (searchlight and repetition-suppression maps with TFCE-corrected p<0.05), and (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults using an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social decision-making task). Sample: 20 healthy male adults (ages 21–37) with results reported for the healthy cohort. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses (flexible factorial, one-sample t tests, FWE cluster-corrected maps) and presents whole-brain activation tables and cluster-corrected results across task phases. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are clearly satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (aged 18–22) that used a social interaction task (iterated Prisoner's Dilemma) during BOLD fMRI (satisfies I3 and I4). The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (Z-thresholding and FWE cluster correction) and describes whole-brain results for the healthy sample (both sexes and genotype subgroup analyses), meeting the requirement for whole-brain, task-evoked statistical maps (I5, I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not patient-only, and not non-empirical).

This is an fMRI study using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) probing responses to an ostensible opponent (social interaction), conducted in healthy adult males (ages 18–35). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (high > low provocation) with cluster-level FWE correction and provides MNI coordinates and figures. Whole-brain results for the healthy sample are clearly described (feedback and decision phase contrasts). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is available. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical restrictions).

This empirical dual-fMRI hyperscanning study uses task-based functional MRI during a social interaction paradigm (pattern game) that manipulates cooperation/competition and turn-based vs concurrent interaction, addressing social processing and understanding of others. The sample consists of 44 healthy adult participants (mean age 22.4), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, group random-effects with non-parametric permutation correction), with cluster tables and figures describing whole-brain results for healthy participants. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is not provided (only abstract/metadata available), so I cannot verify whether whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported (I5). Based on the abstract the study meets I3 (fMRI during a social-related pleasant touch task) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group), but I cannot confirm I5 (whole-brain evidence) from the available content. Therefore the study is excluded pending full-text verification. Full text incomplete, preventing confirmation of whole-brain results.

Provided full text is incomplete (only metadata/title/authors). Cannot verify key inclusion criteria from available content: unclear whether the study used a social-related task fMRI (I3), whether a healthy adult control group aged 18–65 is reported separately (I4), or whether whole-brain group-level healthy-task maps or coordinates are reported (I5). Therefore I cannot confirm eligibility and must exclude pending access to the full article. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/ not verifiable: I3, I4, I5.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata/DOI provided). From the abstract: (1) I3 is met — the study used task-based fMRI of a social cognition (theory of mind) task. (2) I4 is met — sample includes healthy younger adults (adult group within 18–65). However I5 (reporting at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from the healthy/control group) cannot be verified from the provided content. I6 (acceptable reporting in tables/figures/supplement) likewise cannot be confirmed. Because the full text is not available, I cannot confirm that the paper reports the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation map (and therefore cannot rule out E2/E3/E4). Per screening rules, all inclusion criteria must be verifiable; thus I must exclude at this stage. Recommend re-screening once full text (methods/results/maps or coordinate tables) is available.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/highlights/metadata provided). The abstract shows fMRI of dynamic facial-expression processing (social perception), so inclusion I3 is satisfied. However the provided full text does not report participant details or ages, so I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) cannot be confirmed. It also does not present or describe any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy/control group, so I5 is not confirmed. I6 cannot be confirmed either. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending access to the full article. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are positively met based on available content.

This fMRI study investigates social perception (face identity/viewpoint) and tests healthy adult participants (Experiment 1 mean age 25.3), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the report focuses on ROI-based multivariate pattern analyses and regressions across predefined visual-field and face ROIs; the paper does not present or report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or coordinate tables for the healthy group. Because no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map is reported, it fails I5 and meets exclusion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social communication task (live bidirectional conversation) in healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 25.8). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (HHI vs HRI and main effects), thresholded at p<0.05 FDR cluster-level; group maps are available on NeuroVault and raw data on OpenNeuro. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample in 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and available). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating empathy/social processing (observation of human and robot pain/pleasure) using task-based fMRI (pre/post intervention). Sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–27 (n=26) meeting the age and health requirements. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected results) and provides whole-brain contrast maps (NeuroVault) and detailed whole-brain results in the text/tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=20, ages 22–35) that investigates neural processing of co-speech gestures during narrative comprehension—a social-communication task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., low_ID > high_ID, speech > gestures+speech, gestures+speech > speech) with cluster-corrected results, coordinate tables, and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: social-related task—social communication; I4: healthy adult sample within 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts (BPD>HC, NSSI>HC) and conjunction analyses but does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map or within-group (healthy/control) whole-brain statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used fMRI during an explicitly social task — the cyberball paradigm) and I4 (includes a healthy adult control group, age within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported whole-brain, group-level healthy/control task-evoked map), therefore the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study reports an fMRI experiment probing animacy perception (a form of ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’), satisfying I3. Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–36; overall N=111; fMRI groups N≈19), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects whole-brain contrasts, FWE-corrected results, figures and coordinate tables), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task maps).

Meets all inclusion criteria: uses task fMRI with multiple social-related tasks (false belief, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes intention, trustworthiness, vocalization/social face tasks) (I3); sample consists of 78 healthy adults aged 18–40 with results reported for this healthy cohort (I4); reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses and thresholded maps (p<0.05 FWE) with peak tables (I5); whole-brain results are presented in figures and supplementary tables (I6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplements) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. This study is therefore eligible for inclusion in the review focused on social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of dynamic facial-expression perception (a social-communication/perception task) in a healthy adult sample (n=51, mean age 22.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation analyses (random-effects one-sample t tests and ANOVAs) with FWE-corrected thresholds and provides activation coordinates, tables, and figures. It is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or resting-state, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

Exclusion IDs met: E3. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social-related vocal emotion/social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=36, ages 20–35). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 — the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate table of task activations; instead it reports ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical network metrics. The study therefore provides task-evoked connectivity/network results but no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation map, so it fails I5 and is excluded per E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=31, mean age 24.3) using social tasks (take-advice game and trust game) that probe perception/understanding of others and trust. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results (univariate GLM contrasts with voxel- and cluster-level FWE correction, whole-brain searchlight MVPA and LOSOCV classification/prediction analyses) that are clearly attributed to the healthy participant sample. Results are reported in the main text, figures, and supplementary tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical original data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of vocal vs. non-vocal sound processing framed as social/communicative (voice processing), using task fMRI in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=13, ages 21–41; Experiment 2: n=18, ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (vocal > non-vocal and related activation maps; thresholding and cluster criteria and MNI coordinates are provided and figures shown). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (observation of socio-affective touch) with an adult neurotypical control group reported separately. The methods include task fMRI (watching social and non-social touch videos) and MVPA/univariate analyses. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task activation results for the healthy/control group (including univariate contrasts and supplementary tables/figures with peak coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence; such results are available in main and supplementary materials. The healthy control group is adults and reported separately from the clinical ASD group. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating collective/social memory processing and the representation of collective schemas in medial prefrontal cortex. It uses a task involving recall of museum images to probe social/collective knowledge (social-related processing), includes a healthy adult sample (N=24; ages 22–39), and reports group-level whole-brain searchlight results (TFCE-corrected clusters) as well as ROI analyses. Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps and figures are clearly reported for the healthy/control participants. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.
